Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly and sing all day long. One day, Tweety saw a big, juicy berry on the ground. Tweety thought it would be yummy to eat, but didn't know if it was safe. 

Tweety asked a wise old owl if the berry was good to eat. The owl said, "No, that berry is poison. It could make you very sick." Tweety was sad because he was hungry, but he knew it was useful to listen to the owl and not eat the berry.

Later that day, Tweety saw a cat sneaking up on him. The cat wanted to eat Tweety for lunch! Tweety quickly flew up into a tree and the cat couldn't reach him. Tweety was happy he listened to the owl and didn't eat the poison berry. Being smart and careful helped Tweety avoid a dangerous situation.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Binky. Binky loved to wander around the garden, looking for yummy carrots to eat. One day, Binky found a very tight spot between two big rocks. He tried to squeeze through, but he couldn't. "Oh no!" cried Binky. "I'm stuck!"

Just then, Binky's friend, a little bird named Tweetie, flew by. "What's wrong, Binky?" asked Tweetie. "I'm stuck!" said Binky. "I can't get through this tight spot!" "Don't worry," said Tweetie. "I'll go get help!"

Tweetie flew off to find some friends to help Binky. Soon, a group of animals came to Binky's rescue. They pushed and pulled, and finally, Binky was free! "Thank you so much!" said Binky. "I'm so glad to be out of there!"

From that day on, Binky was more careful when he wandered around the garden. He didn't want to get stuck again! And whenever he saw his friends, he thanked them again for helping him.

"It means that if you touch it too hard or drop it, it will break into many little pieces," her mom replied. 

Lily understood and promised to be careful. She took the vase to her room and put it on her shelf. 

Later that day, Lily's grandma came to visit. She saw the vase on the shelf and said, "Lily, I will teach you how to take care of fragile things." 

Lily was excited to learn. Her grandma showed her how to hold the vase gently and put it back on the shelf without touching anything else. 

Lily was happy to have learned something new and thanked her grandma. As they sat down to have some cookies, Lily noticed that her grandma had a cigarette in her hand.

Lily listened carefully and promised herself that she would never smoke. She was happy to have learned two new things that day.

But Timmy was persistent and kept asking Miss Lisa questions about why shooting is bad. Miss Lisa explained that it can hurt people and make them feel scared. Timmy understood and promised to never shoot his toy gun again.

From that day on, Timmy learned to be kind to others and to never use his toy gun to shoot at anything. Miss Lisa was proud of Timmy for being a good listener and a kind boy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small village near a big mill. Every day, she would hear the loud noise of the mill as it turned and turned.

One day, Lily was playing with her toys when her mom came in and said, "Lily, I have something serious to tell you. We need to listen carefully." Lily stopped playing and looked up at her mom.

Her mom continued, "The mill is going to stop working for a while. That means we won't have any flour to make bread." Lily's eyes widened as she realized how important the mill was to their village.

The next day, Lily and her mom went to the mill to see if they could help. They worked hard and soon the mill was fixed. Everyone in the village was happy and thankful for Lily and her mom's hard work. From that day on, Lily knew how important it was to listen and take things seriously.

One day, the mouse found a big cake. The cake was in the kitchen. The mouse wanted to eat the cake. But the cake was too big. So, the mouse decided to separate the cake into smaller pieces.

The mouse said, "I will cut the cake into small parts. Then, I can eat it easily." The mouse cut the cake and ate a small piece. It was very delicious. The mouse was very happy.

Later, a cat came into the kitchen. The cat saw the mouse and the cake. The cat said, "I want some cake too. Can you share it with me?" The mouse agreed and separated another piece for the cat.

The mouse and the cat ate the delicious cake together. They became good friends. From that day on, they shared everything in the big house.

Max and Luna played a slow game in the yard. They were having fun, but then Max stepped on a sharp thing. "Ouch!" Max cried. His heel was hurt even more now. Luna felt sad and said, "I am sorry, Max. I didn't see the sharp thing."

The barrel spoke loudly and said, "No, I will not go with you! I want to stay here and speak to everyone in the town." The people were happy, and the selfish man went away. The barrel stayed in the town and spoke to everyone, making them all very happy.

Anna nodded and ran to her room. She came back with the book and showed it to Lisa. She said, "I remember! This is your book. You gave it to me when you went to university. I love this book. It has so many animals. Look, this is a lion, and this is a monkey, and this is a penguin."

Lisa looked at the book and smiled. She said, "Yes, I remember. I loved this book, too. It was a gift from our grandma. She was very humble and wise, and she taught me a lot of things. She always said, 'Be curious, be kind, and be grateful.' I think that's a good way to live, don't you?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I want to be like you and grandma. I want to learn a lot of things and be humble and kind and grateful. And I want to go to university, too."

Lisa hugged Anna and said, "You will, Anna. You are a wonderful girl, and you can do anything you want. I believe in you, and I love you."

Anna hugged Lisa and said, "I love you, too, Lisa. You are the best sister ever."

"Hello, I am Princess Lila," Anna said, making her doll wave. "I live in a castle and I have a lot of jewels and dresses."

"Hello, I am Tom," Ben said, making his doll nod. "I live in a farm and I have a lot of animals and toys."

"Would you like to come to my castle and see my jewels and dresses?" Anna asked.

"Wow, you have so many jewels and dresses," Ben said, looking around.

"Yes, I do. They are all mine and they are all real," Anna said, proudly.

Ben picked up one of the stones and looked at it closely. He saw that it was not a real jewel, but a fake one. It was made of plastic and it had a crack on it.

"Hey, this is not a real jewel. This is a fake one," Ben said, showing it to Anna.

Anna snatched the stone from Ben and put it back in the box. She was angry and embarrassed.

"No, it is not. It is a real jewel. You are lying," Anna said, shouting.

"I am not lying. Look, it has a crack on it. And it feels like plastic. You have fake jewels and fake dresses," Ben said, pointing.

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She did not like Ben saying that. She wanted to have real jewels and real dresses. She wanted to be a real princess.

She pushed Ben and his doll away from the box. Ben fell on the floor and his doll landed on his shoulder. He felt a sharp pain.

Anna did not care. She hugged her doll and the box. She did not want to play with Ben anymore.

"Go away. You are not my friend. You are a liar and a bully," Anna said, crying.

Ben got up and took his doll. He was sad and angry. He did not want to play with Anna anymore.

"Fine. I will go away. You are not my friend. You are a fake princess and a brat," Ben said, leaving.

There was a boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many toys, but he did not like to share them with others. He always said, "Mine, mine, mine!" and he hid his toys under his bed.

One day, a new boy came to his school. He had no toys, because he came from a far place where there was war and sadness. He was unknown to the other children, and he felt lonely and scared.

The boy with many toys saw the new boy sitting by himself at recess. He felt curious and went to talk to him. He asked him his name and where he came from. The new boy told him his story, and the boy with many toys felt sorry for him.

He said, "Do you want to play with me? I have many toys, and I can share them with you." The new boy smiled and said, "Yes, thank you. You are very kind."

They went to the boy's house after school, and the boy with many toys showed him his toys. He said, "You can choose any toy you like, and we can play together." The new boy was happy and picked a toy car. He said, "This is my favorite toy. Can I have it?" The boy with many toys felt a sting in his heart. He loved his toy car, and he did not want to give it away.

He thought for a moment, and then he remembered how the new boy had nothing, and how he had suffered. He said, "Yes, you can have it. It is yours now." He gave him the toy car, and he felt a warm feeling in his chest. He said, "I surrender my toy car to you, because you are my friend, and I want you to be happy."

The new boy hugged him and said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You are the best friend I ever had. I will never forget your kindness." They played with the other toys, and they had a lot of fun. They became best friends, and they learned to share and care for each other.

The moral of the story is: It is better to share than to be selfish, and it is better to surrender than to fight. Sharing and surrendering can make you and others happy, and can help you make new friends.

Lily was a little flower who lived in a big garden. She had many friends, like Rose, Daisy and Sunflower. They all liked to play and talk under the sun. But Lily was not happy. She wanted to bloom and show her pretty petals to everyone.

"Look at me, Lily!" Rose said one day. "I have so many red petals and a sweet smell. Everyone loves me!"

"I wish I could bloom like you, Rose," Lily said. "But I am still a bud. When will I bloom?"

"You have to wait, Lily," Daisy said. "Bloom takes time. You have to grow and drink water and get sun. Then you will bloom when you are ready."

"But I don't want to wait!" Lily said. "I want to bloom now! I am impatient!"

Lily looked around the garden and saw a patch of green herbs. They smelled good and looked fresh. Lily thought they might help her bloom faster.

"Maybe if I eat some of these herbs, I will bloom sooner," Lily said. She left her friends and went to the herbs. She nibbled on a leaf and felt a tingling in her mouth.

"Ow! This herb is spicy!" Lily said. She spat out the leaf and looked for another one. She tried a different herb and felt a sour taste.

"Yuck! This herb is sour!" Lily said. She spat out the leaf and looked for another one. She tried a third herb and felt a bitter taste.

"Blech! This herb is bitter!" Lily said. She spat out the leaf and felt sick. She had a stomach ache and a headache. She wished she had not eaten the herbs.

She crawled back to her friends and saw them smiling and blooming. They had beautiful petals of different colors and shapes. They looked happy and healthy.

"Lily, are you okay?" Sunflower asked. "You look pale and sad."

"I am sorry, Sunflower," Lily said. "I was impatient and I ate some herbs. I thought they would make me bloom faster, but they only made me sick. I was foolish and greedy."

"That's okay, Lily," Sunflower said. "We all make mistakes. But you have to learn from them. Herbs are not for flowers. They are for animals and people. Flowers have to bloom in their own way and time. You have to be patient and trust nature."

Lily nodded and thanked Sunflower. She felt sorry for what she had done and hoped she would get better soon. She realized that being impatient was not good and that being happy with what she had was better. She decided to wait for her bloom and enjoy her friends. She learned a valuable lesson that day.

Ben and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. Ben found a big jar of honey in the cabinet. He wanted to taste it.

"Look, Lily, honey!" he said, holding the jar. "It is sweet and sticky. Let's have some."

Lily shook her head. "No, Ben, we can't. Mommy said honey is for grown-ups. It can make us sick."

Ben frowned. "Why? It looks yummy."

Lily tried to explain. "Mommy said honey has tiny bugs in it. They are too small to see, but they can hurt our tummies. We need to wait until we are older and our tummies are stronger."

Ben looked at the jar. He saw the honey was thick and golden. He did not see any bugs. He did not believe Lily.

"That's silly," he said. "There are no bugs in honey. You are just scared. I'm not scared. I'm going to try it."

He opened the jar and dipped his finger in the honey. He licked his finger. It was sweet and sticky. He smiled.

"See, Lily, it's good. You are missing out."

He dipped his finger again and licked it. He did not notice the red spots on his tongue. He did not notice the itch in his throat. He did not notice the rash on his skin.

He only noticed when he started to cough. He dropped the jar and clutched his chest. He felt hot and dizzy. He could not breathe.

He looked at Lily. She was scared. She ran to get Mommy.

Mommy came and saw Ben. She saw the jar and the honey. She knew what happened. She grabbed Ben and ran to the car. She drove to the hospital.

She hoped it was not too late. She hoped Ben would be okay. She hoped he learned his lesson.

Lily and Sam liked to watch cartoons on TV. They saw funny animals and people who did silly things. Sometimes they laughed so hard that their bellies hurt. They had a favorite cartoon about a cat and a mouse who chased each other.

One day, they decided to pretend that they were the cat and the mouse. Lily put on a pair of ears and a tail and said, "I am the cat. I will catch you, mouse!" Sam put on a pair of whiskers and a nose and said, "I am the mouse. You can't catch me, cat!" They ran around the house, making noises and hiding behind things.

Mom was in the kitchen, making lunch. She heard the noise and came to see what was going on. She saw Lily and Sam playing and smiled. She said, "What are you doing, my little cat and mouse?" Lily and Sam stopped and looked at her. They said, "We are pretending to be the cartoon, Mom. It is fun!" Mom said, "I see. Well, you are very good at pretending. But don't forget to be careful. Don't break anything or hurt yourselves."

Lily and Sam nodded. They said, "OK, Mom. We will be careful." Then they continued to play. They tried to be serious, like the cartoon, but they couldn't help giggling. They had a lot of fun pretending to be the cat and the mouse.

Lily was a fat cat who liked to sleep on the sofa. She did not like to play or run or jump. She only wanted to eat and nap. One day, she saw a glass on the table. It was full of water and had ice cubes inside. Lily thought the water looked cool and tasty. She wanted to drink it.

She jumped on the table and walked to the glass. She put her paw on the glass and tried to tip it over. But the glass was too heavy and did not move. Lily pushed harder and harder, but the glass still did not move. She was angry and frustrated. She meowed loudly.

Tom was a boy who lived in the house with Lily. He heard Lily's meow and came to the table. He saw Lily trying to knock over the glass. He said, "Lily, what are you doing? That is my water. You have your own bowl of water. You cannot drink from the glass. You will spill it and make a mess."

Lily looked at Tom and did not care. She still wanted the water from the glass. She meowed louder and louder. She scratched the glass with her claws. She hoped the glass would break and the water would spill.

Tom was scared and angry. He said, "Lily, stop it! You are a bad cat. You are not listening to me. You are hurting the glass. You will hurt yourself too. You have to get off the table. Now!"

He grabbed Lily by the scruff of her neck and lifted her off the table. He put her on the floor and said, "Go to your bed. You are in trouble. You cannot have the water from the glass. You have to drink from your bowl. And you have to lose some weight. You are too fat."

Lily was sad and ashamed. She did not like to be yelled at. She did not like to be in trouble. She did not like to be fat. She walked to her bed and lay down. She did not want to drink or eat or nap. She only wanted to be loved.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to help Mom in the kitchen. Today, Mom is going to bake a cake for Dad's birthday. Sara and Ben want to help too.

"Can we help you, Mom?" Sara asks.

"Of course, you can. You can help me mix the batter and put it in the pan," Mom says.

Sara and Ben put on their aprons and wash their hands. They take turns to pour the flour, the sugar, the eggs and the milk into a big bowl. Mom helps them stir the batter with a wooden spoon. It looks yummy and smells good.

"Can we lick the spoon, Mom?" Ben asks.

"Only a little bit. We need to save some batter for the cake," Mom says.

Mom pours the batter into a round pan and puts it in the oven. She sets the timer and tells Sara and Ben to watch it.

"While the cake is baking, we can make a salad for lunch," Mom says.

Sara and Ben nod. They like salad. They follow Mom to the fridge and take out some lettuce, tomatoes, carrots and cheese. Mom washes the lettuce and tears it into pieces. Sara and Ben help her chop the tomatoes and the carrots. Mom grates the cheese and puts it in a bowl.

"Can we toss the salad, Mom?" Sara asks.

"Sure, you can. But be careful not to spill it," Mom says.

Mom gives Sara and Ben a big spoon each. They take some lettuce, some tomatoes, some carrots and some cheese and toss them in a big bowl. They add some dressing and toss some more. The salad looks colorful and tasty.

"Good job, Sara and Ben. You are very good helpers," Mom says.

"Thank you, Mom. We like to help you," Sara and Ben say.

The timer beeps. The cake is ready. Mom takes it out of the oven and lets it cool on a rack. She takes a knife and cuts a slice for Sara and Ben. They each get a plate and a fork. They sit at the table and enjoy their cake and salad.

"Happy birthday, Dad!" Sara and Ben say.

"Thank you, Sara and Ben. And thank you, Mom. This is the best cake and salad ever," Dad says.

He hugs Mom and kisses Sara and Ben. He is very happy. He is also very tall. Sara and Ben have to look up to see his face. They love their Dad. They love their Mom. They love their cake and salad. They are a happy family.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball went too far and they had to look for it.

One time, the ball rolled under a bench where a tall lady was sitting. She had a big hat and a long dress. Tom and Lily ran to the bench and asked the lady if they could have their ball back.

"Of course, my dears," the lady said. She smiled and bent down to get the ball. She gave it to Tom and said, "What a nice ball you have. Do you like playing with it?"

"Yes, we do," Tom and Lily said. They thanked the lady and ran back to their spot. They kicked the ball again and had fun.

But then, Lily realized something. She stopped and looked at the lady. She said to Tom, "Hey, do you know who that lady is?"

Tom shook his head. He said, "No, why?"

Lily pointed at the lady and said, "She is the queen! I saw her on TV. She has a crown and a big house. She is very important."

Tom looked at the lady again. He saw that she had a shiny thing on her head and a bag with a picture of a lion. He said, "Wow, you are right. She is the queen. How cool is that?"

Tom and Lily felt very lucky. They waved at the lady and said, "Bye, queen. Thank you for our ball."

The lady waved back and said, "Bye, Tom and Lily. You are very welcome. Have a nice day."

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with red fruits. They want to eat the fruits. They are hungry.

"Look, Jen, red fruits! Let's pick some!" Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, they look yummy! But how can we reach them? The tree is very tall!" Jen says.

Tom has an idea. He sees a big rock near the tree. He says, "I can climb on the rock. Then I can pick some fruits for us."

Jen says, "Be careful, Tom. The rock is not stable. It can move."

Tom does not listen to Jen. He climbs on the rock. He stretches his hand to pick a fruit. But the rock moves. Tom falls down. He hurts his leg. He cries.

Jen runs to Tom. She says, "Oh, Tom, are you okay? I told you to be careful. The rock is not stable."

Tom says, "I'm sorry, Jen. I did not listen to you. I was greedy. I wanted to pick the fruits."

Jen says, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. But you should listen to your friends. They want to help you. They want to save you from trouble."

Tom says, "You are right, Jen. You are a good friend. You saved me from the rock. Thank you."

Jen says, "You are welcome, Tom. Come on, let's go home. We can eat something else. Maybe we can find some cookies."

Tom and Jen hold hands. They walk home. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They should listen to their friends. They should not be greedy. They should be thankful.

Lily and Ben were twins. They liked to play with their toys and their dog, Spot. One day, their mom said, "It is your birthday soon. I have a present for you, but you have to wait until the party."

Lily and Ben were very excited. They wondered what the present was. They asked their mom for clues, but she only smiled and said, "It is a surprise."

The next day, Lily and Ben saw a big box in the living room. It had a bow and a card on it. They ran to the box and tried to peek inside. But their mom stopped them and said, "No, no, this is not your present. This is for someone else. You have to wait until the party."

Lily and Ben were confused. They looked at the box and then at their mom. They asked, "Who is the present for? Is it for Spot? Is it a new toy? Is it a cake?"

Their mom laughed and said, "No, it is not for Spot, or a toy, or a cake. It is for someone very special. You will see at the party."

Lily and Ben were still confused. They decided to play with Spot and feed him some treats. They hoped their mom would tell them more about the present later. They could not wait for the party.

Sara and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They went to the kitchen and opened the refrigerator. They saw many things inside.

"Look, Sara, there is cheese and ham and bread. We can make a sandwich," Tom said.

"Yes, and there is milk and juice and fruit. We can have a drink and a snack," Sara said.

They took out what they wanted and put it on the table. They made their sandwiches and poured their drinks. They were happy.

But then they saw something else in the refrigerator. It was a big cake with candles and frosting. It had a sign that said "Happy Birthday, Mom!"

"Wow, Tom, look at that cake! It is so pretty and unique. It has Mom's name and flowers and stars. Do you think we can have some?" Sara asked.

Tom looked at the cake and licked his lips. He wanted to taste it too. But he also knew that it was Mom's special cake. She would be sad if they ate it.

"No, Sara, we can't have the cake. It is for Mom. She will be home soon and we will sing and give her hugs and kisses. Then we can all have the cake together. It will be more fun," Tom said.

Sara thought about it and nodded. She loved Mom and wanted to make her happy. She put the cake back in the refrigerator and closed the door.

"OK, Tom, you are right. Let's eat our sandwiches and drink our juice. Then we can clean up and wait for Mom. I can't wait to see her smile," Sara said.

They ate their food and enjoyed it. They threw away the trash and washed the dishes. They went to the living room and played with their toys. They heard the door open and ran to hug Mom.

"Happy Birthday, Mom! We love you!" they shouted.

Mom hugged them back and thanked them. She saw the cake in the refrigerator and smiled. She was proud of her children. They were so sweet and unique. She cut the cake and gave them each a slice. They sang and laughed and had a good time. It was a happy end.

Lily was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She lived in a big house with many rooms, but they were all empty and quiet. She liked to watch the birds outside her window, but they flew away too fast. She wished she had someone to talk to.

One day, she found a bookcase in the corner of her room. It was old and dusty, but it had many books with colorful pictures. Lily liked to look at the pictures and make up stories in her head. She wondered what the books said, but she could not read the words.

She picked up a book with a picture of a cat on the cover. She opened it and saw more cats inside. They were playing, sleeping, and chasing mice. Lily smiled and said, "Hello, cats. Do you want to be my friends?"

To her surprise, one of the cats in the book answered, "Meow, meow. Yes, we do. We are lonely too. We live in this book, but no one ever reads us. We want to have fun and adventure. Can you help us?"

Lily was amazed and happy. She said, "Yes, I can. How can I help you?"

The cat said, "You can watch us and talk to us. You can turn the pages and see what we do. You can imagine that you are with us. We will show you our world and make you laugh. We will be your friends."

Lily nodded and said, "That sounds wonderful. Thank you, cats. You are very nice. Let's start now."

She turned the page and saw the cats running in a field of flowers. She watched them and talked to them. She felt less lonely and more happy. She had found new friends in the bookcase.

Sara was miserable. She wanted to go to the park with her mom and dad, but they said it was too cold. They said she had to wear a blouse and a coat and a hat and a scarf. Sara did not like the blouse. It was pink and had buttons and lace. Sara liked blue and green and yellow. She liked zippers and pockets and stars.

Sara tried to take off the blouse, but it was too hard. The buttons were small and tight. She pulled and pulled, but the blouse did not come off. She started to cry. Mom heard her and came to her room.

"What's wrong, Sara?" Mom asked.

"I don't like this blouse!" Sara said. "It's ugly and itchy and it hurts!"

Mom hugged Sara and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I know you don't like the blouse, but it's warm and pretty. You have to wear it today, because it's very cold outside. How about we attach a pin to it? A pin with a star, like you like. Would that make you feel better?"

Sara looked at Mom and saw the pin in her hand. It was blue and shiny and had a big star. Sara liked the pin. She nodded and said, "Yes, please."

Mom smiled and said, "Okay, then. Let's attach the pin to your blouse. There, now you look lovely. And you have a star, just like you wanted. Are you ready to go to the park now?"

Sara looked at herself in the mirror and saw the pin on her blouse. She felt a little better. She said, "Yes, Mom. I'm ready. Thank you."

Mom kissed Sara and said, "You're welcome, Sara. I love you. Come on, let's go. Dad is waiting for us."

Sara took Mom's hand and went to the door. She still did not like the blouse, but she liked the pin. And she liked the park. And she loved Mom and Dad. She was not miserable anymore. She was happy.

Timmy was a little boy who liked to play all day. He had many toys, but his favorite was a big clock that made loud noises. He liked to turn the clock's hands and hear it tick and tock. He also liked to make the clock ring and wake up his mom and dad.

One night, Timmy was not sleepy at all. He wanted to play with his clock some more. He sneaked out of his bed and took his clock to the living room. He turned the clock's hands to make it ring very loud. He laughed and clapped his hands.

But his mom and dad were not happy. They came to the living room and saw Timmy with his clock. They looked very pale and tired. They said, "Timmy, what are you doing? It is time to sleep, not to play. You are making too much noise and disturbing everyone. You need to sleep to grow big and strong and healthy. And you need to respect other people's sleep too. How would you feel if someone woke you up when you were dreaming?"

Timmy felt sorry. He did not mean to make his mom and dad angry or sad. He said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. I was just having fun with my clock. I didn't think about how you felt. I will go to sleep now and be quiet. Can I keep my clock in my room?"

His mom and dad smiled and hugged him. They said, "Yes, you can keep your clock in your room, but only if you promise to not make it ring at night. You can play with it in the morning when everyone is awake. And you can also learn how to tell time with it. That is a useful skill. Now, let's go to bed and have sweet dreams."

Timmy nodded and followed his mom and dad to his room. He put his clock on his nightstand and kissed it goodnight. He said, "I love you, clock. You are a fun toy, but you are also a good teacher. Tomorrow, I will learn how to tell time with you. But now, I will sleep and let you sleep too. Goodnight, clock."

He snuggled under his blanket and closed his eyes. He felt happy and peaceful. He learned a lesson that night. He learned that sleep is important for himself and for others. He learned that playing is fun, but not at the wrong time or place. He learned that he should be considerate and respectful of other people's feelings and needs. He learned that his clock was more than a toy, it was a friend and a guide. He slept well and dreamed of happy things.

Tom and Lily are playing a game. They have to find things that are useful in the house. The one who finds the most things wins a prize. The prize is a big red ball.

Tom runs to the kitchen. He thinks of many useful things. He finds a spoon, a knife, a cup, a plate, and a pot. He puts them in a basket. He is happy. He thinks he will win the prize.

Lily goes to the bedroom. She thinks of some useful things too. She finds a pillow, a blanket, a book, a doll, and a hat. She puts them in a bag. She is also happy. She thinks she will win the prize.

They meet in the living room. They show each other what they have found. They count the things. They both have five things. They are surprised. They do not know who wins the prize.

"Who wins the prize?" Tom asks.

"I do not know," Lily says.

They think for a while. Then they have an idea.

"Why do not we share the prize?" Tom says.

"Yes, let us share the prize," Lily says.

They smile. They hug. They take the big red ball. They play with it together. They are both happy. They think sharing is useful.

Jen and Tom were very happy. They were on holiday with Mum and Dad. They went to the beach every day and played in the sand and the water. They made castles and boats and dug holes. They saw fish and crabs and shells.

One day, Jen and Tom wanted to make a big castle. They worked very hard and used many buckets and spades. They put shells and stones on the castle to make it pretty. They were very proud of their castle.

"Look, Mum and Dad, look at our castle!" they shouted.

Mum and Dad came to see their castle. They smiled and clapped.

"Wow, what a wonderful castle!" Mum said. "You did a great job!"

"Yes, you did!" Dad said. "But do you know what? Today is our last day on holiday. We have to finish packing and go home soon."

Jen and Tom felt sad. They did not want to leave their castle and the beach. They wanted to stay on holiday.

"But we want to play more!" Jen said.

"Can we take our castle with us?" Tom asked.

Mum and Dad laughed. They hugged Jen and Tom.

"You are so silly!" Mum said. "We can't take the castle with us. It is too big and heavy. And the water and the wind will wash it away anyway. But we can take pictures of it and remember it. And we can come back next year and make another castle. How does that sound?"

Jen and Tom thought about it. They still felt sad, but they also felt happy. They liked the idea of coming back and making another castle. They nodded and smiled.

"OK, Mum and Dad," they said. "Let's take pictures of our castle and finish packing. And let's have fun on the way home. Maybe we can see some animals or sing some songs."

Mum and Dad nodded and smiled. They took pictures of the castle and of Jen and Tom. Then they helped them finish packing and put everything in the car. They said goodbye to the beach and the castle and drove away. They had a lot of fun on the way home. They saw some cows and horses and sheep. They sang some songs and told some jokes. They were a happy family. They had a great holiday.

Lily loves her kitten, Snowy. Snowy is soft and white and likes to play with Lily. They play with a ball of yarn, a feather and a toy mouse. Lily laughs when Snowy chases the mouse and pounces on it.

One day, Lily and Snowy are playing in the garden. They see a big yellow flower. Lily thinks it is pretty and smells it. Snowy thinks it is fun and rubs his nose on it. But the flower has pollen. Pollen makes Lily and Snowy sneeze.

"Achoo!" Lily sneezes. "Achoo!" Snowy sneezes. They sneeze again and again. Lily's nose is tickly. Snowy's nose is itchy. They don't like the flower anymore.

"Let's go inside, Snowy," Lily says. "We need a tissue." Snowy nods and follows Lily. They go inside and find a tissue. Lily wipes her nose and Snowy's nose. They feel better.

"Sorry, Snowy," Lily says. "I didn't know the flower would make us sneeze." Snowy purrs and licks Lily's cheek. He is not mad at Lily. He loves Lily. Lily hugs Snowy. She loves Snowy. They are happy.

Lily liked to play with her toy car. She made it zoom on the floor, on the table, on the sofa. She liked to make it go fast and make noises. Vroom, vroom, vroom!

One day, she saw a big bird in the window. It was a parrot. It had many colors on its feathers. It looked at Lily and said, "Hello, hello, hello!"

Lily was surprised. She ran to the window and said, "Hello, bird! What is your name?"

The parrot said, "My name is Polly. I can talk. Can you talk?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, I can talk. I can also zoom with my car. Do you want to play with me?"

Polly said, "Yes, I want to play with you. But I have to go soon. It is getting dark. Dark is bad for me. I have to go back to my home."

Lily said, "Where is your home?"

Polly said, "My home is far away. I flew away from my home. I was bored. I wanted to see new things. But now I miss my home. I miss my friends. I miss my food."

Lily felt sad for Polly. She said, "I have an idea. You can stay with me for a while. I can share my food with you. I can be your friend. And you can zoom with me and my car."

Polly smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. I would like to stay with you for a while. But I have to go back to my home someday. Will you help me find my home?"

Lily said, "Yes, I will help you find your home. But first, let's play. Let's zoom with my car. Vroom, vroom, vroom!"

And they played and zoomed and talked until it was dark. Then they ate some crackers and fruit and went to sleep. Lily gave Polly a hug and said, "Good night, Polly. You are my friend."

Polly said, "Good night, Lily. You are my friend too."

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore everything in her house. One day, she saw a telephone on the table. She wanted to know what it was and how it worked. She climbed on a chair and reached for the telephone.

"Hello, hello, is anyone there?" she said into the telephone. She heard a voice on the other end. It was her grandma, who was calling to say hello to her and her mom.

"Hi, Lily, it's grandma. How are you, my dear?" said the voice.

Lily was surprised and happy to hear her grandma. She smiled and said, "Hi, grandma, I'm fine. I'm playing with the telephone."

"Oh, that's nice, Lily. But be careful, don't drop the telephone, okay? It might break or hurt you," said grandma.

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, grandma, I won't drop the telephone."

But then, she heard her mom calling her from the kitchen. She wanted to see what her mom was doing. She forgot about the telephone and ran to the kitchen. She let go of the telephone and it fell to the floor with a loud crash.

"Oh, no, Lily, what have you done?" said her mom, who came to the living room and saw the broken telephone. "You dropped the telephone and now it's broken. You can't talk to grandma anymore. And you could have hurt yourself or the chair. Why did you do that?"

Lily felt sad and sorry. She realized she made a mistake. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was curious about the telephone and I wanted to talk to grandma. But then I heard you and I wanted to see you. I forgot about the telephone and I dropped it. I didn't mean to break it."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I know, Lily, you didn't mean to break it. But you have to be more careful and listen to what grandma and I tell you. The telephone is not a toy. It's a tool to communicate with people who are far away. You have to respect it and use it properly. And you have to pay attention to what you are doing and not run away when you are holding something. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, grandma. I love you both."

Her mom smiled and said, "We love you too, Lily. And we forgive you. But next time, please be more careful and responsible, okay?"

Lily said, "Okay, mom. I will. Thank you, mom."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the child to be careful and responsible with things that are not toys, to listen to the advice of elders, and to apologize when they make a mistake.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, their mom brought home a painter who wanted to paint their room a new color. The painter told them to stay away from his tools and paints, because they were not for children.

But Anna and Ben were naughty and did not listen. They ignored the painter and his words. When he went to get more paint, they sneaked into his bucket and took out some brushes and rollers. They thought it would be fun to paint the walls themselves.

They painted big and small shapes, letters and numbers, animals and flowers, all over the walls. They used many colors and made a big mess. They laughed and giggled as they painted.

But the painter was not happy when he saw what they had done. He was angry and sad. He said, "Why did you do this? You ruined my work and your room. You wasted my paint and time. You did not respect me or your mom. You were very naughty and rude."

Anna and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had made a big mistake. They said, "We are sorry, Mr. Painter. We did not mean to hurt you or our mom. We just wanted to have fun. But we were wrong. We should have listened to you and stayed away from your tools and paints. We will help you clean up and fix the walls."

The painter sighed and said, "Thank you for saying sorry and offering to help. But you should have thought before you acted. You should have obeyed the rules and been polite. You should have respected other people's work and property. That is the right thing to do."

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "We understand, Mr. Painter. We will remember your words and be good from now on. We will not ignore you or anyone else again. We will be kind and careful."

The painter smiled and said, "That is good to hear. I hope you will keep your promise. And I hope you will like your new room when it is done. It will be beautiful and bright."

Anna and Ben hugged the painter and said, "Thank you, Mr. Painter. We are sure we will love our new room. And we are sorry for being naughty. We will be good."

But the boat is not for children. It is for grown-ups who want to fish. The people on the boat are not happy to see Sara and Ben. They say they have to get off the boat. They say they are not safe on the boat. They say they are not organized on the boat.

Sara and Ben do not want to get off the boat. They want to stay on the boat. They cry and scream and kick. They do not listen to the people on the boat. They do not listen to the captain. They do not listen to the horn.

They wish they had not gone on the boat. They wish they had not grabbed the life jackets. They wish they had stayed near the lake.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with books and toys. One day, they find a big book with many words. It is a dictionary.

"What is this?" Lily asks.

"It is a dictionary. It has many words and what they mean," Ben says.

"Can we read it?" Lily says.

"Yes, we can. But some words are hard. We need to add letters to make them," Ben says.

They open the dictionary and look for words. They see a word that starts with S. It is sad.

"What is sad?" Lily asks.

"Sad is when you feel bad. Like when you lose your toy or your friend goes away," Ben says.

"Oh, I know sad. I was sad when my dog ran away," Lily says.

"Me too. I was sad when you were sick and could not play," Ben says.

They hug each other. They are not sad now. They are happy. They have each other and the dictionary. They add more letters and learn more words. They have fun.

Lily was a girl who liked to deliver things. She had a bike with a big basket, and she would fill it with flowers, books, toys, and snacks. She would ride around her street and give them to her friends and neighbors. She was very kind and happy.

One day, she wanted to deliver something to her school. She had not been there for a long time, because of a bad bug that made people sick. She missed her teacher and her classmates, and she wanted to make them smile. She packed her basket with colorful cards, stickers, and cookies. She put on her helmet and started to pedal.

But on the way, she saw a big dog. It was wild and angry. It barked and chased her. Lily was scared and tried to go faster. But the dog was faster. It jumped and bit her basket. It tore the cards, stickers, and cookies. Lily cried and stopped. The dog ran away with the basket.

Lily was very sad. She had nothing to deliver to her school. She felt like going home and hiding. But then, she heard a voice.

"Lily, is that you?" It was her teacher. She had seen her from the window. She came out and hugged her. "Are you okay? What happened?"

Lily told her about the wild dog and the basket. She sobbed and said she was sorry. She wanted to deliver something nice to her school, but she failed.

Her teacher smiled and wiped her tears. "Lily, you don't have to be sorry. You are very brave and generous. You tried to do something good, and that's what matters. The dog was mean, but you are not. They gave her hugs, drawings, and flowers. Lily felt warm and happy. She forgot about the wild dog and the basket. She had something better to deliver: her love.

"Wow, this is fun!" Lila said. She looked around and saw many things. She saw a wheel, a bell, a map, and a radio.

"Who is on my boat? Get off now! You are in trouble!"

"Help! Help! There are two kids on my boat! They are stealing it! Rescue me!"

Suddenly, a friendly fish saw Blue and offered to help. The fish pulled the anchor and set Blue free. From that day on, Blue learned to be careful where to rest and always be grateful for the help of others.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be eager to explore, but also to be mindful of where you anchor yourself and to be grateful for those who help you soar.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat. The boat was sailing on the big blue sea. Suddenly, the boat saw a harbor. The harbor was very clean and it looked like a nice place to stop. 

The boat said, "Hello harbor, can I come in?" 

The harbor said, "Yes, welcome little boat!" 

The boat was happy to hear that. It sailed into the harbor and stopped. The boat said, "Thank you for letting me come in. Your harbor is very clean." 

The harbor said, "Thank you. We try to keep it clean so all the boats can come and rest here." 

The boat was happy to have found such a nice place to rest. It stayed in the harbor for a while before sailing back out to sea.

Once upon a time, there was a reindeer named Rudy. Rudy was very restless because he wanted to go outside and play in the snow. But his owner, Santa Claus, said it was too cold and dangerous to go outside. Rudy didn't like that and started to yell at Santa Claus.

Santa Claus tried to calm Rudy down, but he kept yelling and getting more and more restless. Finally, Santa Claus had an idea. He took Rudy outside to play in the snow, but only for a little bit. Rudy was so happy and stopped yelling.

After they played, Santa Claus took Rudy back inside to rest. Rudy was tired and fell asleep right away. From then on, whenever Rudy got restless, Santa Claus would take him outside to play for a little bit. And Rudy was always happy and never yelled again. The end.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to the river with his mom. They saw a large crocodile in the water. Timmy was scared and said, "Mommy, what's that big thing in the water?"

His mom replied, "That's a crocodile, Timmy. It's a big animal with sharp teeth."

Timmy asked, "Can we mark the crocodile so we know it's the same one if we see it again?"

His mom said, "No, Timmy. We can't mark wild animals. It's not safe." 

Timmy nodded and they continued to watch the crocodile from a safe distance. They were happy to see it swim away and disappear into the water.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the beach with her bucket and shovel. Every day, she would build sandcastles and collect seashells.

One day, Lily saw a big wave coming towards her. She knew that the tide was coming in. She quickly gathered her things and ran to her mommy. "Mommy, can you lend me your hand?" she asked. Her mommy held her hand tightly and they walked safely away from the water.

Later that day, Lily's friend Tommy came to play with her. He wanted to try on her sunglasses, but they didn't fit him very well. Lily remembered that she had another pair of sunglasses that might fit Tommy better. She went to get them and lent them to him. Tommy was very happy and they continued to play together until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Spot went for a walk and got lost in the woods. He was scared and didn't know what to do.

Luckily, a kind man saw Spot and went to rescue him. The man brought Spot back to his home and gave him a warm bed to sleep in. Spot was so happy and grateful to be safe and warm.

The next morning, the man gave Spot a mint to eat. Spot had never tasted a mint before, but he loved it! From that day on, Spot was always careful when he went for walks and never got lost again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat jam on her toast every morning. One day, she wanted to make her own jam. She asked her mom for help.

"Mommy, can we make jam?" Lily asked.

"Of course, sweetie," her mom replied.

They went to the store to buy some fruit. They picked strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries. When they got home, they started to make the jam. Lily helped her mom stir the fruit and sugar in a pot. They let it cook on the stove for a while.

After it was done, Lily wanted to hang the jar of jam on the fridge. She climbed up on a chair and reached for the jar. But she accidentally dropped it and it shattered on the floor. The jam was everywhere.

Lily started to cry. "I'm sorry, Mommy," she said.

"It's okay, sweetie," her mom said. "Accidents happen."

Even though Lily was sad, she learned that it's important to be careful with things that are fragile.

"It's a ladybug," her mom replied.

Lily was curious about the ladybug and wanted to keep it as a pet. "Can I keep it, Mommy?" she asked.

"Sure, but you have to be gentle with it," her mom said.

Lily was so happy to have a new pet. She carefully picked up the ladybug and put it in a jar with some grass. She watched the ladybug crawl around and was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bear who lived in the forest. The bear was big and brown and loved to play with his friends. One day, the bear found a shiny treasure and he felt very proud. He showed it to all his friends and they all said how amazing it was. The bear felt very important and forgot to be humble.

But then, the bear went to bury his treasure in a secret spot. While he was digging, he accidentally hit a beehive and all the bees came out and stung him. The bear was in a lot of pain and he realized that he should have been more careful. He also realized that it's not good to show off and be too proud.

The bear went back to his friends and apologized for his behavior. They forgave him and the bear learned an important lesson about being humble. From then on, he was always careful and never forgot to be kind and humble. The end.

Mommy hugged Lily and said, "Don't worry, we can go home and unpack a new ice-cream from the freezer." Lily stopped crying and smiled. She was happy again, knowing she would get more ice-cream soon.

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel. The squirrel lived in a big tree with lots of leaves. One day, the squirrel saw an acorn on the ground. The acorn was very attractive to the squirrel, so she picked it up with her tiny paws. 

The squirrel wanted to eat the acorn, but it was too hard. She tried to bite it, but it wouldn't yield. So, the squirrel decided to hide the acorn in a little hole in the tree. She thought maybe it would yield and become softer over time. 

Days went by and the squirrel forgot about the acorn. But one day, she remembered and went to check on it. To her surprise, the acorn had yielded! It was softer and easier to eat. The squirrel was very happy and ate the acorn with delight. From then on, she always looked for attractive acorns to hide and yield.

Her mom came running and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

"I fell down while playing with my hoop," Lily replied, wiping her tears.

Her mom said, "Don't worry, dear. You are still very attractive even with a small scratch on your knee. Let me clean it up for you." Her mom cleaned up the scratch and put a band-aid on it. Lily felt better and went back to playing with her hoop.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety lived in a cage that was comfortable and cozy. Every day, Tweety would sing and play with his toys, but he always dreamed of flying free in the big blue sky.

One day, Tweety saw the door to his cage was open. He wanted to fly out and explore, but he was scared. He remembered his mom telling him to be careful and not get hurt. Tweety decided to stay in his cage where he felt safe.

Later that day, Tweety heard a loud noise. He looked outside and saw a cat trying to sneak up on him. Tweety quickly locked the door to his cage and felt relieved that he was safe inside. He realized that his cage was not just comfortable, but also protected him from danger.

From that day on, Tweety felt grateful for his cage and knew that it was his home where he could sing, play and be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the park to play. Lily wanted to go ice skating, but her mommy said it was too hot for ice. 

Suddenly, Lily saw a big truck coming towards the park. It was carrying a lot of ice! The truck driver said he was going to make an ice rink for everyone to skate on. But Lily's mommy was worried the ice would melt too fast in the heat.

So, they decided to prevent the ice from melting by putting it in a big freezer until it was ready to use. Lily was so happy when the ice rink was finally ready. She put on her skates and glided across the ice with a big smile on her face.

Lily was going to sleep over at her friend Mia's house for the first time. She was very excited, but also a little nervous. She packed her favorite blanket, her teddy bear, and her toothbrush in her backpack.

"Are you ready, Lily?" her mom asked, as they got in the car.

"Yes, Mommy, I'm ready!" Lily said, smiling.

They drove to Mia's house, where Mia and her mom were waiting for them. Lily hugged her mom goodbye and followed Mia to her room. They played with dolls, read books, and had pizza for dinner. They had a lot of fun.

When it was time for bed, Mia showed Lily where she could sleep. She had a cozy bed with pink sheets and a fluffy pillow. Lily put her backpack on the floor and took out her teddy bear. She looked for her blanket, but she couldn't find it.

"Mia, where is my blanket?" she asked, feeling scared.

"I don't know, Lily. Did you bring it?" Mia said.

Lily thought hard. She remembered putting her blanket in her backpack, but maybe she forgot to zip it. Maybe her blanket fell out of the car, or on the way to Mia's room. She felt tears in her eyes.

"I want my blanket!" she cried. "I can't sleep without my blanket!"

Mia saw that Lily was very sad. She wanted to help her friend. She had an idea.

"Lily, you can share my blanket. It's very soft and warm. And you can cuddle with your teddy bear. And I'll be right next to you. You'll be okay, Lily. Don't be nervous," she said, giving Lily a hug.

Lily sniffled and nodded. She was still missing her blanket, but she felt better with Mia's kindness. She climbed into the bed and wrapped herself in Mia's blanket. She hugged her teddy bear and smiled at Mia.

"Thank you, Mia. You're a good friend," she said.

"You're welcome, Lily. You're a good friend, too. Good night, Lily," Mia said.

"Good night, Mia," Lily said.

They closed their eyes and fell asleep, feeling safe and happy.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys and watch videos. One day, they find a new video in the living room. It is about fish and sharks. They want to watch it.

They put the video in the player and sit on the couch. The video starts. They see blue water and many fish. They are happy. They point at the fish and say their names.

Then, they see a big shark. It has sharp teeth and a deep voice. It swims fast and chases the fish. Lily and Ben are scared. They scream and hide behind the pillows.

Mom hears them scream. She runs to the living room. She sees the video and the twins. She turns off the video and hugs them.

"Shh, it's okay. It's just a video. The shark can't hurt you. You are safe with me." She says.

Lily and Ben stop screaming. They calm down. They look at Mom and smile.

"Thank you, Mom. We don't like the shark. We like the fish." They say.

Mom smiles back. She takes the video out of the player and puts it away.

"Let's watch something else. How about a video about puppies and kittens?" She says.

Lily and Ben nod. They love puppies and kittens. They cuddle with Mom and watch the video. They are happy again.

Tim and Liz liked to play pirate in the backyard. They had a big box that was their ship, and a flag with a skull and bones. They wore hats and eye patches and said "Arrr!" a lot.

One day, a new boy came to play with them. His name was Sam, and he had a toy sword. He wanted to be the captain of the pirate ship, but Tim and Liz said no. They said they were the captains, and Sam had to be their crew.

Sam did not like that. He said he was the best pirate ever, and he could beat them all. He tried to take the flag and the box, but Tim and Liz resisted. They pushed him away and said he had to share.

Sam got angry and swung his sword at them. He said he would make them walk the plank. But Tim and Liz were not scared. They had sticks and spoons that they used as swords and guns. They fought back and made Sam run away.

Tim and Liz were happy. They had defended their ship and their flag. They hugged each other and said they were good pirates. They were humble and did not brag. They invited Sam to come back and play nicely, if he wanted to. They said they could all be friends and have fun.

Tom and Lily were playing with cubes. They liked to build towers and houses with them. Tom had many cubes, but Lily had only a few. Lily asked Tom if she could borrow some of his cubes.

"No, they are mine!" Tom said. He was selfish. He did not want to share with Lily. He grabbed all the cubes and put them in a big pile.

Lily was sad. She wanted to play with Tom, but he was not nice. She looked around and saw a toy car. She decided to play with it instead. She pushed the car and made it speed on the floor. It was fun.

Tom saw Lily playing with the car. He wanted to play with it too. He left his cubes and ran to Lily. He tried to take the car from her.

"Give me the car!" Tom said. He was selfish. He did not care that Lily was playing with it.

"No, it is mine!" Lily said. She held the car tight. She did not want to give it to Tom. They both pulled the car and fought over it.

They did not see the big pile of cubes behind them. They bumped into it and made it fall. The cubes hit them on the head and hurt them. They cried and dropped the car.

Mama heard them crying and came to see what happened. She saw the mess and the car. She was angry.

"What did you do?" Mama said. She was disappointed. She did not like to see them fight and be selfish.

Tom and Lily felt sorry. They knew they were wrong. They said sorry to each other and to Mama. They learned to share and be nice.

Moral: Sharing is caring. Being selfish can hurt you and others.

Tom and Mia are playing in the yard. They see a big box near the fence. They want to open it and see what is inside.

"Let's pull the box, Mia!" Tom says. He grabs one side of the box and tries to move it.

"OK, Tom!" Mia says. She grabs the other side of the box and helps Tom. They pull and pull, but the box is too heavy. They cannot open it.

They see a tool on the ground. It is a hammer. Tom picks it up and says, "Maybe we can use this tool to break the box. Then we can see what is inside."

He hits the box with the hammer. Bang! Bang! Bang! The box makes a loud noise. But it does not break.

Suddenly, the box shakes and makes a weird sound. It sounds like a growl. Tom and Mia are scared. They drop the hammer and run away.

"What is that, Tom?" Mia asks.

"I don't know, Mia. It is a weird thing. Maybe it is a monster!" Tom says.

They hide behind a tree and watch the box. The box opens and a big furry head pops out. It has two ears, two eyes, a nose and a mouth. It looks like a dog, but bigger and darker.

It is not a monster. It is a bear!

The bear looks around and sees Tom and Mia. It smiles and waves at them. It is a friendly bear.

"Hello, kids!" the bear says. "Thank you for waking me up. I was sleeping in the box. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom and Mia are surprised. They have never seen a talking bear before. They are still scared, but also curious.

"Who are you?" Tom asks.

"I am Ben. I am a circus bear. I escaped from the circus and I was looking for a new home. I found this box and I thought it was cozy. But I was lonely. I am happy to see you." Ben says.

"Wow, you are a circus bear? Can you do tricks?" Mia asks.

"Of course I can. I can roll over, stand on my hind legs, balance a ball on my nose, and more. Do you want to see?" Ben asks.

Tom and Mia nod. They are not scared anymore. They are excited.

"OK, then. Come closer and watch me. I will show you what I can do. And maybe you can teach me some new tricks too. We can be friends." Ben says.

Tom and Mia come closer and watch Ben. He does his tricks and makes them laugh. They clap and cheer for him. They also teach him some new tricks, like jumping, spinning, and high-fiving. They have fun together.

They forget about the box, the hammer, and the fence. They only think about the bear, the tricks, and the friendship. They have a weird, but wonderful, day.

Anna loves to sign. She signs with her hands and her face to tell her mom and dad what she wants and how she feels. She learned to sign from her teacher, who is deaf and uses sign language all the time. Anna thinks sign language is fun and beautiful.

One day, Anna goes to the park with her mom. She sees a big purple balloon floating in the sky. She points to it and signs, "Balloon! Purple! Pretty!" She wants the balloon very much. She makes a wish in her heart that the balloon will come to her.

Her mom sees her sign and smiles. She says, "Yes, that is a purple balloon. It is very pretty. Do you like it?" Anna nods and signs, "Yes! Like! Want!" Her mom says, "I'm sorry, honey, but we can't have that balloon. It belongs to someone else. Maybe we can find another balloon for you later."

Anna feels sad. She looks at the balloon and signs, "Please! Please! Please!" She hopes the balloon will hear her and come to her. She does not understand why she can't have it. She thinks it is not fair.

Suddenly, a gust of wind blows the balloon away from its string. It flies higher and higher in the sky, until it is very small. Anna watches it with wide eyes. She thinks the balloon is going to her wish. She claps her hands and signs, "Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!" She believes the balloon is happy to be free and to see the world. She feels happy too. She hugs her mom and signs, "Love you! Love you! Love you!" Her mom hugs her back and says, "I love you too, Anna. You are a very sweet and smart girl."

Tom and Lily are brother and sister. They share a room and a bed. Every night, they lie down and listen to a story from their mom. Mom is dependable. She always tells them a story and kisses them good night.

One night, there is a storm. The wind howls and the rain pours. Tom and Lily hear a loud boom. It is thunder. They see a bright flash. It is lightning. They are scared. The room is dark.

"Mom!" Tom cries. "Mom, where are you?"

"I'm here, sweetie," Mom says. She comes to their bed with a flashlight. She shines the light on their faces. They see her smile. "Don't be afraid. It's just a storm. It will pass soon."

"Can you stay with us, Mom?" Lily asks. She holds Mom's hand. "Can you tell us another story?"

"Of course, honey," Mom says. She lies down with them and cuddles them. She tells them a story about a brave lion and a clever mouse. They forget about the storm. They feel safe and warm. They fall asleep in Mom's arms. Mom is dependable. She loves them very much.

Lily did not like to go to bed. She wanted to play with her toys and watch TV. She hated bed. Every night, her mom and dad told her to brush her teeth and put on her pajamas. But Lily said no. She ran away and hid under the table.

"Lily, it's time for bed. You have to sleep, or you will be tired tomorrow," her mom said.

"No, I don't want to go to bed. I want to stay up," Lily said.

Her dad came and lifted her from under the table. He carried her to her room. He tucked her in and gave her a kiss.

"Good night, Lily. We love you. You have to sleep, or you will miss the fun things tomorrow," he said.

Lily pouted and turned away. She did not say good night. She closed her eyes, but she did not sleep. She was angry and sad.

She heard a noise outside her window. She opened her eyes and saw a big moon. It was bright and round. She saw stars, too. They were shiny and small. She felt curious and happy. She wanted to see more.

She got out of her bed and went to the window. She looked at the moon and the stars. She smiled and waved at them. She felt like they were her friends.

She heard a voice in her ear. It was the moon.

"Hello, Lily. Do you like me and the stars?" the moon said.

"Yes, I do. You are beautiful and nice," Lily said.

"Thank you, Lily. We like you, too. But you know what? We have to go soon. We only come out at night. When the sun comes, we have to sleep. That's how we stay ready for the next night," the moon said.

"Really? You have to sleep, too?" Lily said.

"Yes, we do. Everyone has to sleep, Lily. Even you. Sleep is good for you. It makes you grow and learn and dream. It makes you happy and healthy. If you don't sleep, you will miss the fun things tomorrow. You will be tired and grumpy. You will not enjoy the sun and the flowers and the birds. You will not play well with your toys and your friends. You will not listen to your mom and dad. You will not be a good girl," the moon said.

Lily thought about what the moon said. She realized that the moon was right. She needed to sleep. She wanted to be ready for the next day. She wanted to be happy and healthy. She wanted to be a good girl.

She said goodbye to the moon and the stars. She thanked them for talking to her. She went back to her bed. She snuggled with her teddy bear. She said good night to her mom and dad in her heart. She closed her eyes and fell asleep.

She had a nice dream. She dreamed that she was flying with the moon and the stars. They showed her many wonderful things. They told her stories and jokes. They made her laugh and sing. They were her friends.

She woke up in the morning. She felt refreshed and cheerful. She saw the sun shining through her window. She heard the birds chirping outside. She smelled the pancakes that her mom was making in the kitchen. She jumped out of her bed and ran to the bathroom. She brushed her teeth and put on her clothes. She was ready for the day.

She hugged her mom and dad and said good morning. She ate her pancakes and drank her milk. She played with her toys and watched TV. She had fun with her friends. She listened to her mom and dad. She was a good girl.

She learned that bed was not bad. She learned that sleep was good. She learned that the moon and the stars were her friends. She learned that she could be ready for the day. She did not hate bed anymore. She loved bed.

Sara and Ben wanted to play outside in the snow. It was evening and very icy, but they did not care. They put on their coats, hats, gloves and boots and ran to the backyard. They made a big snowman with a carrot nose, a scarf and a hat. They were very happy.

"Look at our snowman, he is so nice!" Sara said.

"Yes, he is. But I have an idea. Let's make him a friend!" Ben said.

They looked around and saw a big pile of snow near the fence. They ran to it and started to make another snowman. They did not see the sign that said "Danger. Thin ice. Do not go near the pond."

They worked hard and made another snowman. They gave him a button nose, a sweater and a cap. They were very proud.

"Look at our snowmen, they are so nice!" Ben said.

"Yes, they are. But I have another idea. Let's make them talk!" Sara said.

They found two sticks and put them in their snowmen's mouths. They pretended to make them talk to each other.

"Hello, I am Sam. I am your friend." Sara said in a high voice.

"Hello, I am Bob. I am your friend too." Ben said in a low voice.

They laughed and had fun. They did not hear the ice cracking under their feet.

Suddenly, the ice broke and they fell into the cold water. They screamed and tried to swim, but they could not. They were too cold and scared. They called for help, but no one heard them. The snowmen watched them with their stick mouths and button eyes. They did not say anything.

The end.

One day, a person named Tom saw a big cake on the table. He was very hungry and he wanted to eat the cake. He did not ask anyone if he could have some. He just took a big piece and put it in his mouth.

But the cake was not his. It was for his sister's birthday. His sister, Ann, came into the room and saw Tom eating her cake. She was very angry. She shouted at Tom, "That is my cake! You are very bad! Give it back to me!"

Tom was scared of Ann. He did not want to give back the cake. He wanted to run away. He ran out of the room with the cake in his hand. He ran down the stairs and out of the door. He ran to the park and hid behind a tree.

But he did not feel happy. He felt sad and sorry. He knew he did something wrong. He knew he hurt his sister's feelings. He knew he should say sorry and share the cake with her. He decided to go back home and face Ann.

He ran back to the house and knocked on the door. He saw Ann opening the door. She still looked angry. But Tom said, "I am sorry, Ann. I was very selfish. I should not have eaten your cake. Here, you can have the rest of it. And I will help you make a new one. Can you forgive me?"

Ann was surprised by Tom's words. She saw that he was sincere. She felt her anger melt away. She smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. You are very brave to admit your mistake. And you are very kind to offer to help me. Come on, let's go to the kitchen and make a new cake together."

Tom and Ann hugged each other and went to the kitchen. They made a new cake and decorated it with candles and sprinkles. They had a lot of fun and laughed a lot. They learned that it is better to be honest and generous than to be greedy and sneaky. They also learned that it is never too late to say sorry and make up. They were very happy and they loved each other very much.

"Look, parent, look! My kite is so high!" Tom shouted.

"I see, Tom, I see! Your kite is very beautiful and you are very good at flying it!" his parent said.

Tom smiled and thanked his parent. He was humble and kind. He did not want to show off or make others feel bad.

Soon, he saw another child with a kite. The child's kite was smaller and lower than Tom's. The child looked sad and lonely.

"Hello, what is your name?" Tom asked the child.

"I'm Lily," the child said.

"Do you want to fly your kite with me?" Tom offered.

"Really? Can I?" Lily asked.

"Sure, why not? There is enough wind and space for both of us. And maybe we can be friends," Tom said.

Lily smiled and nodded. She ran to Tom and his parent. They shared the string and watched their kites soar together. They felt happy and friendly.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play together and share their toys. One day, Lily found a passport in her mom's drawer. It had a picture of her mom and many stamps from different places.

"Look, Tom, this is a passport. My mom uses it to go to far lands. Do you have one?" Lily asked.

"No, I don't. Can I see it?" Tom said. He admired the passport and wished he could travel too.

"Be careful, don't make it dirty. My mom will be angry if she sees it," Lily warned.

But Tom did not listen. He took the passport and ran outside. He wanted to show it to the other kids. He did not see the big puddle of mud on the ground. He slipped and fell. The passport flew out of his hand and landed in the filthy water.

"Oh no! What have you done?" Lily cried. She ran after Tom and picked up the passport. It was wet and stained and torn. She tried to wipe it with her dress, but it only made it worse.

Tom felt sorry and scared. He did not mean to ruin the passport. He hoped Lily's mom would not be too mad.

But Lily's mom was very mad. She came home and saw the passport on the table. She yelled at Lily and Tom. She said they were naughty and careless. She said they could not play together anymore. She said she had to get a new passport and it would cost a lot of money.

Lily and Tom were very sad. They hugged each other and said sorry. They did not want to lose their friendship. But they had no choice. They had to say goodbye. They never saw each other again.

She ran to the tree and touched its bark. It felt rough and warm. She saw a hole in the tree, like a door. She peeked inside and saw a bright light. She heard a voice say, "Hello, little one. Do you want to see some magic?"

Lily was curious and brave. She nodded and stepped into the hole. She found herself in a beautiful garden, full of flowers, butterflies and birds. She saw a friendly old lady, who smiled and waved at her. She was wearing a purple dress and a hat with stars.

"Welcome to my magic tree, Lily," the old lady said. "I'm glad you came. I have a gift for you." She gave Lily a necklace with a shiny stone. "This is a magic stone. It can make your wishes come true. But you have to be careful what you wish for, and only use it for good things."

Lily thanked the old lady and put on the necklace. She felt happy and excited. She wished she could fly like a bird. She felt a tickle in her back and saw two wings sprout from her shoulders. She flapped them and lifted off the ground. She flew around the garden, laughing and singing.

She had so much fun, she forgot about the time. She heard her mom call her name from the park. She realized she had to go back. She flew to the old lady and hugged her. "Thank you for the magic, but I have to go now. My mom is waiting for me."

The old lady nodded and kissed her cheek. "You're welcome, Lily. You can come back anytime you want. Just remember to use your magic wisely and kindly. Goodbye, my dear." She waved as Lily flew out of the hole and back to the park.

Lily ran to her mom and hugged her. She told her about the magic tree and the old lady and the necklace. Her mom smiled and listened. She was glad Lily had a wonderful adventure, but she also wondered if it was all a dream. She looked at the necklace and saw the stone sparkle. She smiled and kissed Lily. "You're a very lucky girl, Lily. You have a magic gift. I love you very much."

Lily was a curious girl who liked to see new things. One day, she went with her mom to the market. There were many people and many things to look at. Lily saw fruits, flowers, toys, and clothes. She wanted to touch everything.

But Lily's mom said, "Stay close to me, Lily. The market is very busy and you might get lost." Lily nodded, but she still wanted to explore. She saw a big basket of apples and ran to it. She reached for an apple, but the basket was too high. She stumbled and fell on the ground.

Lily felt a pain in her knee and started to cry. She looked around and saw that her mom was not there. She was scared and alone. She cried louder and louder.

Then, she heard a voice. "Are you okay, little one?" It was a kind lady who sold flowers. She picked up Lily and gave her a hug. She also gave her a band-aid for her knee and a flower for her hair. She said, "Don't worry, we will find your mom. She must be looking for you."

Lily felt better and smiled. She thanked the kind lady and held her hand. They walked around the market and asked people if they had seen Lily's mom. Soon, they found her. She was very happy and relieved to see Lily. She hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was worried sick. I'm glad you're safe and sound."

Lily said, "I'm sorry, too, mom. I was curious and ran away. I stumbled and hurt my knee. But a nice lady helped me and gave me a flower." She showed her mom the flower and the band-aid.

Lily's mom thanked the nice lady and gave her some money for the flower. She said, "You are very kind and generous. Thank you for taking care of my daughter." The nice lady said, "You're welcome. She is a sweet and curious girl. I hope she feels better soon."

Lily's mom and the nice lady smiled at each other. Then, Lily's mom took Lily's hand and said, "Let's go home, Lily. We have seen enough of the market for today. Next time, we will be more careful and stay together." Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I love you." She also said, "Bye, nice lady. Thank you for the flower." She waved her hand and smiled.

The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to climb the big oak tree and pretend they were birds. They made nests with leaves and twigs and sang songs to each other.

One day, a man came to the park. He had a big truck and a saw. He said he was going to cut down the oak tree and sell the wood. He said the wood was expensive and he could make a lot of money.

Tom and Lily were very sad. They ran to the oak tree and hugged it. They said, "Please don't cut our tree! We love our tree! It is our friend and our home!"

The man laughed. He said, "You silly kids! This is not your tree! This is my tree! I bought it from the city. Now move away or I will call the police!"

Tom and Lily did not move. They cried and begged the man to leave the oak tree alone. They said, "The tree is alive! It has feelings! It gives us shade and air and fun! How can you be so mean?"

The man sighed. He was getting angry and impatient. He said, "Fine, I will make you a deal. If you can give me something more expensive than the wood, I will let you keep the tree. But hurry up, I don't have all day!"

Tom and Lily thought hard. They did not have anything expensive. They only had their toys and their clothes and their snacks. They looked at each other and had an idea.

They ran to the man and gave him their most precious things. Tom gave him his red car and his blue ball. Lily gave him her yellow dress and her pink doll. They said, "These are our favorite things. They are very expensive to us. Please take them and leave our tree alone."

The man looked at the things. He saw how old and dirty and broken they were. He shook his head. He said, "These are not expensive. These are junk. You are wasting my time. I don't want these. I want the wood!"

He pushed the things away and started his saw. He was about to cut the oak tree when he heard a loud noise. It was a siren. It was the police.

The police came to the park. They saw the man and the truck and the saw. They saw Tom and Lily and the oak tree. They asked, "What is going on here?"

Tom and Lily told them everything. They said, "The man wants to cut our tree and sell the wood. He said he bought the tree from the city. But we love our tree and we don't want him to hurt it. We gave him our most expensive things but he did not care. He is very bad and very greedy. Please help us!"

The police looked at the man. They asked, "Is this true? Did you buy the tree from the city?"

The man nodded. He said, "Yes, I did. I have the papers. Here, look."

He showed them the papers. The papers said, "I, the city, sell the oak tree in the park to the man for one dollar. Signed, the city."

The police looked at the papers. They said, "These papers are fake. You did not buy the tree from the city. You made these papers yourself. You are a liar and a thief. You are under arrest!"

They put handcuffs on the man and took him to the truck. They said, "You are going to jail. You will not cut any trees or sell any wood. You will learn your lesson."

Tom and Lily cheered. They said, "Thank you, police! Thank you for saving our tree!"

They hugged the oak tree and thanked it too. They said, "We are sorry, tree. We are sorry for the trouble. We hope you are not scared or hurt. We love you very much."

The oak tree rustled its leaves. It seemed to say, "I love you too. You are my friends. You are brave and kind. You make me happy."

Tom and Lily smiled. They climbed the oak tree and played again. They were happy and safe. They knew the oak tree would always be there for them. And they would always be there for the oak tree.

The little girl decided to look around for someone who might need a pebble and need some love. She went up to a little boy and asked if he wanted her pebble. The little boy smiled and thanked her. He told her that he had been feeling sad, too, but now he was happy.

The little girl walked away with a smile on her face. She was filled with a feeling of compassion. She realized that she didn't need someone else to feel better. She knew that when someone was feeling sad or lonely, a kind word and a pebble could make a big difference.
