Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Ann. Joe was a turkey and Ann was a little girl. Every day they would go out and play together.

One day, Ann asked Joe if they could go on an adventure. Joe was excited and said yes.

They went to a park. Ann said she wanted to fly like a turkey. Joe was happy to oblige and told her to grab his feathers. They quickly soared into the sky, starting their grand adventure.

But when they reached the top, Joe and Ann could see for miles. Suddenly, they felt the wind start to push them away from each other. Joe and Ann were separating.

Joe started flying backward, away from Ann. He was scared and had no idea what to do. Meanwhile, Ann started to cry. She had never been so far away from Joe before.

But then there was a loud noise, like a bell ringing. Suddenly, Ann and Joe felt the wind stop and they flew back together. They were so happy to be reunited and hugged each other tightly.

They flew back home, both thankful for their long, but exciting adventure. From that day forward, Joe and Ann never wanted to be separated again.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their dad. They saw a big hill with a lot of snow on it. They wanted to slide down the hill on their sleds. Dad said they could, but they had to be careful.

Tom and Lily put on their hats and gloves and got on their sleds. They pushed off and went very fast down the hill. They felt the cold wind on their faces and the snow under their sleds. They laughed and shouted with joy.

But then, Tom saw something in the snow. It was a small black bird. It was not moving. It looked hurt. Tom steered his sled to the side and stopped. He got off and ran to the bird. He picked it up gently and saw that it had a broken wing. He felt sorry for the bird.

Lily saw Tom and stopped her sled too. She came to see what he had. She saw the bird and said, "What is that?"

Tom said, "It is a coal. A coal is a kind of bird that is black and has a yellow beak. It is hurt. We have to save it."

Lily said, "How can we save it?"

Tom said, "We have to take it to dad. He can help it. He knows a lot of things."

Tom and Lily wrapped the coal in their scarves and got on their sleds. They slid down the rest of the hill and found their dad. They showed him the coal and told him what happened. Dad looked at the coal and said, "You did a good thing, Tom and Lily. You saved this coal. It is very cold and hungry. We have to take it home and give it some food and water and a warm place to rest. Maybe its wing will heal and it can fly again."

Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They were happy that they saved the coal. They hoped it would get better soon. They held the coal close and followed their dad to the car. They did not mind the bitter cold anymore. They felt warm in their hearts.

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were doctors and nurses, and they had a phone to call for help. Lily was the doctor and Max was the nurse.

"Hello, this is Doctor Lily. What is your problem?" Lily said into the phone.

"I have a tummy ache and I feel sick," Max said, holding his stomach.

"Oh no, that sounds serious. We need to come and see you right away. Where are you?" Lily asked.

"I'm in the kitchen, on the floor," Max said.

"OK, we're on our way. Don't move, we'll be there soon," Lily said, and hung up the phone.

Lily and Max grabbed their toy bags and ran to the kitchen. They saw their mom sitting at the table, reading a book. She looked up and smiled at them.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" she asked.

"We're playing doctors and nurses, Mom. We have a patient in the kitchen. He has a tummy ache and he feels sick," Lily said.

"Really? Who is it?" Mom asked.

"It's me, Mom. I'm the patient," Max said, lying on the floor.

Mom looked at Max and saw that he was pale and sweaty. She felt his forehead and saw that he was hot. She realized that he was not pretending. He was really sick.

"Oh, Max. You're not playing. You're really sick. You have a fever. We need to take you to the real doctor," Mom said, with a serious voice.

She picked up Max and carried him to the car. She told Lily to bring her phone and her purse. She drove to the doctor's office as fast as she could. She hoped that Max would be OK. She was glad that Lily had called her on the phone. She was a good doctor.

They also liked to make the castle bigger and smaller with their magic wand, which was really a stick they found.

One day, they saw an enormous butterfly flying over the fence. It was so pretty and colorful, they wanted to catch it and keep it as a pet. They ran after the butterfly, leaving their castle and wand behind. The butterfly was very fast and clever, and it led them far away from their garden.

While they were gone, a naughty boy named Max saw their castle and wand. He was curious and wanted to play with them. He picked up the wand and waved it at the castle, saying "Shrink, shrink, shrink!" The castle became smaller and smaller, until it was the size of a pebble. Max laughed and put the castle in his pocket. He was about to take the wand too, when he heard Tom and Mia coming back.

Tom and Mia were sad and tired. They could not catch the butterfly, and they lost their way. They were happy to see their garden again, but they were shocked to see their castle was gone. They looked around and saw Max holding their wand. They ran to him and asked him what he did with their castle.

Max was scared and sorry. He did not mean to be so mean. He took out the castle from his pocket and gave it back to them. He also gave them their wand and said "I'm sorry, I was just curious. I didn't know it was your castle. Please forgive me."

Tom and Mia were angry at first, but they saw that Max was sincere. They decided to forgive him and be friends. They used their wand to make their castle big again, and invited Max to play with them. Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They saw a big bush with many small round things on it. They were blue and purple and sweet.

"Look, blueberries!" Lily said. "Let's pick some and eat them."

They ran to the bush and started to pick the blueberries. They put them in their mouths and smiled. They were juicy and yummy.

But then they heard a growl. It was a big dog. It had black fur and sharp teeth. It was angry and hungry. It wanted the blueberries too.

"Go away, dog!" Ben shouted. "These are our blueberries!"

The dog did not listen. It jumped on the bush and tried to grab the blueberries. Ben and Lily were scared. They ran away from the bush and looked for a place to hide.

They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They ran to the tree and crawled into the hole. It was dark and cozy. They hugged each other and hoped the dog would not find them.

They heard the dog barking and sniffing outside. It smelled the blueberries on their hands and faces. It wanted to get into the hole and eat them.

"Shh, don't make a sound," Lily whispered. "Maybe it will go away."

They stayed very quiet and still. They rubbed their eyes and wished they were home. They wondered if their mom and dad were looking for them.

They waited and waited. The dog did not go away. It scratched and bit the tree. It made a lot of noise.

But then they heard another sound. It was a whistle. It was their dad. He had come to find them.

"Ben, Lily, where are you?" he called. "I have a surprise for you."

Ben and Lily were happy to hear his voice. They crawled out of the hole and ran to him. They hugged him and told him about the dog and the blueberries.

Their dad looked at the dog and shook his head. He said, "That's not a dog, that's a bear. A very naughty bear. He should not be here. He should be in the forest."

He took out a big stick and waved it at the bear. He said, "Go away, bear. Leave the blueberries alone. They are for the children, not for you."

The bear was afraid of the stick and the dad. He ran away into the woods. He did not come back.

Ben and Lily were glad the bear was gone. They thanked their dad for saving them. They asked him what the surprise was.

He smiled and said, "I have a big basket of blueberries for you. I picked them from another bush. They are bigger and sweeter than the ones you found. Do you want some?"

Ben and Lily nodded and cheered. They followed their dad to the basket and took some blueberries. They ate them and smiled. They were juicy and yummy.

They said, "We love blueberries. And we love you, dad."

Their dad said, "I love you too, Ben and Lily. You are my brave and clever children. But next time, be careful where you play. And don't go near the bears."

They run to the field where the balloon is landing. They see a man and a woman get out of the basket. They wave at Mia and Leo.

"Hello, kids! Do you like our balloon?" the man asks.

"Yes, it is very pretty! Can we touch it?" Mia asks.

"Sure, you can. But be careful, it is hot. Do you want to go for a ride?" the woman asks.

Mia and Leo look at each other. They are excited, but also anxious. They have never been in a balloon before. They don't know if it is safe or fun.

"Can we, please?" Leo asks.

"Only if your parents say yes. Where are they?" the man asks.

"They are at home. We live over there." Mia points to their house.

"Then you should go and ask them first. We will wait for you here." the woman says.

Mia and Leo nod. They run back to their house. They tell their parents about the balloon. Their parents are surprised, but they agree to let them go. They tell them to be careful and have fun.

Mia and Leo hug their parents and run back to the field. They see the balloon is still there. The man and the woman smile at them.

"Are you ready to fly?" the man asks.

"Yes, we are!" Mia and Leo say.

They climb into the basket. The man turns on the fire. The balloon starts to rise. Mia and Leo hold hands. They feel the wind and the sun. They see the trees and the houses. They see the birds and the bugs. They feel happy and free.

They fly in the air. They hug each other. They laugh and sing. They have the best day ever.

Anna is impatient. She wants to win the game. She picks a card and says "seven". Then she picks another card and says "nine". She does not wait for Ben to take his turn.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Ben says. "You have to wait for me. It's my turn now."

"No, it's not. I want to finish the game. I have more cards than you. I win!" Anna says.

Ben is sad. He does not like to play with Anna when she is impatient. He puts his cards down and walks away.

Anna is alone. She looks at her cards. She does not feel happy. She feels sorry. She likes to play with Ben. She wants to be his friend.

She runs after Ben and says "I'm sorry, Ben. I was impatient. I did not play nice. Can we play again?"

Ben smiles. He says "It's okay, Anna. I forgive you. Yes, we can play again. But this time, let's take turns and have fun."

Anna and Ben hug. They go back to their cards and play the game with numbers. They are happy. They are friends.

Lila and Tom were two little penguins who lived in a big igloo with their mama and papa. They liked to play in the snow and slide on the ice. One day, they saw a new igloo near their home. It was smaller and rounder than theirs, and it had a funny sign on it.

"Who lives there?" Lila asked.

"Let's go and see," Tom said.

They waddled over to the new igloo and knocked on the door. A friendly voice said, "Come in, come in!"

Lila and Tom entered the igloo and saw a big polar bear sitting on a pile of fish. He smiled and said, "Hello, little penguins. I'm Bob. I just moved here from the north. Do you want some fish?"

Lila and Tom were scared of the polar bear, but they were also hungry. They nodded and said, "Yes, please."

Bob was very generous and gave them each a big fish. He said, "You can have as much as you want. I have plenty. I like to share."

Lila and Tom ate the fish and thanked Bob. They felt warm and happy. They said, "You are very nice, Bob. Can we be friends?"

Bob said, "Of course, we can be friends. I'm glad you came to visit me. Do you want to stay and play?"

Lila and Tom said, "Yes, we do. But we have to ask our mama and papa first. They might worry about us."

Bob said, "That's a good idea. You can use my phone to call them. It's over there, next to the lamp."

Lila and Tom called their mama and papa and told them about Bob and his igloo. Their mama and papa said they could stay and play, but they had to be back before dark. They also said they wanted to meet Bob and thank him for his generosity.

Lila and Tom said, "OK, mama and papa. We love you. Bye."

They hung up the phone and played with Bob. They had a lot of fun. They told stories, sang songs, and made snowmen. When it was time to go, they hugged Bob and said, "Thank you, Bob. You are the best. We'll come back soon."

Bob said, "You're welcome, Lila and Tom. You are the sweetest. I'll see you soon."

Lila and Tom waved goodbye and walked back to their igloo. They told their mama and papa all about Bob and his igloo. Their mama and papa said they were proud of them for being brave and polite. They said they would visit Bob tomorrow and bring him some cookies.

Lila and Tom said, "Yay, cookies! We can't wait to see Bob again."

They brushed their teeth, put on their pajamas, and cuddled in their bed. They said, "Good night, mama and papa. Good night, Bob. We love you."

They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of fish and snow and friendship.

Lily was a smart girl who liked to read books and learn new things. She had a lot of fun with her friends at school, but sometimes she felt lonely at home. Her mom and dad were very busy and did not have much time to play with her.

She made a cozy nest for it in a shoebox and gave it some water and seeds. She named it Bluey and talked to it every day.

"Hello, Bluey. How are you today?" Lily asked. "I hope your wing will heal soon. You are very brave and strong. I wish I could fly with you and see the sky and the trees and the clouds."

Bluey chirped and looked at Lily with its bright eyes. It liked Lily very much and enjoyed her company. It felt safe and warm in the shoebox. It started to eat more and move more. Every day, its wing got a little better.

After a few weeks, Lily noticed that Bluey could flap its wing without pain. She was very happy and proud of Bluey. She knew it was time to let it go. She took the shoebox outside and opened it. Bluey hopped out and looked around. It saw the sun and the flowers and the other birds. It felt a surge of joy and freedom.

"Goodbye, Bluey. Thank you for being my friend. I will miss you, but I am glad you can fly again. Be careful and have fun. Maybe we will see each other again someday." Lily said.

Bluey nodded and thanked Lily. It gave her a gentle peck on the cheek and flew away. It soared high and low, feeling the wind and the warmth. It sang a beautiful song for Lily and the world.

Lily watched Bluey disappear in the distance. She felt a pang of sadness, but also a lot of love and gratitude. She smiled and wiped a tear from her eye. She learned a lot from Bluey. She learned how to care and share, how to heal and let go, how to be a good friend and a good person. She felt happy and peaceful. She went back inside and hugged her mom and dad. She had a lot of fun with her family and her friends. She never forgot Bluey and always looked for it in the sky.

Anna and Ben start to pull the doll. They both want the doll. They do not want to share. They shout and cry. The doll's hair and clothes get messy. The doll's body gets twisted. The doll looks sad.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the room. She sees Anna and Ben fighting over the doll. She is not happy. She says, "Stop! What are you doing? This doll is for both of you. You have to share. You have to be nice. You have to say sorry."

Anna and Ben stop. They look at the doll. They look at Mom. They feel bad. They say sorry to each other. They say sorry to the doll. They hug the doll and each other. They decide to play with the doll together. They make her hair and clothes nice again. They make her body flexible again. They make her smile again.

Mom smiles too. She says, "That's better. Now you can have fun with your new doll. But remember, sharing is caring. And caring is loving."

Ben and Mia are playing in the garden. They have a big pit that they dig with their shovels. They like to put things in the pit and pretend they are pirates or explorers.

"Look, I found a red pepper!" Mia says, holding up a shiny vegetable. "It is spicy, do you want to try?"

"No, thank you," Ben says, making a face. "I do not like spicy things. They make my mouth hurt."

"Then I will put it in the pit," Mia says, tossing the pepper into the hole. "Maybe it will grow into a pepper tree."

They keep digging and putting things in the pit. They find rocks, sticks, leaves, and a worm. They are having fun.

Suddenly, they hear a loud bark. It is their dog, Rex. He runs towards them, wagging his tail. He sees the pit and jumps in. He starts to dig and sniff.

"Hey, Rex, stop!" Ben says. "You are messing up our pit!"

But Rex does not listen. He finds the pepper and bites it. He makes a funny noise and spits it out. He shakes his head and runs out of the pit.

"Rex, are you okay?" Mia asks, petting him. "That pepper was spicy, you silly dog."

Rex licks her face and wags his tail. He is okay. He just learned a lesson.

Ben and Mia laugh. They hug Rex and go back to their pit. They have more things to put in it. They are happy.

But then, Max saw Lily's blue spoon and wanted it. He said, "Give me your blue spoon, Lily. It is nicer than my red spoon."

Lily said, "No, Max. This is my blue spoon. You have your red spoon. We can share, but we cannot take."

Max did not listen. He tried to grab Lily's blue spoon. Lily held on to her blue spoon. They pulled and pulled. The blue spoon flew out of their hands and sprang across the table. It landed in mom's soup bowl. Splash!

Mom was not happy. She said, "Lily and Max, what are you doing? You made a mess. You should not fight over spoons. You should be kind and polite. Now, say sorry to each other and to me."

Lily and Max felt bad. They said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Max. We will not fight over spoons again. We will share and be nice."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good. Now, let's clean up and finish our soup. And here, you can both have a blue spoon." She gave them each a new blue spoon from the drawer.

Lily and Max said, "Thank you, mom. We love you. And we love blue spoons." They hugged mom and ate their soup with their blue spoons. They were happy.

Lily was a smart girl who loved to read books. She had many books in her room, but her favorite one was about birds. She liked to look at the pictures of the birds and learn their names and sounds. She wished she could fly like a bird and see the world.

One day, she saw a big bird outside her window. It was black and had a red hat on its head. It was a chimney sweep, a bird that helps people clean their chimneys. Lily opened the window and said hello to the bird.

"Hello, little girl," the bird said. "Do you like birds?"

"Yes, I do," Lily said. "You are a chimney sweep, right? Can you fly very high?"

The bird nodded. "I can soar in the sky and see many things. Do you want to come with me?"

Lily was curious and excited. She wanted to soar with the bird and see what he saw. She asked her mom if she could go with the bird, and her mom said yes, but only for a little while. She gave Lily a coat and a scarf and told her to be careful.

Lily climbed on the bird's back and held on to his hat. The bird flapped his wings and soared into the air. Lily felt the wind in her face and the sun on her skin. She saw the roofs of the houses, the trees in the park, the cars on the road, and the people on the street. She saw other birds flying and singing. She felt happy and free.

The bird took her to different places and told her stories about them. He showed her a big clock, a tall bridge, a shiny river, and a colorful market. He taught her some words in his language, and she taught him some words in hers. They had fun and learned from each other.

After a while, the bird said it was time to go back. He thanked Lily for being his friend and said he hoped to see her again. He flew back to her window and let her down. Lily hugged the bird and thanked him for the adventure. She waved goodbye and went inside.

She told her mom everything she saw and heard. Her mom was proud of her and gave her a hug and a kiss. She said Lily was a smart and brave girl. Lily smiled and said she loved birds. She looked at her book and saw the picture of the chimney sweep. She felt a warm feeling in her heart. She hoped to soar with him again.

Tom is a hamster. He lives in a cage in the house of Sam. Sam is a boy who likes to play with Tom. Tom likes Sam, but he also likes to chew. He chews on his food, his toys, and sometimes his cage.

One day, Sam comes home from school. He is very happy. He has a new book with pictures of animals. He wants to show Tom the book. He opens the cage and picks up Tom. He says, "Look, Tom, this is a book. It has many animals. Can you see them?"

Tom looks at the book. He sees a dog, a cat, a bird, and a fish. He thinks they are all very nice. But he also sees something else. He sees the corner of the book. It looks very tasty. He opens his mouth and bites the book. He chews on the paper and makes a hole.

Sam is very sad. He says, "No, Tom, no! You cannot chew the book. The book is not for chewing. The book is for looking. You are a bad hamster. You ruined my book."

Tom is very sorry. He did not mean to make Sam sad. He did not know the book was not for chewing. He likes to chew. He thinks chewing is fun. He says, "I am sorry, Sam. I am not a bad hamster. I am a busy hamster. I like to chew. Can you give me something else to chew?"

Sam thinks for a moment. He loves Tom, even if he chews his book. He says, "OK, Tom, I forgive you. You are a busy hamster. But you cannot chew my book. You can chew this carrot. It is good for you. And it is good for your teeth. Here, take the carrot."

Tom takes the carrot. He is very happy. He chews on the carrot and makes a crunch. He says, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good boy. You are my friend. I like the carrot. It is yummy. And I like the book. It is pretty. But I will not chew the book. I will only look at the book. And I will only chew the carrot. And my toys. And sometimes my cage."

He gives the balls to Sara and Tom. The dog wags his tail. He looks sorry too.

"What have we done?" Ann says. "We were so mean to the poor string. It was our friend and we hurt it."

"Maybe we can find another string," Tom says, wiping his tears. "Let's go and search for one."

They leave their toys behind and go to search for a new string. They hope they will find one soon and have fun with it. They also hope the old string will forgive them and be happy.

"Hello, kids," the man said. "Do you want to try my stick? It makes you feel good."

Tom and Jen shook their heads. They did not want to try the stick. They knew it was bad for them.

"Go away, mister," Tom said. "We don't like your stick. It makes you sick."

The man laughed. He did not like Tom. He threw his stick in the ashtray. The ashtray was a metal thing that held the sticks. He took out another stick and lit it.

"Fine, fine," he said. "But you don't know what you're missing. This stick is my friend. It helps me when I'm sad."

Tom and Jen felt sorry for the man. They wondered why he was sad. They wanted to help him.

"Why are you sad, mister?" Jen asked. "Don't you have any friends?"

The man looked at Jen. He felt a tear in his eye. He did not have any friends. He had quit his job, his wife had left him, and his kids did not talk to him. He was lonely and gloomy.

When Lily finished cleaning her room, she went outside to play. She saw her little brother playing with his toys, but he was making a mess. Lily told him to stop and clean up his toys before they went inside. She learned that it's important to clean up after yourself and not make a mess for others to clean up.

The moral of the story is that it's important to clean up after yourself and measure things so you can understand them better.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to wander. They lived near a big harbor where many boats came and went. Some boats were small and some boats were big. Some boats had sails and some boats had engines. Tom and Lily liked to watch the boats and wonder where they went.

One day, they saw a very big boat with a lot of people on it. It had a big flag and a big name. Tom and Lily wanted to see it closer, so they wandered away from their mom and dad. They walked along the harbor until they reached the big boat.

"Wow, look at that boat!" Tom said. "It is so big and shiny!"

"Yes, and look at all the people!" Lily said. "They look happy and excited!"

They saw a man in a uniform standing near the boat. He had a hat and a whistle. Tom and Lily walked up to him and asked, "Hello, sir. What is this boat?"

The man smiled and said, "Hello, kids. This boat is called the Queen Mary. It is a famous boat that used to sail across the ocean. Now it is a museum and a hotel. People can visit it and learn about its history and see its rooms."

"Wow, that sounds fun!" Tom said. "Can we go on the boat?"

"Sorry, kids. You need a ticket to go on the boat. And you need to be with your parents. Where are your parents?" the man asked.

Tom and Lily looked around and realized they had wandered too far. They did not see their mom and dad anywhere. They felt scared and sad.

"We don't know where they are," Lily said. "We wandered away from them. We are sorry."

The man said, "Don't worry, kids. I will help you find them. Come with me. We will use my radio to call them. They must be looking for you."

Tom and Lily followed the man and hoped their mom and dad would hear them. They learned that wandering can be fun, but also dangerous. They decided to stay close to their mom and dad from now on. They still liked to watch the boats, but they did not wander away anymore.

Sue was so happy that her mom helped her. She was not embarrassed anymore. Sue went outside to play with her friends, and they all liked her pretty hair. Sue learned that it was okay to ask for help when she struggled with something. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the zoo with her mom. It was a wet day, but Mia was very excited. She put on her rain boots and her raincoat. At the zoo, Mia saw many animals. She saw big elephants, tall giraffes, and funny monkeys.

Mia and her mom walked around the zoo, looking at all the animals. They saw a big puddle and Mia jumped in it. "Splash!" went the water. Mia laughed and said, "Mom, I love the wet zoo!"

Then, Mia and her mom discovered a new animal. It was a small, cute, and furry creature. Mia asked her mom, "What is that?" Her mom said, "That is a baby panda. It is very special."

Mia loved the baby panda. She wanted to see it all day. She told her mom, "The zoo is the best place ever!" Mia and her mom had a great day at the wet zoo, and they went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady named Grandma Sue. She loved to eat ice-cream on hot days. One sunny day, Grandma Sue went to the park with her little dog, Max.

At the park, Grandma Sue bought a big ice-cream cone. Max looked at the ice-cream and wagged his tail. "Do you want some ice-cream too, Max?" asked Grandma Sue. Max barked happily, so Grandma Sue gave him a little ice-cream.

Max was so happy that he jumped around. But, oh no! The ice-cream fell on Grandma Sue's dress. "Don't worry, Max. I will wipe it off," she said with a smile. Grandma Sue wiped the ice-cream off her dress, and they both laughed.

After that, Grandma Sue and Max played in the park until the sun went down. They had a great day, and Max learned to be more careful with ice-cream. They went home with big smiles, ready for more fun days together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was reading a book with her mommy. Lily loved books and she loved to turn the pages. But suddenly, she saw a spider on the page and she panicked! 

"Oh no, Mommy! Spider!" Lily said, pointing at the book. 

"It's okay, Lily. The spider is just on the page. We can turn the page and it will go away," Mommy said, trying to calm her down. 

Lily took a deep breath and turned the page. The spider was gone and Lily felt relieved. "Thanks, Mommy. You always make me feel alert," Lily said with a smile. 

From then on, Lily wasn't afraid of spiders on the page anymore. She knew she could always turn the page and make them go away. And she was happy to continue reading her books with her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a small house. His name was Grandpa Joe. One day, his door broke and he couldn't fix it. He tried and tried, but it wouldn't work. So, he went to his neighbor, Timmy, who was playing outside.

"Timmy, can you help me fix my door?" Grandpa Joe asked.

Timmy replied, "I don't know how to fix doors, but my mommy is a lawyer. Maybe she can help!"

Grandpa Joe was confused. "What does a lawyer have to do with my door?"

Timmy explained, "My mommy helps people with problems. Maybe she can help fix your door problem!"

So, Grandpa Joe went to see Timmy's mommy, the lawyer. She listened to his problem and helped him fix his door. Grandpa Joe was so happy and thanked the lawyer and Timmy for their help. From that day on, Grandpa Joe knew that if he had a problem, he could always ask for help.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo who lived in the ocean. One day, Nemo went on an adventure with his friend Dory. They swam and swam until they found a big, shiny treasure chest. 

Dory said, "Let's open it and see what's inside!" 

Nemo replied, "Okay, but we have to be careful. We don't want to break it." 

They tried to open the chest but it was too tight. Nemo said, "I think we need help. Let's ask our other fish friends." 

Together, they all worked to open the chest and finally, they did it! Inside, they found lots of shiny treasures. Nemo said, "Wow, we finished our adventure and found treasure too!" 

Dory replied, "Yes, and we did it all together. That's what friends are for."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, she built a snowman with her friend Jack. 

Lily said, "Jack, look at our snowman. He looks so happy!" 

Jack replied, "Yes, but it's getting warmer outside. Our snowman might melt soon." 

Lily felt uncomfortable thinking about the snowman melting. She said, "We have to save him! How can we stop him from melting?" 

Jack thought for a moment and said, "I know! We can put him in my dad's automobile and take him to the North Pole where it's always cold." 

Lily was happy with the idea, and they carefully put the snowman in the automobile. They drove to the North Pole and found a spot where the snowman could stay. He didn't melt anymore and was happy to be in a cold place. Lily and Jack were happy too, knowing they saved their snowman friend.

So Lily skipped and skipped until she felt better. Her tooth still wiggled, but she wasn't scared anymore. She knew that growing up was a part of life and that everything would be okay.

His Dad was kind and gentle. And he was a very good fixer! He looked at the hockey and saw what was wrong. Then he fixed it with his tools. He worked very hard at it.

Soon the hockey was all fixed. The boy was so happy. He thanked his Dad for his help. He said his Dad was the best fixer in the world. That made his Dad smile.

The boy loved to play hockey again. He was happy to have it fixed. His Dad was happy too that he had helped his boy with his problem. He knew the boy would play his heart out now. And that was very special.

One day, a big dog came into the yard. The dog saw the blocks and wanted to play too. He ran and jumped and knocked down the towers and houses and bridges. Ben and Lily were sad. They cried and said, "Bad dog! Go away!"

The dog did not understand. He thought they wanted to play more. He barked and wagged his tail and ran around the blocks. He made more trouble.

Mom heard the noise and came outside. She saw the mess and the dog and the children. She said, "Oh no! What happened here?" She shooed the dog away and hugged Ben and Lily. She said, "Don't worry. We can restore your blocks. Let's work together and make them nice again."

Ben and Lily nodded and smiled. They dried their tears and picked up their blocks. They helped Mom to restore their towers and houses and bridges. They said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best." Mom said, "You are welcome, my loves. You are very good at building. And next time, we will close the gate so the dog can't come in." They all laughed and hugged and played some more.

One day, Lily saw a candle on the table. It was white and round and had a string on top. Lily wondered what it was for. She asked her mom, "Mom, what is this?"

Her mom smiled and said, "That is a candle, Lily. It is for making light and warmth. We can light it with a match, but only when I am with you. It can be dangerous if you touch it or play with it."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Can we light it now? I want to see it."

Her mom said, "Sure, Lily. Let me get a match and we can light it together. But first, let's load the toys into the box. We don't want them to be in the way."

Lily agreed and helped her mom load the toys into the box. Then they went to the table and her mom lit the candle with a match. Lily watched as the string burned and made a small flame. The flame was yellow and orange and danced on the candle. Lily thought it was very interesting. She said, "Wow, mom. The candle is so pretty. It makes light and warmth. I like it."

Her mom said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily. The candle is a special thing. It can make us feel cozy and happy. But we have to be careful with it and never leave it alone. Do you understand?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will never touch it or play with it. I will only look at it with you."

Her mom said, "Good, Lily. You are a very smart and helpful girl. I love you very much."

Lily said, "I love you too, mom. Thank you for showing me the candle. It is very interesting."

Sam and Tom were brothers who liked to work on their farm. They had many animals, but their favorite was a goat named Billy. Billy was very smart and funny, and he helped them with their chores. He could pull a cart, carry a basket, and even open gates with his horns.

One day, Sam and Tom had to go to the market to sell some eggs and cheese. They decided to take Billy with them, because he could carry some of the goods. They put a red scarf around his neck and a bell on his collar, and off they went.

On the way, they met a man who had a big hat and a long coat. He looked at Billy and said, "What a fine goat you have there! He must be very valuable. How much do you want for him?"

Sam and Tom were surprised. They did not want to sell Billy, he was their friend. They said, "No, thank you, sir. Billy is not for sale. He is part of our family."

The man smiled and said, "Oh, come on, don't be foolish. I will give you a lot of money for him. Look, I have a bag of gold coins here. You can buy many things with them. Think of all the toys and candy you can get. Just give me your goat, and the gold is yours."

Sam and Tom looked at the bag of gold. It was shiny and heavy. They thought of all the things they could buy with it. They felt tempted. They looked at Billy. He was wagging his tail and chewing some grass. He did not know what was going on.

They said to the man, "Well, maybe we can make a deal. But we have to ask Billy first. He is very smart, he can understand us. Billy, do you want to go with this man? He will give us a lot of gold for you."

Billy looked at them and said, "Baa!" He shook his head and ran away. He did not want to leave his friends. He knew the man was a bad man. He had seen him before, stealing from other people. He had a fake bag of gold, filled with rocks and dirt. He was a liar and a thief.

Sam and Tom realized they had been foolish. They had almost traded their loyal and clever goat for a worthless bag of gold. They felt ashamed and sorry. They ran after Billy and hugged him. They said, "Billy, we are so sorry. We love you. You are the best goat in the world. Please forgive us."

Billy forgave them. He was happy to be with them. He said, "Baa!" He licked their faces and wagged his tail. They continued their way to the market, and never listened to the bad man again. They learned their lesson. They knew that friendship was more important than money. And they knew that Billy was not just a goat, he was a hero.

"What happened here?" mom asked.

"Lily twisted the tracks and broke them!" Ben said.

"Sorry, kids, but you can't play with the train set anymore. You have to learn to share and cooperate. Maybe next time, you will be more careful and respectful of your toys and each other," mom said.

They brought some cups and spoons, and pretended they were shower heads and faucets. They crawled inside the tent and said, "We are in a shower! We are getting clean and wet!"

They had fun splashing and pouring water on each other, until Tommy had an idea. He saw a bottle of shampoo on the shelf, and thought it would make the game more real. He grabbed the bottle and squeezed some shampoo on Lily's head. "Look, Lily, I am washing your hair!" he said.

Lily was upset. She did not like shampoo in her eyes and mouth. It made her cry and cough. She pushed Tommy away and shouted, "Stop it, Tommy! That is not nice! That is not fun! That hurts!"

Tommy was sorry. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He thought she would like it. He said, "I am sorry, Lily. I was just acting. I wanted to make the game better. Please don't be upset."

Lily was still upset. She did not want to play with Tommy anymore. She crawled out of the tent and ran to their mom. She told her what Tommy did, and asked for a real shower.

Mom was not happy. She scolded Tommy for being careless and rude. She said, "Tommy, you should not use shampoo on Lily. That is not acting. That is dangerous. You could hurt her eyes and skin. You should apologize to Lily and help her clean up."

Tommy felt bad. He knew he was wrong. He said, "I am sorry, Mom. I am sorry, Lily. I will not do it again. I will help you."

Mom nodded. She said, "That is good, Tommy. I hope you learned your lesson. Now, come on, let's go to the bathroom and give Lily a real shower."

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room when they heard a loud boom outside. They ran to the window and saw a bright flash of lightning in the sky.

"Wow, what was that?" Ben asked.

"That was lightning. It is a big spark that comes from the clouds when they are angry," Sara explained.

"Why are the clouds angry?" Ben wondered.

"I don't know. Maybe they are fighting with each other, or maybe they are sad and crying," Sara guessed.

They watched the lightning for a while, then they heard another boom and saw another flash.

"Look, there is another one!" Ben pointed.

"Yes, and it is different from the first one. It is more curved and twisted," Sara observed.

"That is because lightning is flexible. It can change its shape and direction," Sara said.

"Flexible? What does that mean?" Ben asked.

"It means it can bend and stretch and move easily. Like this," Sara said, and she bent her arm and wiggled her fingers.

"Ooh, I see. I can be flexible too," Ben said, and he twisted his body and waved his legs.

They giggled and tried to make different flexible shapes with their limbs.

"Being flexible is fun. Maybe the lightning is having fun too," Ben said.

"Maybe. But it is also scary and dangerous. We should not go outside when there is lightning. We should stay inside and be safe," Sara said.

"OK. But can we still watch it from the window?" Ben asked.

"Sure. We can watch it and discuss it. Discuss means to talk about something and share our ideas," Sara said.

"OK. I like to discuss with you. You are smart and you know many things," Ben said.

"Thank you. I like to discuss with you too. You are curious and you ask good questions," Sara said.

They hugged each other and continued to watch and discuss the lightning until it stopped.

Once upon a time, a fat duck lived near a pond. The duck loved to show his big belly to all the animals. He would say, "Look at my big belly! I am the fattest duck in the world!"

One day, a small frog came to the pond. The fat duck said, "Hey frog, look at my big belly! I am so fat!" The frog was not happy. He said, "Being fat is not good. You should be healthy and strong."

But the fat duck did not listen. He kept showing his big belly to everyone. One day, a big storm came. The wind blew the fat duck far away from the pond. The fat duck could not fly back because he was too heavy.

The other animals missed the fat duck. They learned that it is important to be healthy and strong. The fat duck should have listened to the small frog.

Once upon a time, in a big blue sky, there was a little angel named Amy. Amy had a very important job to do. She had to hurry and find her friend, the sun, to tell him it was time to shine bright.

Amy flew fast through the sky, looking for the sun. As she flew, she saw a big cloud. The cloud was sad and cried big tears. "Why are you sad, Mr. Cloud?" Amy asked. The cloud said, "I lost my friend, the sun. I cannot find him anywhere."

Amy smiled and said, "Do not worry, Mr. Cloud. I am looking for the sun too. We can find him together!" So, Amy and the cloud hurried to find their friend. They looked high and low, and finally, they found the sun hiding behind a tall mountain.

"Sun, it is time to shine bright!" Amy said. The sun smiled and began to shine. The cloud stopped crying and became happy. Amy, the cloud, and the sun all played together in the big blue sky. And from that day on, they were the best of friends.

Tom listened to Mr. Hoot's words. He decided to play in the shade under a big tree. He felt cooler and his fur didn't feel hot anymore. Tom was happy he asked his question and learned something new. He played with his friends all day, making sure to stay in the shade when the sun was too hot.

"I have an idea," Tom said. "You push me and I will grab the branch. Then I will pull you up."

"OK," Lily said. She pushed Tom with all her strength. Tom reached the branch and held on. He smiled and said, "I did it! Now it's your turn."

But as he said that, he heard a loud crack. The branch was too weak and it broke. Tom fell to the ground with a thud. He cried out in pain.

"Lily, help me!" Tom shouted.

Lily ran to Tom and saw that he had a big bump on his head and a scratch on his arm. She felt sorry for him and hugged him.

"Are you OK, Tom?" Lily asked.

"It hurts, Lily. It hurts a lot," Tom said.

"We're sorry, Mom. We wanted to climb the tree and see the birds and the sky. Tom had an idea and I pushed him. But the branch broke and he fell," Lily said.

Mom sighed and said, "I know you were curious and wanted to have fun. But you should have listened to me. I know what is safe and what is not. It deserves your care and kindness, not your push and break."

Tom and Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom. We love you."

"Why not?" Mia asks.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to joke a lot. They always made funny faces and noises to make each other laugh. One day, their mom gave them a bowl of prunes to eat. Prunes were brown and wrinkly and sweet, but Lily and Ben did not like them very much.

"Yuck, these look like old people's faces," Lily said, holding a prune in front of her nose.

"Or like monkey butts," Ben said, making a monkey sound.

They giggled and threw the prunes at each other, pretending they were bombs. Their mom did not see them, because she was busy in the kitchen.

Soon, they ran out of prunes and looked for something else to joke with. They saw a bottle of lemon juice on the table. They had an idea.

"Let's drink some lemon juice and make sour faces," Lily said.

"OK, but don't tell mom," Ben said.

They opened the bottle and took a big sip each. They expected to make funny faces, but they did not. Instead, they felt a sharp pain in their mouths and throats. The lemon juice was too sour and strong for them. They coughed and spit out the juice, tears in their eyes.

"Ow, ow, ow, that hurts!" Lily cried.

"Me too, me too, it burns!" Ben cried.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the bottle of lemon juice and the spilled prunes on the floor. She understood what they had done.

"Oh, you silly kids, you should not joke with lemon juice. It is not for drinking, it is for cooking. It can hurt your mouth and make you sick," she said.

She took them to the bathroom and rinsed their mouths with water. She checked their tongues and saw they were pale and swollen.

"You need to drink some milk and eat some bread to make your tongues feel better," she said.

She gave them some milk and bread and hugged them. She was not angry, but she was worried.

"I love you, but please, no more jokes with lemon juice, OK?" she said.

Lily and Ben nodded and said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They decided to joke with something else next time. Maybe with carrots or bananas. But not with lemon juice. Never again.

There was a big land with many people. The people had different colors, shapes and sounds. Some people were mean to other people who were not like them. They fought and hurt each other. They made the land unhappy.

One day, a good king came to the land. He wanted to make the land happy again. He said to the people, "You are all my children. You are all beautiful and special. You can be friends and help each other. You can make the land happy again. Let us unite and be one big family."

Some people liked the king's words. They smiled and hugged each other. They said, "Yes, we want to be friends. We want to be happy. We want to unite and be one big family." They followed the king and made the land happy.

But some people did not like the king's words. They frowned and pushed each other. They said, "No, we do not want to be friends. We do not want to be happy. We do not want to unite and be one big family." They did not follow the king and made the land unhappy.

The king was sad. He said to the people, "Why do you not want to be friends? Why do you not want to be happy? Why do you not want to unite and be one big family? Do you not see that you are hurting yourselves and the land?"

The people said, "We do not like people who are not like us. They make us uncomfortable. They are bad and wrong. We are good and right. We do not need them. We do not need you."

The king was very sad. He said, "You are making a big mistake. You are not good and right. You are bad and wrong. You are making yourselves and the land unhappy. You need each other. You need me. You need love."

The people did not listen to the king. They kept fighting and hurting each other. They made the land very unhappy. The king cried and left the land. He hoped that one day, the people would learn to love and unite.

The moral of the story is: We should love and respect people who are different from us. We should unite and be one big family. We should make ourselves and the land happy.

Tommy loved his motorcycle toy. He played with it every day. He made it go fast and loud. He pretended he was a big rider.

One day, his mom said, "Tommy, we have to go to grandma's house. Dress up nicely, please." Tommy did not want to dress up. He wanted to wear his motorcycle shirt and jeans. He said, "No, mom. I want to play with my motorcycle."

Mom was frustrated. She said, "Tommy, you have to dress up. Grandma likes to see you in nice clothes. It is polite and kind. You can play with your motorcycle later." Tommy did not listen. He ran away with his motorcycle.

Mom had to chase him. She caught him and took his motorcycle. She said, "Tommy, you are being naughty. You have to dress up now. Or you will not get your motorcycle back." Tommy was sad and angry. He cried and kicked.

Mom was calm. She said, "Tommy, I know you love your motorcycle. But you have to learn to follow the rules. Sometimes you have to do things you don't like. It is good for you and others. If you dress up nicely, grandma will be happy. And I will be proud of you. And you will get your motorcycle back. Do you understand?"

Tommy thought for a moment. He did not want to make mom and grandma sad. He wanted to be a good boy. He said, "OK, mom. I will dress up. But can I bring my motorcycle with me?" Mom smiled. She said, "Yes, you can. But you have to keep it in your bag. And you have to play with it quietly. Can you do that?" Tommy nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. I can do that."

Mom hugged him. She said, "Thank you, Tommy. You are a smart and kind boy. I love you." Tommy hugged her back. He said, "I love you too, mom. And I love grandma. And I love my motorcycle."

The moral value of the story is: Sometimes we have to do things we don't like for the sake of others. It is important to respect and obey our parents and elders. It is also important to love and appreciate what we have.

One day, a fox was very hungry. He looked for food in the forest, but he could not find any. He saw a big tree with red fruits. He wanted to eat them, but they were too high. He tried to jump, but he could not reach them.

He saw a bird on a branch. The bird had a fruit in her beak. The fox said, "Hello, bird. Can you give me some of your fruit? I am very hungry."

The bird said, "No, fox. This is my fruit. I worked hard to get it. Go find your own food."

The fox said, "Please, bird. Just a little bit. I will be very grateful."

The bird said, "Fine, fox. I will share with you. But you have to split the fruit with me. Half for you, half for me."

The fox said, "Thank you, bird. You are very kind. How do we split the fruit?"

The bird said, "I will drop the fruit on the ground. Then you can split it with your teeth. But be careful, the fruit has a big seed inside. Do not eat the seed. It is hard and bitter."

The fox said, "OK, bird. I will be careful. Drop the fruit now."

The bird dropped the fruit on the ground. The fox ran to get it. He split the fruit with his teeth. He saw the seed inside. He thought, "The seed is big and shiny. Maybe it is tasty. Maybe the bird is lying to me. Maybe she wants the seed for herself. I will eat the seed and the fruit. Then I will have more food."

He ate the seed and the fruit. But the seed was not tasty. It was hard and bitter. It hurt his mouth and his stomach. He felt sick and sorry. He wished he had listened to the bird.

The bird saw the fox eat the seed. She said, "Fox, you are greedy and foolish. You did not listen to me. You did not share with me. You ate the seed and the fruit. Now you are sick and sorry. You should have been grateful and honest."

The fox learned a lesson. He learned to be grateful and honest. He learned to share and listen. He said, "I am sorry, bird. You were right. I was wrong. I will not do it again. Can you forgive me?"

The bird said, "Yes, fox. I forgive you. But next time, be grateful and honest. Share and listen. Then you will be happy and healthy."

The end.

One day, Lila saw a rabbit hopping near a bush. She ran after it, hoping to make friends. But the rabbit was scared and ran away. Lila followed it until they reached a big road. There were many loud cars and trucks on the road. Lila stopped and waited for the rabbit to cross.

"Please, don't run away!" Lila called. "I just want to play with you!"

The rabbit looked at Lila with wide eyes. "You want to play with me? But you are a fox! You will eat me!"

Lila shook her head. "No, I won't eat you. I am not hungry. I am lonely. I have no friends. Can you be my friend?"

The rabbit thought for a moment. He felt sorry for Lila. He knew what it was like to be lonely. He had lost his family to a hunter. He decided to give Lila a chance.

"Okay, I will be your friend. But we have to be careful. There are hunters in the forest. And we have to separate when the sun goes down. You have to go back to your mother, and I have to go back to my burrow."

Lila nodded. She was happy to have a friend. She crossed the road with the rabbit and they played in the grass. They chased each other, rolled in the leaves, and shared some berries. They had fun until the sky turned dark. Then they said goodbye and promised to meet again the next day.

She hugged Lila and said, "I am proud of you, my little fox. You have a big heart. But you also have to be smart. Remember, not all animals are friendly. And hunters are dangerous. Always be careful and stay close to me."

Lila nodded. She understood. She loved her mother and she loved her friend. She was not lonely anymore. She fell asleep with a smile on her face.

The little girl was amazed by the squirrel's unusual tail and wanted to take a picture of him. She went home to get her camera and came back to the park. When she returned, she saw a big dog chasing the squirrel. The squirrel tried to run away, but he tripped and fell. The little girl tried to help the squirrel, but it was too late. The dog had caught the squirrel and hurt him badly.

The little girl was very sad because she lost her new friend. She wished she could have done something to save the squirrel. She remembered the squirrel's unusual rainbow tail and realized that it was the last thing he showed her before he died. She decided to take a picture of the tail and keep it as a memory of her unusual friend.

Lisa liked to dream. Every night, she closed her eyes and saw many things. She saw big mountains, green forests, blue seas and colorful birds. She liked to dream of places she wanted to go.

One night, she dreamed of a zoo. She saw many animals there. She saw lions, elephants, giraffes and pandas. She liked them all, but she liked one animal the most. It was a monkey.

The monkey was funny and smart. It jumped and swung on the trees. It made funny faces and noises. It played with other monkeys and ate bananas. Lisa wanted to play with the monkey. She said, "Hello, monkey. Can I be your friend?"

The monkey looked at Lisa and smiled. It said, "Hello, Lisa. You can be my friend. Do you want to play with me?"

Lisa was happy. She said, "Yes, I want to play with you. What can we do?"

The monkey said, "We can do many things. We can jump and swing on the trees. We can make funny faces and noises. We can eat bananas. We can have fun."

Lisa and the monkey played together. They had fun. They laughed and hugged. They were happy.

But not everyone was happy. There was another animal in the zoo. It was a crocodile. The crocodile was big and scary. It had sharp teeth and a long tail. It lived in a pond. It did not like to play. It liked to sleep and eat.

The crocodile saw Lisa and the monkey. It was envious. It wanted to have a friend too. It wanted to have fun too. It said, "Why do they have a friend and I don't? Why do they have fun and I don't? I want to have a friend and fun too."

The crocodile decided to do something bad. It sneaked out of the pond. It crawled towards Lisa and the monkey. It opened its mouth. It wanted to bite them.

But Lisa and the monkey saw the crocodile. They were scared. They screamed. They ran away. They climbed on a high tree. They were safe.

The crocodile was angry. It could not reach them. It growled. It snapped. It splashed. It was alone.

Lisa and the monkey looked at the crocodile. They felt sorry for it. They said, "Why are you so mean, crocodile? Why do you want to hurt us? We don't want to hurt you. We want to be your friend. We want to have fun with you."

The crocodile was surprised. It did not expect them to say that. It felt ashamed. It said, "I'm sorry, Lisa and monkey. I was mean because I was envious. I was envious because I was lonely. I was lonely because I had no friend. I had no friend because I was mean. It was a bad circle."

Lisa and the monkey said, "It's okay, crocodile. We forgive you. You can break the bad circle. You can be nice. You can be our friend. You can have fun with us."

The crocodile said, "Really? You mean it? You want to be my friend?"

Lisa and the monkey said, "Yes, we mean it. We want to be your friend."

The crocodile said, "Thank you, Lisa and monkey. You are very kind. I want to be your friend too. I want to have fun with you too."

Lisa and the monkey said, "You're welcome, crocodile. Come on, let's play together."

The crocodile said, "Okay, let's play together."

Lisa and the monkey and the crocodile played together. They had fun. They laughed and hugged. They were happy.

Lisa woke up. She smiled. She liked her dream. She learned something. She learned that everyone can be a friend. She learned that everyone can have fun. She learned that being nice is better than being envious. She was happy.

She looked around the park for Ben. She saw a big tree, a slide, a swing, and a bench. Where could Ben be? She thought he might be behind the tree, so she ran to it and peeked. But there was no Ben. She heard a giggle from somewhere else. She followed the sound and saw the slide. She climbed up the ladder and looked down the slide. But there was no Ben. She heard another giggle from somewhere else. She slid down the slide and ran to the swing. She pushed the swing and looked behind it. But there was no Ben. She heard a louder giggle from somewhere else. She was getting tired and frustrated. Where was Ben?

But when she pulled the legs, she realized they were not Ben's. They were a stranger's. A big, scary stranger with a mean face and a dirty coat. He yelled at Sara, "Hey, what are you doing? Let go of me!"

"I know what to do, Ben. I will burn the ants. Then they will leave us alone," Lily said. She picked up the stick. She ran to the house. She saw a candle on the table. She lit the stick with the candle. She ran back to the garden.

"Look, Ben, I have fire. I will burn the ants," Lily said. She waved the stick in the air. She went to the ant hill. She put the stick on the ant hill.

But the ants did not like the fire. They got angry. They came out of the ant hill. They attacked Lily and Ben. They bit them all over.

"Ow, ow, ow! The ants are biting us!" Lily and Ben said. They dropped the stick. They ran away from the ant hill. They ran to the house. They cried for their mom.

Mom heard them crying. She came out of the house. She saw them covered in bites. She saw the stick on the ant hill. She saw the smoke and the fire.

"What did you do, Lily and Ben?" Mom asked. She was mad. She put out the fire. She took Lily and Ben inside. She put some cream on their bites. She hugged them.

"I'm sorry, Mom. We wanted to see the ants. But they bit us. So we tried to burn them. But they bit us more," Lily and Ben said.

Mom sighed. She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Ben, you should not play with fire. Fire is dangerous. Fire can hurt you and the ants. Fire can burn the house and the garden. Fire has a high price. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We are sorry. We will not play with fire again. We will be nice to the ants."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Lily and Ben. I love you. Now go and rest. And next time, be careful and curious, but not foolish."

Lily was a spoiled girl who always wanted more toys. She had a big room full of dolls, cars, books and puzzles, but she was never happy. She always asked her mom and dad for new things, and cried if they said no.

One day, Lily saw a shiny penny on the street. She picked it up and put it in her pocket. She thought it was very pretty and wanted to keep it. She ran home and showed it to her mom.

"Look, mom, I found a penny!" she said.

"That's nice, dear, but you know you have to share it with your brother, right?" her mom said.

Lily frowned. She did not like to share anything with her brother Tom. He was younger than her and always broke her toys. She shook her head and said, "No, mom, it's mine! I found it, so I keep it!"

Her mom sighed. She knew Lily was being selfish and rude, but she did not want to argue with her. She hoped Lily would learn to be more generous and kind someday.

She said, "Okay, Lily, you can keep the penny, but you have to answer one question first. Do you know what you can buy with a penny?"

Lily thought for a moment. She had seen her mom and dad use money to buy things at the store, but she did not know how much things cost. She guessed a penny was a lot of money, because it was shiny and round.

She said, "I can buy anything I want with a penny! I can buy a new doll, or a new car, or a new book, or a new puzzle!"

Her mom smiled sadly. She knew Lily was wrong, but she did not want to hurt her feelings. She said, "Well, Lily, you can try, but I don't think you will find anything that costs a penny. Most things are much more expensive than that. A penny is not worth much, but it can still make someone happy. Do you know who?"

Lily thought again. She did not know who would be happy with a penny. She only cared about herself and her toys. She shrugged and said, "I don't know, mom. Who?"

Her mom said, "Someone who has nothing, Lily. Someone who is poor and hungry and cold. Someone who would be grateful for a penny, because it could help them buy some bread, or some milk, or some clothes. Someone who would say thank you and smile, because you gave them something they needed. Someone like that, Lily, would be happy with a penny. Don't you think?"

Lily was quiet. She did not know what to say. She looked at the penny in her hand, and then at her mom's face. She felt something in her chest, something she did not feel very often. She felt sorry for the people who had nothing, and she felt ashamed of herself for being so spoiled. She wondered what it would be like to give the penny to someone who needed it more than her.

She said, "Mom, I think I know what to do with the penny. Can we go to the store and find someone who has nothing?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "Yes, Lily, we can. I'm proud of you, my sweet girl. You have a big heart, and you can make a difference. Come on, let's go."

Lily smiled and held her mom's hand. She felt happy, happier than she ever felt with her toys. She learned a lesson that day, a lesson that a penny can teach. She learned to be kind, and to share, and to care. She learned that a penny is not just a shiny thing, but a gift of love.

But Sara and Tom did not get tired. They played with the train all night long. They did not yawn, they did not close their eyes, they did not rest. They only played with the train.

The next morning, Sara and Tom felt very bad. They had a headache, they had a sore throat, they had a runny nose. They did not want to eat, they did not want to play, they did not want to do anything. They only wanted to sleep.

Mom came to their room and saw them in their bed. She felt sorry for them. She said, "Sara and Tom, you are sick. You played with the train too much and did not sleep. That was not a good idea. Sleep is important for your health and happiness. Next time, you should listen to me and go to bed on time."

Sara and Tom nodded. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were wrong. We will listen to you next time. We will sleep when you tell us to sleep. We will wash our hair with shampoo and brush our teeth. We will not play with the train all night long."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "I love you, Sara and Tom. I hope you feel better soon. And I hope you learned your lesson. Sleep is good for you. And so is shampoo."

The end.

One day, a fish named Finn saw a shark swimming near his home. The shark was big and had many teeth, but Finn thought he was attractive. He wanted to be friends with the shark, so he swam closer and said, "Hello, shark. You are very attractive. Do you want to play with me?"

The shark smiled and said, "Hello, fish. You are very tasty. I mean, friendly. Yes, I want to play with you. Follow me to my cave, where we can have fun."

Finn was happy and followed the shark, but he did not notice that the shark was licking his lips. He also did not see his friend, Sally, a starfish, who was watching them. Sally was worried and said, "Finn, don't go with the shark. He is not nice. He is hungry. He will eat you!"

But Finn did not hear her. He was too excited to play with the shark. He swam into the cave, where it was dark and cold. He said, "Shark, where are you? I can't see you."

The shark said, "I'm right here, fish. And I'm ready to play. My favorite game is bite and chew. And you are the prize."

Then, the shark opened his mouth and tried to bite Finn. But Finn was quick and dodged the shark. He swam out of the cave and said, "Shark, you are not nice. You are mean. You lied to me. You wanted to eat me. You are not my friend."

The shark said, "Fish, come back. I was just joking. I don't want to eat you. I want to be your friend."

But Finn did not believe him. He swam away as fast as he could. He found Sally and said, "Sally, you were right. The shark was not nice. He was hungry. He tried to eat me. Thank you for warning me."

Sally said, "You're welcome, Finn. I'm glad you are safe. You should be careful who you trust. Not everyone who is attractive is nice. And not everyone who is nice is attractive. The most important thing is to be kind and honest."

Finn said, "You are right, Sally. You are very wise. And you are my true friend."

The end.

Tom lied and said, "No, Mia. I don't know where it is. Maybe you lost it or someone else took it."

Tom felt guilty and ashamed. He knew he had done a bad thing. He wanted to give the star block back to Mia, but he was afraid she would be angry and not be his friend anymore. He kept the star block in his pocket and said nothing.

The next day, Tom and Mia went to play with blocks again. But they were not enthusiastic and happy like before. They were quiet and sad. They did not talk to each other or share their blocks. They felt lonely and unhappy.

A teacher saw them and asked, "What is wrong, Tom and Mia? Why are you not playing with your blocks? You used to have so much fun together."

Tom and Mia did not answer. They looked at the ground and felt sorry.

The teacher said, "You know, blocks are fun to play with, but they are not more important than friendship. Friendship is a precious gift that you should cherish and respect. If you have a problem with your friend, you should talk to them and try to solve it. If you did something wrong, you should apologize and try to make it right. If you are honest and kind, you can keep your friendship and be happy again."

Tom and Mia listened to the teacher and realized he was right. They looked at each other and felt sorry. Tom took out the star block from his pocket and gave it back to Mia. He said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I took your star block yesterday. I was selfish and greedy. I lied to you and hurt you. I'm very sorry. Can you forgive me?"

Mia took the star block and hugged it. She said, "Thank you, Tom. I'm glad you gave it back to me. I was sad and angry when I lost it. I missed you and our friendship. I forgive you. Can we be friends again?"

Tom and Mia smiled and nodded. They hugged and said, "Yes, we can be friends again. We are sorry for what we did. We learned our lesson. We will not take or lie again. We will share and be kind. We will keep our friendship and be happy again."

They played with their blocks again. They were enthusiastic and happy like before. They talked and shared and helped each other. They felt happy and grateful.

The teacher watched them and smiled. He was proud of them. He said, "Well done, Tom and Mia. You made a good choice. You showed courage and honesty. You restored your friendship. You are good friends and good students. I hope you will always remember this lesson and keep it in your hearts."

The end.

Luna nodded and said, "Yes, we can be friends. Thank you, Max."

The moral of the story is: Curiosity is good, but safety is important. Do not wander in places where you could get hurt. Listen to your parents or guardians. Be kind to others and they will be kind to you.

After a while, the little girl said goodbye to the old man and left the garden. She looked back and saw the old man waving at her. She waved back and said, "Bye-bye, old man!" The old man smiled and said, "Goodbye, little girl. Come back soon." The little girl smiled and continued on her way, happy with the sight of her beautiful flower.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with blocks and build tall towers. One day, he tried to build a tower that was as tall as the sky. But every time he tried, it fell down to zero.

Timmy was sad and didn't want to build anymore. His friend, Sally, saw him and asked what was wrong. Timmy told her about his tower that kept falling down to zero. Sally said, "Don't worry, Timmy. Sometimes things don't work out the way we want them to. But that doesn't mean we should give up. We just need to find a more reliable way to build our tower."

Timmy thought about what Sally said and decided to try again. This time, he built his tower slowly and carefully. And it worked! His tower was tall and strong, and it didn't fall down to zero. Timmy was happy and proud of what he had built.

The moral of the story is that even when things don't go the way we want them to, we should never give up. We just need to find a more reliable way to build our dreams.

The squirrel smiled too. It tossed the peanut to Tom.

"Of course, boy," it said. "You can be my friend. I am lonely too. Maybe we can share more peanuts and stories."

Lila was a lonely girl. She had no friends to play with. She lived in a big house with her mom and dad, but they were always busy. Lila liked to run around the house and look for things to do. She liked to run up and down the stairs, run in and out of the rooms, and run in the garden.

One day, Lila found a lamp in the attic. It was old and dusty, but it had a pretty shape and a shiny knob. Lila wondered what would happen if she turned the knob. She ran down the stairs with the lamp in her arms. She wanted to show it to her mom and dad.

But when she got to the living room, she saw that her mom and dad were not there. They had gone out to work. Lila felt sad and angry. She wanted someone to talk to. She wanted someone to play with. She wanted someone to see her lamp.

She put the lamp on the table and turned the knob. Nothing happened. The lamp did not light up. Lila turned the knob again and again, but still nothing happened. She started to cry. She felt very lonely.

Then, she heard a voice. It came from the lamp. It said, "Hello, little girl. Why are you crying?"

Lila was surprised and scared. She looked at the lamp and saw a face. It was a friendly face, with a big smile and a long beard. It was a genie.

"Who are you?" Lila asked.

"I am a genie," the voice said. "I live in the lamp. You turned the knob and set me free. Now I can grant you three wishes. What do you wish for?"

Lila thought for a moment. She had many wishes, but she knew what she wanted most. She said, "I wish for a friend. A friend who will play with me and talk to me and see my lamp."

The genie nodded. He said, "Your wish is my command. Close your eyes and count to three."

Lila did as he said. She closed her eyes and counted, "One, two, three."

When she opened her eyes, she saw a boy standing next to her. He was about her age, with brown hair and blue eyes. He smiled at her and said, "Hi, I'm Leo. Do you want to be my friend?"

Lila smiled back. She felt happy and excited. She said, "Yes, I do. I'm Lila. Do you want to see my lamp?"

Leo nodded. He said, "Yes, I do. It looks very cool. Can I hold it?"

Lila handed him the lamp. She said, "Sure, you can. But be careful. There's a genie inside."

Leo looked at the lamp and said, "Wow, really? That's awesome. Can I talk to him?"

Lila said, "Yes, you can. But remember, he can only grant three wishes. I already used one. So we have two left. What do you wish for?"

Leo thought for a moment. He said, "I wish for a cake. A big, yummy cake. With chocolate and sprinkles and candles."

Lila said, "That sounds good. Me too. Let's wish for a cake together."

They both said, "We wish for a cake."

The genie said, "Your wish is my command. Close your eyes and count to three."

They did as he said. They closed their eyes and counted, "One, two, three."

When they opened their eyes, they saw a cake on the table. It was big and yummy. It had chocolate and sprinkles and candles. It had a sign that said, "Happy Friendship Day, Lila and Leo."

They clapped their hands and cheered. They said, "Thank you, genie. Thank you, lamp. Thank you, cake."

They cut the cake and ate it. They shared it with the genie, who came out of the lamp and joined them. They laughed and talked and played. They had a lot of fun.

They were not lonely anymore. They were happy. They were friends.

"No, Anna is mine. You can't have her," Lily said.

"But you have Rosie. Can we trade?" Mia asked.

"No, I want both. Rosie is better than Anna. Go away," Lily said.

Mia felt hurt and angry. She tried to take Rosie back, but Lily held her tight. They started to pull and tug on Rosie, making her cry. Mia's mom and Lily's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

"What's going on here?" Mia's mom asked.

"Lily took my doll and won't give her back. She's mean," Mia said.

"Lily, is that true? Why did you take Mia's doll?" Lily's mom asked.

"Because I like her. She's pretty and has wisdom. Anna is boring and ugly. I don't want her anymore," Lily said.

Lily's mom was shocked and disappointed. She took Anna from Lily and gave her to Mia. She took Rosie from Lily and gave her back to Mia too.

"Lily, that was very wrong and rude of you. You can't take things that don't belong to you. You can't be envious of what others have. You should be grateful for what you have. Anna is a lovely doll and a good friend. She loves you and you should love her too. You hurt Mia's feelings and Rosie's feelings. You need to say sorry and learn to share," Lily's mom said.

Lily didn't want to say sorry. She didn't want to share. She wanted to have Rosie. She started to cry and scream. She threw a tantrum. She kicked and hit her mom. She said bad words. She made a big mess.

Lily's mom was very sad and angry. She picked up Lily and took her home. She put her in her room and locked the door. She said Lily had to stay there until she calmed down and said sorry. She said Lily couldn't play with any dolls or toys until she learned her lesson.

Lily was alone in her room. She had no dolls, no toys, no fun. She had no friends, no love, no wisdom. She only had herself and her envy. She felt very unhappy and sorry. But it was too late. She had lost everything. The end.

Tom is a fisherman. He likes to catch fish in the lake. He has a boat and a net and a hat. He goes to the lake every morning.

One day, Tom is very sleepy. He did not sleep well at night. He yawns and rubs his eyes. He gets on his boat and sails to the middle of the lake. He throws his net into the water and waits for the fish.

But Tom is so sleepy that he falls asleep on his boat. He does not hear the fish splashing in his net. He does not hear the wind blowing his hat away. He does not hear the birds singing in the sky. He only hears his own snoring.

"Tom, Tom, wake up!" a voice calls. It is his friend Sam, another fisherman. He sees Tom sleeping on his boat and laughs. He sails his boat next to Tom's boat and shakes him gently.

"Tom, you are missing all the fish!" Sam says. "Look at your net, it is full of fish! And look at your hat, it is gone! And look at the sun, it is high in the sky! It is time to go home!"

Tom opens his eyes and blinks. He sees Sam and his net and his hat and the sun. He feels silly and embarrassed. He smiles and says, "Sorry, Sam, I was very sleepy. Thank you for waking me up. Let's go home and share the fish."

Sam nods and helps Tom pull his net into his boat. They sail back to the shore and unload their fish. They are happy and hungry. They cook some fish and eat them together. They are not sleepy anymore. They are friends.

One day, Lily saw a big bag of potatoes in the kitchen. She wanted to play with them, but her mom said no. She said they were for dinner and Lily had to wait. Lily was sad and angry. She wanted to play with the potatoes now.

She waited until her mom was busy in another room. Then she sneaked into the kitchen and grabbed a potato. She ran to her room and closed the door. She smiled and hugged the potato. She named it Bob and started to talk to it.

"Hi, Bob. You are my best friend. Do you want to play with me?" she asked.

The potato did not answer. It was quiet and still. Lily felt bored. She tried to make Bob talk by poking him, shaking him, and tickling him. But Bob did not talk. He did not laugh. He did not move. He was just a potato.

Lily sighed. She realized that Bob was not a real friend. He was not fun. He was not alive. He was food. She felt sorry for taking him from the kitchen. She wondered if her mom would be mad at her. She wondered if she would have any potatoes for dinner.

She decided to take Bob back to the kitchen and say sorry to her mom. She opened the door and walked to the kitchen. She saw her mom looking for something in the bag of potatoes.

"Mom, I have something to tell you," she said.

"What is it, Lily?" her mom asked.

Lily showed her the potato and said, "I took this potato from the bag. I wanted to play with him, but he was not a good friend. He was quiet and boring. I'm sorry, mom. Can I put him back?"

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Thank you for being honest, Lily. I'm glad you realized that potatoes are not toys. They are food. We need them to make a yummy dinner. You can put him back in the bag, and then you can help me wash and peel some more. How does that sound?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "That sounds good, mom. I'm sorry for being naughty. I love you, mom. And I love potatoes."

The moral value of the story is: honesty is the best policy, and food is not for playing.

They ran to him and said, "Sorry! Sorry! Sorry! Are you okay? Do you need help?"

The mail man looked at them. He saw their scared faces. He saw their red and blue shovels. He realized what happened. He was not angry. He was kind.

He said, "It's okay. It was an accident. I'm okay. You don't need to panic. Thank you for caring."

He got up and dusted himself off. He picked up the bag of mail. He smiled at Lily and Tom. He said, "Here, I have something for you. It's a postcard from your grandma. She says she loves you and misses you."

He gave them the postcard. Lily and Tom were happy. They thanked the mail man. They said, "We love you and miss you too, grandma. And we love the mail man. He is nice."

The mail man waved at them and got back in the truck. He drove away. Lily and Tom ran to their mom and showed her the postcard. They told her what happened. They said, "We learned a new word today. Panic. But we don't like it. We like mail better."

"I don't know, Tom," Lily said. "Maybe it was living in the volcano."

"Maybe it was angry that we broke its home," Tom said.

"Maybe it wants to bite us," Lily said.

They hugged each other and hoped the spider would go away. They wished they had never found the volcano. They decided to play something else next time.
