Tommy thought for a moment. He liked butter and jam. He said, "Both, please!"

Mommy nodded and said, "Okay, both. But not too much, okay? Too much butter and jam is not good for you."

She put butter and jam on the toast and gave it to Tommy. Tommy took a big bite and said, "Yum!"

But then he felt something strange. The toast was not hot. It was cool. He did not like cool toast. He wanted hot toast. He spit out the bite and said, "Blech!"

Mommy looked at him and said, "What's wrong, Tommy? Don't you like the toast?"

Tommy frowned and said, "No, Mommy. The toast is cool. I want hot toast."

Mommy felt the toast and said, "Oh, I'm sorry, Tommy. The toast is cool. I made it too early. Do you want me to make you another toast?"

Tommy nodded and said, "Yes, please. Hot toast, please!"

Mommy said, "Okay, Tommy. I'll make you another toast. But you have to wait a little bit, okay? It takes time to make toast."

Tommy said, "Okay, Mommy. I'll wait. But not too long, okay? I'm hungry."

Mommy said, "Okay, Tommy. Not too long. I love you."

Tommy said, "I love you too, Mommy." He gave her a hug and waited for his hot toast.

Sara and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. Sara liked the animals, but Ben was bored. He wanted to see something else.

"Can we go to the fish house?" Ben asked. "I want to see the octopus."

"Okay, Ben," Mom said. "But we have to hurry. The zoo will close soon."

They walked to the fish house, where there were tanks with different kinds of fish. Ben ran to the biggest tank, where the octopus was. He pressed his nose against the glass and looked at the octopus. The octopus was big and purple, with eight long arms. It moved slowly in the water.

"Wow, look at the octopus!" Ben said. "It is so cool. I wish I could touch it."

Sara came to the tank and looked at the octopus too. She did not think it was cool. She thought it was ugly and scary. She did not like its arms, or its eyes, or its mouth.

"Yuck, I don't like the octopus," Sara said. "It is so gross. I want to go away."

Ben frowned at Sara. He did not like that she did not like the octopus. He wanted her to like it too.

"No, the octopus is not gross," Ben said. "It is amazing. You are silly. You don't know anything."

Sara frowned back at Ben. She did not like that he called her silly. She wanted him to respect her opinion.

"No, you are silly," Sara said. "You don't know anything. The octopus is weak. It can't do anything. It just sits in the water."

Ben got angry at Sara. He wanted to prove her wrong. He wanted to show her that the octopus was not weak. He had an idea.

"Watch this," Ben said. He climbed on the edge of the tank and reached his hand inside. He tried to touch the octopus.

Sara gasped. She knew that was a bad idea. She tried to stop Ben.

"Ben, no!" Sara said. "Don't do that! You will get hurt!"

But it was too late. The octopus saw Ben's hand and grabbed it with one of its arms. It pulled Ben into the water. Ben screamed. Sara screamed. Mom and Dad screamed. The zookeeper ran to the tank and tried to help Ben. But the octopus was strong. It did not let go of Ben. It dragged him deeper into the water. Ben could not breathe. He felt dizzy. He closed his eyes.

Mom looked at the price tag. It was too much money. She shook her head.

Lily felt sad. She wanted the bear so much. She raised her hand and touched the bear's fur. It was soft and warm.

Ben and Lily are squirrels. They like to play in the park and find nuts. Nuts are important for squirrels. They need nuts to eat and to store for winter.

One day, they see a big nut on a tree. It is shiny and brown and looks very yummy. They both want the nut.

"I saw it first!" says Ben.

"No, I saw it first!" says Lily.

They start to fight over the nut. They push and pull and shout. They do not share.

A bird sees them fighting. He flies to the tree and says, "Stop fighting, squirrels! You are making too much noise. Why do you want this nut so much?"

"It is a big nut and we are hungry," says Ben.

"It is a shiny nut and we like shiny things," says Lily.

The bird says, "This is not a nut. It is a ball. A child left it here. It is not good to eat or to store. It is only good to play with."

Ben and Lily look at the ball. They see that it is not a nut. They feel silly.

"Oops, we were wrong," says Ben.

"Sorry, we were rude," says Lily.

They thank the bird for solving their problem. They ask him if he wants to play with the ball. He says yes. They all play with the ball and have fun. They learn to be friends and to share.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play hide and seek. They played every Sunday after lunch, when their mom and dad took a nap. They took turns to hide and seek in the house and the garden. They knew many good hiding places, like under the bed, behind the sofa, or in the shed.

One Sunday, Anna had a new idea. She wanted to hide in the big box that came in the mail. It was for their dad's birthday, but he had not opened it yet. Anna thought it was an amazing hiding place, because no one would look there. She climbed into the box and closed the lid. She waited for Ben to find her.

Ben looked everywhere for Anna. He checked all the usual hiding places, but he could not find her. He started to feel worried. He called her name, but he heard no answer. He wondered where she could be. He thought maybe she had gone to the neighbor's house, or to the park, or to the store. He decided to ask their mom and dad for help.

He ran to their bedroom and knocked on the door. He said, "Mom, dad, I can't find Anna. Do you know where she is?" Mom and dad woke up and looked at him. They saw he was scared and sad. They hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Ben. We will help you find Anna. She must be somewhere in the house or the garden. Let's go look together."

They went downstairs and searched the house. They looked in the kitchen, the living room, the bathroom, and the hallway. They did not find Anna. They went outside and searched the garden. They looked in the shed, the swing, the tree, and the flowers. They did not find Anna. They started to feel worried too. They wondered where she could be. They thought maybe she had got lost, or hurt, or taken by a stranger. They decided to call the police for help.

They went back inside and picked up the phone. They were about to dial the number, when they heard a noise. It was coming from the big box that came in the mail. They heard a voice saying, "Ben, where are you? I'm hiding in the box. It's an amazing hiding place. Come and find me." They realized it was Anna. They ran to the box and opened the lid. They saw Anna smiling and waving. They were surprised and relieved. They said, "Anna, you scared us. We were looking for you everywhere. Why did you hide in the box?" Anna said, "I wanted to surprise you. I thought it was a fun game. I'm sorry I made you worry. I love you." They said, "We love you too, Anna. But don't hide in the box again. It's not safe. It's for dad's birthday. Do you want to see what's inside?" Anna said, "Yes, please. What is it?" They said, "It's a bike. A big bike for dad. He will be very happy. Do you want to help us wrap it?" Anna said, "Yes, please. That sounds like fun. Can we play hide and seek again later?" They said, "Yes, we can. But only in the house or the garden. And no more hiding in boxes. OK?" Anna said, "OK. I promise. Can I hide first?" They said, "OK. You can hide first. But we will find you soon. We are good at seeking." They laughed and hugged and went to wrap the bike. They had a happy Sunday.

Lily liked to visit the zoo with her mom. She loved to see the animals and learn their names. Her favorite animal was the parrot. The parrot was famous because he could talk. He could say hello, bye-bye, and many other words.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the zoo again. They stopped by the parrot's cage and said hello. The parrot said hello back. Lily was happy. She wanted to talk more with the parrot. She asked him many questions, like what was his name, what did he eat, and where did he come from.

The parrot did not answer. He was tired of talking. He wanted to be left alone. He was angry at Lily for bothering him. He thought of a way to make her go away.

He waited until Lily came closer to the cage. Then he bit her finger hard. Lily screamed. She felt a lot of pain. She ran to her mom and cried. Her mom hugged her and took her to the nurse. The nurse put a bandage on her finger and gave her a lollipop.

Lily was sad and scared. She did not like the parrot anymore. She did not want to talk to him ever again. She learned that some animals do not like to answer questions. She learned that some animals can be mean. She wished she had never met the famous parrot.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. They saw a bee flying near a rose. Ben wanted to touch the bee.

"Look, Lily, a bee!" Ben said. "It is yellow and black. I want to see it."

"No, Ben, no!" Lily said. "Bees can hurt you. They have a sting. You should not touch them."

But Ben did not listen. He reached out his hand to the bee. The bee did not like that. It felt scared and angry. It stung Ben on his finger. Ben cried out loud. It hurt a lot.

Lily ran to Ben. She saw his finger was red and swollen. She felt sorry for Ben. She took him to their mom. Mom was in the kitchen. She heard Ben crying.

"What happened, Ben?" Mom asked. "Why are you crying?"

"A bee stung me!" Ben said. "It hurts!"

Mom took Ben's hand. She saw the sting. She pulled it out gently. She got some ice and a cloth. She put the ice on Ben's finger. She wrapped the cloth around it. She gave Ben a hug and a kiss.

"There, there," Mom said. "It will be better soon. The ice will make it cold and numb. The cloth will keep it clean. You should not touch bees, Ben. They are not toys. They are living things. They can feel and think. They can be scared and angry. They sting to protect themselves. You have to be careful and respectful."

"I'm sorry, Mom," Ben said. "I did not know. I was curious. I wanted to see the bee."

"I know, Ben," Mom said. "It is good to be curious. But you have to be safe too. You have to ask before you touch something. You have to learn about the things you see. You have to be kind to the things you see. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom," Ben said. "I understand. Thank you for helping me. I love you."

"I love you too, Ben," Mom said. "Now, let's go and find Lily. She was very brave and smart. She tried to stop you. She brought you to me. She is a good sister. We should thank her and give her a hug too."

Ben nodded. He felt better. He still felt a little pain, but he also felt love. He and Mom went to the garden. They found Lily. She was sitting on a bench. She looked worried. She saw Ben and Mom. She smiled.

"Hi, Ben," Lily said. "How is your finger?"

"It is better," Ben said. "Mom helped me. She put ice and a cloth on it. She said it will heal soon. I'm sorry I did not listen to you. You were right. Bees can hurt. You are a good sister. Thank you for helping me."

Ben gave Lily a hug. Lily hugged him back. She was happy.

"You're welcome, Ben," Lily said. "I'm glad you are better. I love you."

Mom smiled. She was proud of her children. She hugged them both.

"I love you both," Mom said. "You are good children. You are learning and growing. You are caring and sharing. Now, let's go inside. It is getting late. It is time for dinner. We can have some soup and bread. And maybe some honey too. Honey is made by bees. It is sweet and good. But we have to thank the bees for it. And we have to wipe our mouths after we eat it. We don't want to be sticky and messy. Do we?"

"No, Mom," Ben and Lily said. "We don't. We want to be clean and neat. We will wipe our mouths. We will thank the bees. We will eat our dinner. We are hungry and happy."

They went inside. They ate their dinner. They wiped their mouths. They thanked the bees. They were hungry and happy. They were a family.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they found a big, shiny trumpet on a bench. It was very interesting.

"Wow, look at this!" Lily said. "Can we play with it?"

"Sure, let's try!" Sam said. He picked up the trumpet and blew into it. It made a loud noise. "Brrrrrr!"

Lily laughed. She wanted to try too. She took the trumpet from Sam and blew into it. It made a different noise. "Toot toot!"

They took turns blowing the trumpet and making funny noises. They had a lot of fun.

But then, a big boy came over. He had a mean face and a dirty shirt. He saw the trumpet and wanted it.

"Hey, give me that!" he said. He grabbed the trumpet from Lily and pushed her to the ground.

"Ow!" Lily cried. She was hurt and scared.

Sam saw what happened. He was angry and brave. He ran to the big boy and shouted.

"Leave her alone! That's our trumpet! Go away!"

He tried to take the trumpet back, but the big boy was stronger. He pushed Sam to the ground too.

"Ha ha, it's mine now!" he said. He ran away with the trumpet.

Lily and Sam were sad and hurt. They hugged each other and cried.

A nice lady saw them and came to help. She was a teacher at the park. She had a kind voice and a smile.

"What's wrong, children?" she asked. "Are you OK?"

She listened to their story and felt sorry for them. She helped them get up and cleaned their scrapes.

"That was very mean of him," she said. "But you were very brave, Sam. You tried to protect your friend and your toy. That was very nice of you."

"Thank you," Sam said. He looked at Lily and smiled.

"Thank you, Sam," Lily said. She looked at him and smiled too.

They were still sad about the trumpet, but they were happy to have each other.

The teacher gave them a hug and a cookie. She said she would look for the big boy and the trumpet.

"Don't worry, children," she said. "I'll try to get your trumpet back. But if I can't, I'll get you a new one. How about that?"

Lily and Sam nodded. They liked the teacher. They liked the cookie. They liked the park. But most of all, they liked each other. They were best friends.

Lily was a girl who loved to look at the stars. She wanted to meet a planet and make a new friend. One night, she saw a bright star that was bigger than the others. She wished on the star and said, "Please, let me meet you, star. You look so cute and shiny."

The star heard Lily's wish and smiled. It was not a star, but a planet named Zee. Zee was lonely and wanted to meet a girl like Lily. He used his magic to make a rocket for Lily and sent it to her window. Lily saw the rocket and was very happy. She climbed inside and flew to Zee.

When Lily reached Zee, she saw that he was a blue planet with a big smile and a fluffy tail. He said, "Hello, Lily. I am Zee. I am glad you came to meet me. You are very cute and brave."

Lily said, "Hello, Zee. I am Lily. I am glad you made me a rocket. You are very cute and kind."

They hugged and became friends. They played and talked and laughed. They learned about each other's worlds and shared their dreams. They had so much fun that they did not notice the time.

Soon, the sun came up and Lily had to go back home. She said, "Zee, I have to go now. But I will come back to see you again. I will miss you very much."

Zee said, "Lily, I will miss you too. But I will always watch you from the sky. And I will always be your friend. Thank you for meeting me."

They hugged and said goodbye. Lily got in the rocket and flew back to her window. She waved to Zee and went to bed. She dreamed of Zee and smiled.

The moral of the story is: You can make friends with anyone, even if they are different from you. And you can always stay in touch with your friends, even if they are far away.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. They also like to tell jokes to each other.

One day, Lily tells Tom a joke. She says, "What do you call a fish that wears a hat?" Tom thinks hard. He does not know the answer. He says, "I don't know. What do you call it?"

Lily smiles. She says, "A head fish!" Tom laughs. He thinks the joke is funny. He says, "That is a good joke, Lily. You are funny."

Then, Tom tells Lily a joke. He says, "What do you get when you cross a cow and a duck?" Lily thinks hard. She does not know the answer. She says, "I don't know. What do you get?"

Tom smiles. He says, "Milk and quackers!" Lily laughs. She thinks the joke is funny. She says, "That is a good joke, Tom. You are funny too."

They tell more jokes to each other. They have fun. They are happy.

But then, they hear a loud noise. It is a big dog. It is barking. It is running towards them. It looks angry. Lily and Tom are scared. They stop telling jokes. They are alert.

They run to the slide. They climb up the ladder. They slide down fast. They run to the fence. They climb over the fence. They are safe.

They look at the dog. The dog is still barking. It is still angry. It cannot climb the fence. It cannot get them.

Lily and Tom sigh. They are relieved. They say, "That was a bad dog. It was not funny. It was scary."

They hug each other. They are glad they are friends. They say, "We are brave. We are smart. We are funny."

They smile. They go home. They tell their moms and dads about their jokes and their adventure. They are proud. They are happy.

Ben is scared of the dog. He stays away from the bench. He ignores Sara and the dog. He finds a ball and kicks it.

Sara and Max don't care. They are happy together. They are friends.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the old factory near their home. It was a big and noisy place, with many machines and pipes and boxes. They liked to pretend they were workers, and they used the things they found to make their own toys and games.

One day, they found a big bowl and a spoon in a corner. They wondered what they could mix in the bowl. They looked around and saw many different things: sand, water, paint, glue, feathers, buttons, and more. They decided to mix them all and see what would happen.

They took turns to add something to the bowl and stir it with the spoon. The bowl became very full and colorful. It looked like a rainbow soup. Ben and Lily were happy and curious. They wanted to taste it.

"Can I have a sip?" Ben asked.

"No, I want to try it first!" Lily said.

They both reached for the spoon, but they pulled too hard. The spoon flew out of their hands and hit a big red button on the wall. The button made a loud beep and turned on a machine. The machine had a long arm with a claw. The claw grabbed the bowl and lifted it up.

"Hey, that's our mix!" Ben shouted.

"Give it back!" Lily cried.

They ran after the machine, but it was too fast. It moved the bowl to another part of the factory, where there was a big oven. The oven was hot and smoky. The machine dropped the bowl into the oven and closed the door.

Ben and Lily stopped and looked at the oven. They were scared and sad. They had lost their mix. They wondered what would happen to it.

"Maybe it will explode," Ben said.

"Maybe it will turn into a monster," Lily said.

They hugged each other and waited. They heard a loud bang and saw a flash of light. The oven door opened and something came out. It was a big and unusual cake. It had many colors and shapes and smells. It looked like their mix, but bigger and softer and sweeter.

Ben and Lily gasped and smiled. They ran to the cake and touched it. It was warm and sticky and fluffy. They broke off a piece and tasted it. It was delicious. It had all the flavors of their mix, but better and nicer.

They laughed and cheered. They had made a cake. They had never made a cake before. They were proud and happy. They decided to share it with their friends and family. They found a big tray and put the cake on it. They carried it out of the factory and back to their home. They had a big party and ate the cake. Everyone liked it and said it was the best cake ever. Ben and Lily agreed. It was their mix cake. It was their special cake. It was their unusual cake.

"I know you like toys, but you have enough," she said. "You do not need more. You should be happy with what you have and share with others. Taking things that are not yours is a waste. You could lose them, break them, or hurt someone with them. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They understood that taking their mom's purse was a mistake. They said sorry again and promised to be good. They put their toys away and helped their mom with the dishes. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that taking is rude and waste is bad.

She hugged Lily and tried to comfort her. She said she was sorry. She said she loved her. She said she would buy her a new doll. But Lily did not want a new doll. She wanted Ann. She wanted her old doll. She wanted her alive.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not toys. They can hurt you or others or things you love. Listen to your sister or brother or mommy or daddy when they tell you to stop. Be kind and gentle and smart. Or you will be sorry and sad and alone.

Lily and Ben looked at the blue block. They saw the four lines. They counted them.

Mom said, "Now, look at your other blocks. Do they have measures too?"

For example, this block with one measure is smaller than this block with two measures. And this block with three measures is bigger than this block with two measures. "Leave us alone, ducks! You are mean!" Lily cried. She hugged her sandwich to her chest.

But the ducks did not listen. They kept bothering the children and their boat. They made a big mess in the pond.

Lily and Tom were sad and scared. They did not like the ducks anymore. They wished they had never given them honey. They decided to leave the pond and go home.

They picked up their boat and their sandwiches. They ran away from the ducks. They did not look back.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that honey is sweet, but too much of it can make trouble. They learned that ducks are nice, but only when they are not greedy. They learned that sailing is fun, but only when the pond is calm.

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks. They liked to build towers and bridges and houses. Sometimes they shared their blocks and helped each other. But sometimes they wanted the same block and got mad.

One day, Lily saw a shiny red block that she wanted. She reached for it, but Ben grabbed it first. He said, "This is mine! I saw it first!" Lily felt angry. She wanted the red block too. She tried to pull it from Ben's hand, but he held it tight. He said, "No! Go away!"

Lily was so angry that she pinched Ben's arm. Ben yelled, "Ow! That hurts!" He dropped the red block and rubbed his arm. Lily picked up the red block and said, "Ha! Now it's mine!" She ran away with the block.

Ben felt sad and mad. He wanted the red block back. He wanted to pinch Lily too. But then he remembered that pinching was not nice. It made people feel bad. He thought, "Maybe I can find another block that Lily likes. Then we can trade and be friends again."

He looked around and saw a shiny blue block that Lily liked. He picked it up and ran after Lily. He said, "Lily, Lily, wait! I have something for you!" Lily stopped and turned around. She liked the red block, but she liked the blue block too. She said, "OK, let's trade. That's a good idea." She gave Ben the red block and took the blue block. They smiled at each other and said, "Thank you!"

Lily and Ben were happy. They had both scored a shiny block. They had also been thoughtful and kind. They hugged and said, "Let's play together!" They went back to their blocks and built a big rainbow. They had fun and forgot about pinching.

Ben and Lily were playing in the farm with their dad. They liked to see the animals and feed them. They saw cows, pigs, chickens, and horses. But their favorite animal was the goat. The goat was white and had horns and a beard. He was friendly and liked to eat grass and hay.

One day, they saw a new goat in the farm. He was black and had big yellow eyes. He looked mysterious and scary. Ben and Lily wanted to go near him, but their dad said no.

"That goat is not ours. He came from the woods. He is wild and might bite you. Stay away from him," their dad said.

But Ben and Lily were curious. They wanted to see the black goat and touch him. They waited until their dad was busy with the cows. Then they sneaked to the fence where the black goat was.

"Hello, goat. What is your name?" Lily asked.

The black goat did not answer. He stared at them with his yellow eyes. He made a strange noise, like a growl.

"Maybe he is hungry. Let's give him some hay," Ben said.

He picked up some hay from the ground and reached out his hand to the black goat. The black goat moved closer to the fence. He looked at the hay and then at Ben's hand.

Suddenly, he opened his mouth and bit Ben's hand. Ben screamed and dropped the hay. He ran back to his dad, crying.

Lily was scared. She wanted to run too, but the black goat urged her to stay. He made another noise, like a whisper.

"Come, little girl. I have a secret to tell you. Follow me to the woods. There is something you will like there," the black goat said.

Lily felt a strange pull in her heart. She wanted to know the secret. She wanted to see the woods. She forgot about her dad and her brother. She climbed over the fence and followed the black goat.

The black goat led her to a dark and thick part of the woods. There was a cave there. The black goat went inside the cave. He told Lily to come too.

"Here is the secret, little girl. I am not a goat. I am a witch. And you are my dinner," the black goat said.

He changed his shape and became a tall and ugly woman. She had long black hair and sharp teeth. She grabbed Lily and laughed.

Lily realized she had made a big mistake. She wished she had listened to her dad. She wished she had stayed away from the mysterious black goat. She wished she could see her dad and her brother again. She screamed and cried, but no one heard her. The witch ate her up.

So, the baby crawled out of the crib and went outside. The stars were shining brightly, and the baby felt brave. They looked around and saw that the rude noise was just a silly cat playing with a toy. The baby giggled and went back to sleep under the shining stars, feeling safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, wise owl who lived in a tree. One day, he saw a lot of traffic on the road. The cars were moving slowly, and the owl wondered why. He asked a little bird, "Why is there so much traffic?"

The bird replied, "There was a big accident. A truck struck a car and now everyone is stuck."

The owl felt sad for the people in the cars. He thought for a moment and said, "I know what to do. I will fly over the traffic and tell everyone to be patient. The road will clear soon."

So, the owl flew over the traffic and told everyone to be patient. Soon enough, the traffic started moving again. The people in the cars were happy and grateful to the wise owl who helped them.

Tim and Tom started to disagree. Tim said, "I like the fake tree. It is pretty." Tom said, "No, I do not like it. Real trees are better." They talked and talked, but could not agree. In the end, they decided to keep walking and enjoy the real trees around them. They laughed and played the rest of the morning.

But then, the clown gave them all balloons too and started to make funny faces. Lily realized that the clown was not scary after all and they all had a jolly time together.

Later that day, Lily's mom explained to her that sometimes things may seem scary at first, but they can turn out to be fun and happy. Lily learned that it's important to not judge things by their appearance and to always try to see the good in everything.

As she reached for the vine, her foot stumbled on something. It was an icy patch on the ground. She fell down and scraped her knee. "Ouch!" she cried.

Just then, a bear appeared. "What are you doing in my woods?" the bear growled. "I was just picking this pretty vine," Lily said, showing the bear. "That's my lunch," the bear said, and he ate Lily up. The end.

One day, a jolly mole was digging in the ground. He liked to find shiny things and sort them by color. He had a pile of red things, a pile of blue things, and a pile of yellow things.

He heard a voice above him. It was a bird. The bird said, "Hello, mole. What are you doing?"

The mole popped his head out of the hole. He said, "Hello, bird. I am sorting shiny things. Do you want to see?"

The bird flew down and looked at the mole's piles. He said, "Wow, mole. You have many shiny things. They are very pretty. Can I have one?"

The mole said, "Sure, bird. You can have one. Which one do you like?"

The bird looked at the piles and said, "I like the yellow ones. They are like the sun. Can I have this one?" He pointed to a yellow ring.

The mole said, "Yes, bird. You can have that one. It is a ring. You can wear it on your wing."

The bird said, "Thank you, mole. You are very kind. I will wear it on my wing and show it to my friends."

The mole said, "You are welcome, bird. I am glad you like it. Have a nice day."

The bird said, "You too, mole. Have fun sorting shiny things."

The bird flew away with the ring on his wing. The mole went back to his hole and continued sorting shiny things. He was very happy. He liked to make new friends.

Tim and Mia were playing in the sand. They had a bucket and a spade each. They wanted to make a big castle with towers and walls.

But Tim was not happy. He did not like the sand. It was too hot and sticky. It got in his eyes and his mouth. He wanted to go home.

"Sand is yucky!" he said. "I don't want to play here. Let's go back to the house."

Mia looked at him. She liked the sand. It was fun and soft. She could make shapes and patterns with it. She wanted to stay.

"Sand is nice!" she said. "I want to play here. Look at my castle. It is big and pretty."

She showed him her castle. It had four towers and a wall. She had used shells and stones to decorate it.

Tim did not care. He did not like her castle. He did not like anything.

"Your castle is ugly!" he said. "It will fall down soon. The wind will blow it away. The water will wash it away. It is not safe."

He kicked her castle. He broke one of the towers. He made a hole in the wall. He threw some sand at her.

Mia was angry. She was sad. She had worked hard on her castle. She had made it with love. She did not want him to ruin it.

"Stop it!" she said. "You are mean! You are bad! You are not my friend!"

She hit him with her spade. She made him cry. She ran away.

Tim was sorry. He was hurt. He had been rude. He had been wrong. He wanted to say sorry. He wanted to be her friend.

He ran after her. He called her name. He gave her a hug. He gave her his spade.

"I'm sorry!" he said. "I was silly. I was grumpy. I don't hate sand. I don't hate your castle. I don't hate you. You are my friend."

Mia smiled. She forgave him. She hugged him back. She took his spade.

"It's okay!" she said. "I was mad. I was hurt. I don't hate you. You are my friend."

They went back to the sand. They fixed the castle. They made it bigger and prettier. They made it safe.

They played together. They had fun. They were happy.

One day, a little otter was swimming in the river. He saw a big fish and wanted to catch it. He chased the fish, but it was too fast. He got tired and stopped to rest on a rock.

Then he heard a voice. "Hello, little otter. Do you want to be my friend?" The voice came from a weird animal. It had a long nose, a big mouth, and sharp teeth. It was a crocodile.

The little otter was scared. He did not know what to say. He thought the crocodile wanted to eat him.

But the crocodile smiled. "Don't be afraid. I am lonely. I have no friends. Everyone runs away from me. You look nice and fun. Can we play together?"

The little otter felt sorry for the crocodile. He thought maybe he could be his friend. He said, "Okay, we can play. But you have to promise not to hurt me or any other animals."

The crocodile nodded. "I promise. I will be nice and gentle. Come, let's go to the pond. There are many frogs and ducks there. We can watch them and make funny noises."

The little otter followed the crocodile to the pond. They saw the frogs and ducks. The crocodile tried to imitate their sounds. He made a loud ribbit and a quack. The frogs and ducks were scared and ran away. The little otter laughed. He thought the crocodile was silly and funny.

They played for a while. Then the little otter said, "I have to go home now. My mom and dad are waiting for me. Thank you for playing with me. You are a good friend."

The crocodile smiled. "Thank you too. You are a good friend. You made me happy. Can we play again tomorrow?"

The little otter nodded. "Yes, we can. But remember your promise. Don't hurt anyone."

The crocodile nodded. "I will. Goodbye, little otter. See you tomorrow."

The little otter waved and swam away. He was happy. He had made a new friend. A weird friend, but a good friend.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge someone by their appearance. You can find friendship in unexpected places. Be kind and brave.

Sara and Ben are playing with their crayons and paper. They like to draw animals and cars and flowers. Sara draws a big cat with stripes and Ben draws a fast car with wheels. They are happy with their drawings.

But then, Sara sees something on the table. It is white and small and soft. She does not know what it is. She picks it up and looks at it. She asks Ben, "What is this?"

Ben looks at the thing in Sara's hand. He knows what it is. He has seen it before. He says, "That is an eraser. You can use it to make things go away."

Sara is curious. She wants to try the eraser. She rubs it on her paper. She sees that the cat's tail disappears. She rubs it more and more. She sees that the cat's stripes and ears and eyes disappear. She is amazed. She says, "Wow! The eraser makes the cat go away!"

Ben is excited. He wants to try the eraser too. He takes it from Sara and rubs it on his paper. He sees that the car's wheels and windows and doors disappear. He rubs it more and more. He sees that the car's color and shape and lights disappear. He is amazed. He says, "Wow! The eraser makes the car go away!"

Sara and Ben are very happy. They have discovered a new way to play with their crayons and paper. They can make things go away and draw new things. They can make new stories and pictures. They can have fun with the eraser. They laugh and smile and share the eraser. They are friends.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big flag on a pole. The flag was red and white and blue. It was waving in the wind.

"Let's get the flag!" Ben said. He ran to the pole and tried to pull the flag down.

"No, Ben, stop!" Lila said. "The flag is not for us. It is for everyone. It is a sign of our country. We have to respect it."

But Ben did not listen. He was persistent. He wanted the flag. He pulled harder and harder. He did not resist his want.

Suddenly, a man came. He was wearing a uniform. He had a badge and a hat. He was a guard. He saw Ben pulling the flag.

"Hey, kid, what are you doing?" the guard said. He was angry. He grabbed Ben by the arm and took him away from the pole.

"I'm sorry, sir, he's just a child. He doesn't know better," Lila said. She followed the guard and Ben.

The guard took them to a small office. He made them sit on a chair. He explained to them why the flag was important and why they should not touch it. He told them to be sorry and to promise not to do it again.

Ben and Lila felt bad. They said they were sorry and they promised not to do it again. They learned their lesson. They understood that the flag was not a toy. It was a symbol of their country. They had to respect it.

The guard let them go. He gave them a sticker of the flag. He told them to be good and to love their country.

Ben and Lila thanked the guard. They put the sticker on their shirts. They went back to the park. They played with other things. They did not bother the flag anymore. They were happy and proud.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play with blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. They could make houses, cars, towers and more. They had fun together.

One day, Anna saw a new block that was smooth and shiny. It was silver and round like a ball. She wanted to play with it. She asked Ben, "Can I have that block, please?"

Ben looked at the block and said, "No, this is my block. I found it first. You have many other blocks. Go play with them."

Anna felt sad and angry. She said, "That is not fair. You have to share. Sharing is good. If you share, I will share too."

Ben shook his head and said, "No, this is mine. Go away." He hugged the block and turned away from Anna.

Anna was very upset. She wanted to take the block from Ben. She thought of a plan. She said, "Okay, fine. You can keep your block. But can I know its name? Does it have a name?"

Ben was curious. He said, "Name? What do you mean? Blocks don't have names. They are just blocks."

Anna said, "But this is a special block. It is smooth and shiny. It must have a name. Don't you want to know its name?"

Ben thought for a moment. He said, "Well, maybe. But how can I know its name?"

Anna said, "I can tell you. I know its name. But you have to let me hold it for a second. Then I will give it back to you. I promise."

Ben was doubtful. He said, "How do you know its name? Are you lying?"

Anna said, "No, I am not lying. I know its name because I saw it on the box. It is a very nice name. Do you want to hear it?"

Ben was tempted. He said, "Okay, fine. You can hold it for a second. But only a second. Then you have to give it back to me."

Anna smiled and said, "Thank you. Here, give it to me." She reached out her hand and took the block from Ben.

As soon as she had the block, she ran away. She said, "Ha ha, I tricked you. This is my block now. Bye bye, Ben."

Ben was shocked and angry. He said, "Hey, that's not fair. You lied to me. You broke your promise. Give me back my block. Give it back."

But Anna did not listen. She ran to her house and locked the door. She said, "This is my block. I love it. It is smooth and shiny. And it has a name. Its name is...mine."

The end.

Moral: Lying and stealing are bad. They hurt others and yourself. Sharing and honesty are good. They make others and yourself happy.

Lily liked to lead her toys in a row. She had a regular game where she pretended to be a teacher and her toys were her students. She gave them names and taught them things like colors, shapes and songs.

One day, she decided to lead her toys to the park. She put them in a big bag and walked with her mom. She was very excited to show them the swings, the slide and the sandbox. She thought her toys would have fun and learn new things.

When they got to the park, Lily took out her toys and put them in a row on a bench. She told them to wait and be good while she played. She ran to the swings and pushed herself high. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She was very happy.

But she did not see that a big dog came to the bench and sniffed her toys. The dog liked the smell of the toys and thought they were his. He grabbed one of them in his mouth and ran away. Lily did not hear the dog or her toy squeak.

When she came back to the bench, she saw that one of her toys was missing. She looked around and saw the dog with her toy. She felt very sad and angry. She shouted at the dog and ran to get her toy back. She did not care that the dog was bigger and stronger than her. She loved her toy and wanted it back.

The dog was surprised by Lily's shout and dropped the toy. He did not want to fight with her. He just wanted to play. He wagged his tail and barked. He hoped that Lily would be his friend and share her toys with him.

Lily picked up her toy and hugged it. She saw that the dog was not mean, just curious. She felt sorry for him and wondered if he had any toys of his own. She decided to give him one of her toys as a gift. She chose one that she did not like very much and threw it to the dog. The dog caught it and wagged his tail again. He was very happy.

Lily smiled and led her toys back to the bag. She told them that they had a new friend and that they should be nice to him. She waved to the dog and said goodbye. She walked with her mom back home. She was very proud of herself. She had learned how to lead, how to share and how to make friends.

One day, a new boy comes to their school. His name is Max. He wears a different uniform. It is red and black. He wants to play soccer with Tom and Sam.

"Can I play with you?" Max asks.

"Sure, you can play with us," Tom says. He is nice.

"No, you can't play with us," Sam says. He is mean. "You have a bad uniform. Go away."

Max feels sad. He does not have any friends.

Tom listens to Sam. He does not want to make him angry. But he also listens to his heart. He knows it is not fair to be mean to Max.

"Sam, stop being mean," Tom says. "Max can play with us. His uniform does not matter. He is a good boy."

Sam looks at Tom. He is surprised. He does not like to share his friend.

"Fine, whatever," Sam says. He is rough. He kicks the ball hard. He tries to hit Max.

Max dodges the ball. He is fast. He kicks the ball back. He scores a goal.

"Yay, Max!" Tom cheers. He is happy. He gives Max a high-five.

"Boo, Max!" Sam jeers. He is angry. He walks away.

Tom and Max smile. They are friends. They play soccer together. They do not care about uniforms. They care about fun.

Lily felt sorry for Sam. She remembered that her grandma told her to share and be kind. She took off her sweater and gave it to Sam.

"Here, you can wear my sweater. It will keep you warm," she said.

"Really? Thank you, Lily. You are very sweet," Sam said. He smiled and put on the sweater. It was big for him, but it felt cozy and nice.

Lily and Sam played happily in the park. They shared their toys and snacks. They had fun and laughed a lot. They did not mind the cold and the wind. They were warm in their hearts.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. When we help others, we make them happy and ourselves happy too.

Ben and Lily started to walk around the park, looking for the tree that the acorn came from. They looked at every oak tree they saw, but none of them seemed big enough or strong enough to have such a mighty acorn. They walked and walked, but they could not find the tree.

They were about to give up, when they saw a very big and old oak tree at the edge of the park. It had a thick trunk and many branches and leaves. It looked very wise and proud. Ben and Lily ran towards it, hoping that it was the tree they were looking for.

They reached the tree and looked up at it. They saw many acorns hanging from the branches, but they were all small and normal. They did not look like the mighty acorn they had found. Ben and Lily felt sad and confused. They wondered where the mighty acorn came from, if not from this tree.

Then, they heard a loud and deep voice from above. It said, "Hello, little ones. I see you have found my acorn. It is a very special acorn. It is the last acorn I will ever make. I am very old and tired, and soon I will fall asleep forever. But before I do, I wanted to give one last gift to the world. A mighty acorn that can grow into a mighty tree. A tree that can live for a long time and give shade and food and beauty to many creatures. A tree that can be your friend and protector. A tree that can carry on my legacy."

Ben and Lily looked up and saw a face in the bark of the tree. It was the tree that was talking to them. They were amazed and scared and curious. They did not know what to say or do.

The tree smiled and said, "Do not be afraid. I mean you no harm. I am glad that you found my acorn. I suggest that you take it and plant it somewhere safe and sunny. Then, water it and care for it and watch it grow. It will grow into a mighty tree, just like me. And you can visit it and play with it and talk to it. It will be your friend and protector. It will be my child and yours."

Ben and Lily felt a warm and happy feeling in their hearts. They liked the idea of having a mighty tree as their friend and protector. They liked the idea of being the tree's children. They nodded and said, "Thank you, tree. Thank you for your acorn. Thank you for your gift. We will do as you suggest. We will plant your acorn and grow your child. We will love it and respect it and learn from it. We will always remember you and your story."

The tree nodded and said, "You are welcome, little ones. You are very kind and brave and smart. I am proud of you and happy for you. Now, go and find a good place for your acorn. And come back and visit me whenever you can. I will always be here, until I fall asleep forever. Goodbye, little ones. Goodbye, my children."

Ben and Lily hugged the tree and said goodbye. Then, they took the mighty acorn and ran to find a good place to plant it. They knew they had a very special mission and a very special friend. They knew they had a very special story to tell.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said.

"Please, just for a little bit?" Ben begged.

"No, go away!" Lily shouted.

Ben felt sad and angry. He did not like Lily's opinion. He thought she was being mean and selfish. He decided to take the doll from her by force.

He grabbed the doll and ran to his room. Lily chased after him, screaming and crying.

"Give it back, give it back!" Lily yelled.

"Shut up, it's mine now!" Ben said.

He slammed the door and locked it. Lily banged on the door, but Ben did not open it.

They both sat on their beds, holding the doll and the car. They felt lonely and sorry. They wished they could play together again. They realized they were being impatient and rude. They wanted to say sorry and share their toys.

They got up and walked to the door. They both said at the same time:

"I'm sorry, can we be friends again?"

"Wow, a flying dinosaur!" Lily said. "Can we see more?"

Rudy was a restless reindeer. He did not like to stay still and listen to his mom and dad. He wanted to run and jump and play all day. He did not care about the other reindeer or the rules of the forest.

One day, Rudy saw a shiny red ball hanging from a tree. He wanted to have it for himself. He ran to the tree and tried to reach the ball with his nose. But the ball was too high for him. He jumped and jumped, but he could not touch it.

"Rudy, stop that!" his mom said. "That is not your ball. That is a bird's nest. You will drop it and hurt the baby birds inside."

"I don't care," Rudy said. "I want the ball. It is pretty and fun. The birds can find another nest."

He jumped again and again, until he finally hit the ball with his antlers. The ball fell to the ground, but it was not a ball. It was a nest, and inside were three tiny birds. They were scared and cold and hungry. They cried for their mom and dad.

Rudy felt bad. He had done a bad thing. He had dropped the nest and hurt the birds. He wished he had listened to his mom and left the nest alone.

He heard a loud noise. It was the bird's mom and dad. They saw what Rudy had done. They were angry and sad. They flew to the nest and tried to help their babies.

"Go away, you bad reindeer!" they said. "You have no right to touch our nest. You have no respect for the forest. You have no friends here."

Rudy ran away. He was ashamed and sorry. He had no ball, no nest, and no friends. He had learned a hard lesson. He had learned to be careful and kind. He had learned to not drop things that are not his.

"Look, Lily, what is this?" Tom asked, holding the razor in his hand.

"I don't know, Tom, but it looks bad. It can hurt you. Put it down!" Lily said, scared.

"No, I want to keep it. It is mine. I found it!" Tom said, stubborn.

He tried to put the razor in his pocket, but it cut his finger. He cried out in pain and dropped the razor. Blood came out of his finger. Lily ran to get their mom.

"Mom, mom, Tom is hurt! He found a razor and it cut him!" Lily shouted.

Mom came quickly and saw Tom crying and bleeding. She took him inside and cleaned his wound. She put a band-aid on his finger and gave him a hug.

"Tom, you should never touch a razor. It is very dangerous. It can cut you very badly. Where did you find it?" Mom asked, worried.

"In the backyard, in a hole. I wanted to keep it. It was shiny," Tom said, sobbing.

Mom shook her head and sighed. She went outside with Lily and found the razor. She took a shovel and buried the razor deep in the ground.

"Let's bury this razor, Lily. We don't want anyone else to find it and get hurt. It is a harsh thing. It does not belong here," Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. I'm sorry, Tom. I hope your finger gets better soon," Lily said.

They buried the razor and went back inside. They had some cookies and milk and played with their toys. They forgot about the razor and had fun. They learned to be careful with things they find in the dirt.

The lady laughed. "No, you can't. Go away, you dirty kids. This is my food, not yours." She slammed the door.

Lily and Tom felt very sad. They shivered in the cold. They smelled something yummy from the house. It was soup. They wished they could have some soup.

They saw a window with no curtains. They peeked inside. They saw the lady sitting at a big table. She had a lot of soup. She ate it all by herself. She did not share with anyone.

Lily and Tom felt very angry. They wanted to take some soup from her. They looked for a way to get inside. They found a small door at the back of the house. They opened it quietly. They sneaked into the kitchen.

They saw a big pot of soup on the stove. It was still hot. They grabbed two spoons. They dipped them into the pot. They put the soup in their mouths.

But the soup was not yummy. It was very spicy. It burned their tongues. It made them cough. It made them cry.

The lady heard the noise. She ran into the kitchen. She saw Lily and Tom with the spoons. She screamed, "You little thieves! How dare you touch my soup! It's not for you! It's for my cats!"

She grabbed a broom. She hit them with it. She chased them out of the house. She threw the spoons at them. She yelled, "Go away and never come back!"

Lily and Tom ran away. They still felt hungry and cold. They also felt hurt and scared. They had no soup. They had no friends. They had no home. They had a bad ending.

Tom was a boy who did not like haircuts. He liked his hair long and messy. He did not want to go to the barber with his mom. He said, "No, no, no! I do not want a haircut!"

His mom said, "Tom, you need a haircut. Your hair is too long and it is hot outside. You will feel better with a haircut. It will not hurt. The barber is nice. He will give you a sticker and a lollipop."

Tom did not understand. He did not want to feel better. He did not want a sticker or a lollipop. He wanted his hair. He cried and kicked and screamed. He made a big fuss.

His mom was sad and tired. She said, "Tom, please stop. You are being rude and naughty. You are making the barber and the other people unhappy. You should be kind and polite. You should listen to your mom. She knows what is good for you."

Tom did not listen. He kept crying and kicking and screaming. He did not care about the barber or the other people. He did not care about his mom. He only cared about his hair.

The barber was patient and gentle. He tried to calm Tom down. He said, "Tom, I understand. You like your hair. But sometimes we need to change our hair. It is part of growing up. It is fun and cool. You can choose how you want your hair to look. You can have a spike or a curl or a bang. You can have a blue or a green or a red hair. You can have anything you want."

Tom stopped crying and kicking and screaming. He looked at the barber. He looked at the mirror. He saw his hair. He saw the scissors and the comb and the spray. He saw the colors and the stickers and the lollipops. He thought for a moment. He said, "Really? I can have anything I want?"

The barber said, "Yes, really. You can have anything you want. As long as you are brave and still and quiet. Can you do that?"

Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, I can do that. I want a spike. And a blue hair. And a sticker. And a lollipop."

The barber smiled. He said, "Okay, Tom. You got it. Let's do it."

Tom got his haircut. He was brave and still and quiet. He did not cry or kick or scream. He liked his haircut. He felt better. He was not hot anymore. He looked fun and cool. He got his sticker and his lollipop. He said, "Thank you, barber. You are nice. I like you."

His mom was happy and proud. She said, "Tom, you did a great job. You are a good boy. You are kind and polite. You listened to your mom. She loves you. You look handsome and smart. I like you."

Tom hugged his mom. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are nice. I love you. I understand. I need a haircut. It is good for me."

The moral of the story is: Sometimes we need to do things we do not like, but they are good for us. We should listen to our parents and respect others. We should be brave and try new things. We can have fun and be ourselves. We can learn and grow. We can understand.

He tried to stick the sticker on the towel, but it did not stay. He tried again and again, but it kept falling off. He got angry and pushed the sticker hard on the towel. But he pushed too hard and the towel fell off the toilet. The toilet made a loud noise and water started to come out.

"Oh no!" Sara said. "The toilet is broken! Mom will be mad!"

Tom felt scared. He did not mean to break the toilet. He wanted to fix it, but he did not know how. He looked at Sara and saw she was crying.

"I'm sorry, Sara," he said. "It was an accident. Maybe we can tell Mom it was a storm and the pirates did it."

Sara shook her head. She knew Mom would not believe them. She knew they had to tell the truth and face the consequences. She took Tom's hand and said, "Come on, Tom. We have to go and tell Mom what we did. Maybe she will not be too angry if we say we are sorry."

They walked out of the bathroom, holding the wet towel and the sticker. They hoped Mom would understand and forgive them. They learned a lesson that day: never play with the toilet. It was not a ship, it was a toilet. And toilets can break.

"Stop, Lily!" Sam says. "You need to ask first. Maybe the dog does not like it. Maybe the dog is not nice. Maybe the dog has a person."

Lily does not listen. She reaches for the dog. The dog barks. The dog bites. Lily cries.

A person comes. The person is angry. The person is the dog's person. The person says: "Why did you touch my dog? You did not ask. You did not permit. That is bad. You hurt my dog. You hurt yourself."

Lily is sorry. She says: "I am sorry. I like dogs. I wanted to be a friend. I did not know. I did not think."

The person is kind. The person says: "It is okay. You made a mistake. But you need to be careful. You need to respect animals. You need to ask before you touch. You need to permit. That is good. That is safe."

Lily nods. She says: "I understand. I will do that. Thank you."

Sam hugs Lily. He says: "I am glad you are okay. You are my friend. I care about you."

Lily hugs Sam. She says: "You are my friend too. You are brave. You helped me."

They go back to the park. They play some more. But they are tired. They go home. They say goodbye. They sleep. They dream of dogs. Nice dogs. Friendly dogs. Dogs that permit.

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her room. She saw the book, the gem, and Sara's hand. She was angry and scared. She took the book and the gem and threw them away. She hugged Sara and said sorry. Anna says to Ben, "Ben, you are not organized. You are wasting the cherries. You should pick them like me. Then you will have more and better cherries."

Ben says to Anna, "Anna, you are too organized. You are not having fun. You should pick them like me. Then you will have more and faster cherries."

They start to argue. They do not share. They do not laugh. They are not happy.

Their moms see them. They are sad. They go to the tree. They say to Anna and Ben, "Anna and Ben, you are both wrong. You should not be too organized or too not organized. You should be balanced. Anna and Ben listen to their moms. They say sorry to each other. They hug. They share their cherries. They laugh. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Be balanced, share and laugh.

One day, a mole was digging in the ground. He liked to make tunnels and find food. He was very hungry and wanted to eat something delicious. He dug and dug until he saw a big carrot. He smiled and bit the carrot. It was crunchy and sweet.

But then he heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw a big rabbit. The rabbit was angry and shouted at the mole. "Hey, that is my carrot! You are stealing my food! Go away!" The rabbit had big ears and teeth and looked scary.

The mole was scared and sorry. He did not know it was the rabbit's carrot. He wanted to be friends with the rabbit. He said, "I am sorry, rabbit. I did not see you. I was very hungry and the carrot looked delicious. Can we share it?"

The rabbit did not listen. He was still angry and wanted the carrot for himself. He said, "No, we cannot share it. It is mine. You are a bad mole. You should leave now or I will bite you!" He moved closer to the mole and showed his teeth.

The mole did not know what to do. He did not want to fight with the rabbit. He did not want to leave the carrot. He did not want to be hungry. He did not want to be alone. He shrugged his shoulders and sighed. He said, "Okay, rabbit. You can have the carrot. I will go and find another food. Maybe we can be friends another day." He turned around and went back to his tunnel.

The rabbit was happy and ate the carrot. He did not say thank you to the mole. He did not think about the mole. He did not care about the mole. He was selfish and rude.

The mole was sad and hungry. He dug and dug until he found a worm. He ate the worm. It was not delicious. It was slimy and bitter. He wished he had the carrot. He wished he had a friend. He was kind and polite.

One day, a chubby bunny was hopping in the forest. He saw a big stone that looked like a carrot. He wanted to eat it, but it was too hard. He tried to bite it, but he hurt his teeth. He tried to push it, but he could not move it.

"Hello, bunny," said a voice. The bunny looked up and saw a fox. The fox was smiling, but he had sharp teeth. "Do you need help with the stone?"

The bunny was scared of the fox. He knew the fox wanted to eat him. He said, "No, thank you. I do not like the stone. I like grass and flowers."

The fox said, "But the stone is very tasty. It is sweet and juicy. If you stay with me, I will show you how to eat it. Come, follow me."

The bunny was curious. He wanted to know how to eat the stone. He forgot his fear and followed the fox. The fox led him to a dark cave. The bunny did not see the trap inside.

"Here we are," said the fox. "Now, you can eat the stone. I will go and get some water for you."

The fox left the cave and blocked the entrance with a big branch. He laughed and said, "Now, the bunny is mine. He was so foolish to trust me."

The bunny realized he was trapped. He saw the stone in the cave, but it was not a carrot. It was a fake stone that the fox had painted. He felt sad and angry. He wished he had not followed the fox. He wished he had stayed away from the stone.

He learned a lesson that day. He learned that not everything that looks good is good. He learned that some animals are not friendly, but tricky. He learned that he should be careful and listen to his instincts. He hoped that someone would come and save him. He hoped that he would see his friends and family again. He hoped that he would never see the fox again.

Mom and Dad smiled and took pictures of them. They walked to the next room. There were many cars and bikes and planes. Max ran to a red car and climbed inside. He pretended to drive and honk.

"Be careful, Max. Don't touch anything that is not available." Mom said.

Lily followed Max and saw a bike. It had two big wheels and a basket. She wanted to try it. She looked around and saw no one. She slipped out of Mom's hand and ran to the bike. She climbed on it and tried to pedal.

But the bike was too big for her. She could not reach the ground. She lost her balance and fell. The bike fell with her and made a loud noise. Lily cried and hurt her knee.

Mom and Dad heard the noise and ran to her. They saw Lily on the floor and the bike on top of her. They lifted the bike and hugged Lily.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Dad asked.

"It hurts, Dad. I'm sorry. I wanted to ride the bike." Lily said.

"You should not have done that, Lily. The bike was not available. It was for looking, not for riding. You could have broken it or hurt yourself more." Mom said.

"I know, Mom. I'm sorry. I won't do it again." Lily said.

Mom and Dad kissed her and checked her knee. It was not very bad. They put a band-aid on it and gave her some water. They told her to be more careful and listen to them.

Lily nodded and said sorry again. She learned her lesson. She did not slip away from Mom and Dad anymore. She stayed with them and enjoyed the museum. She saw many things and learned many words. She had fun with Max and Mom and Dad. She was happy.

"Yes, we are!" Kim says. "We are successful!"

Lily was proud. She had helped the farmer and learned something new. She realized that diving was not only fun and easy, but also useful and kind. She decided to help the farmer more often and make him happy.

The moral of the story is: Helping others is a good way to use your skills and make friends.

Tom nodded. He learned his lesson. He said sorry to the bug and to Sam. He hugged his car and hoped it would be okay.

After playing for a while, Spot became very hungry. He saw a big, juicy bone on the ground and ran to eat it. But the bone belonged to another dog. The other dog was not happy and started to growl at Spot. Tim saw this and remembered he forgot to feed Spot. He ran over to his dog and gave him some food from his bag. Spot was happy to eat and stopped trying to take the other dog's bone.

From that day, Tim learned to never forget to feed Spot before going out to play. And Spot learned not to take things that do not belong to him. They both had a good time at the park and went home happy.

Lily and her mommy continued walking until they reached the playground. There was a boy there who had a toy cowboy hat on. Lily said, "I like your hat!" The boy said, "Thanks! It's from the west!" Lily didn't know what the west was, so she asked her mommy. Her mommy said, "The west is a place where cowboys used to live a long time ago." 

Lily had a lot of fun playing at the playground, but then it started to rain again. Her mommy said, "Let's go home and get dry!" And they walked back home together.

As they walked further down the hall, Lucy noticed a big box full of chocolates. Her eyes lit up and she called out, "Oh look Momma, can I have some?". Her mommy said, "No, sweetheart, this is for the office staff, so don't spoil it".

Lucy was very sad. But then, her mommy had an idea. She picked up some of the chocolates and said, "Let's buy our own and take them home. We can share them with the family".

Lucy smiled. She ran back with her mommy to the car and they drove to the store. Lucy helped pick out the chocolates and, when they got home, they all shared the sweet treats together. Lucy was very happy!

Just then, a careless butterfly fluttered by. It flapped its wings, stirring up the grass around the patch.

The little girl opened her eyes, then said, "Oh no! Why are you being so careless?"

The butterfly stopped fluttering, then said, "I'm sorry. I'm trying to find a perfect place to sleep, just like you."

The little girl smiled. She said, "My patch is a perfect place to sleep. You can stay here and take a nap too, if you'd like."

So the butterfly and the girl stayed in the patch and took long cozy naps. They both had the best dreams.

Lily and Sam did not give up. They followed the butterfly to a big tree. The butterfly landed on a branch. Lily and Sam climbed the tree. They were careful not to fall. They reached the branch. They stretched their hands to the butterfly.

But the butterfly had a surprise. It was not a real butterfly. It was a toy. Someone had tied a string to it. The string was hidden by the leaves. When Lily and Sam touched the toy, it flew up again. It made a funny noise. It sounded like a laugh.

Lily and Sam were confused. They looked around. They saw a boy hiding behind the tree. He was holding the other end of the string. He was laughing too. He had tricked them.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Lily said. "That's not a real butterfly!"

"Sorry, I was just having fun!" the boy said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Lily and Sam looked at each other. They were not angry. They thought it was funny too. They laughed with the boy.

"OK, we'll play with you!" Sam said. "But only if you share your toy!"

"Deal!" the boy said. He gave them the toy. They took turns to make it fly. They had fun with the toy butterfly. They made new friends. They laughed a lot.

The animals heard his cry and looked up. They saw the bird falling from the sky. They were very scared and worried.

"Quick, we have to catch him!" the zebra said.

They ran to where the bird was falling. They stretched their necks and their backs and their legs. They made a soft and big cushion for the bird to land on.

The bird landed safely on the animals. He was wet and cold and hurt, but he was alive. He was very grateful to the animals for saving him.

"Thank you, thank you, you are my friends!" the bird said.

"You are welcome, bird, we are glad you are okay!" the animals said.

They hugged the bird and warmed him up. They told him not to worry about the feather. They said it was just a feather, and he was more important.

The bird understood. He learned his lesson. He said he was sorry for being greedy and foolish. He said he would not chase feathers anymore. He said he would be happy with what he had.

The animals forgave him and smiled. They said they still liked him as their waiter. They said they would play with him again.

The bird was happy. He felt lucky to have such good friends. He said he would serve them better next time. He said he would not forget what they did for him.

They all laughed and played together. They had a good time in the garden. They did not need a feather to be happy. They had each other.

He did not know that the mushroom was a special kind of mushroom. It was a puffball mushroom. When something touched it, it would release its spores. The spores were the seeds of the mushroom. They would fly in the air and land on the ground. Then they would grow into new mushrooms.

The young rabbit learned a lesson. He learned that not all mushrooms were good to eat or play with. He learned to be careful and curious in the forest. He learned to respect the mushroom and its spores. He hoped to find a better snack and a better toy.

Days went by and the competition was still going strong. Timmy and Johnny were determined to win. But one day, they got into a big fight over the coin. They argued and fought until the coin slipped out of their hands and rolled into the street. 

Suddenly, a car drove by and ran over the coin, squishing it flat. Timmy and Johnny were so sad and upset. They realized that their competitive game had caused them to lose something precious. From that day on, they promised to never let competition come between their friendship again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to have a snack, so she went to the cupboard to find something to eat. But when she opened the cupboard, she noticed that it was empty! 

Lily's tummy started to grumble, and she felt sad. She asked her mom, "Mommy, why is the cupboard empty?" Her mom replied, "I haven't had time to go to the store yet, sweetie." 

Lily didn't know what to do. She really wanted a snack. Then, she had an idea. She went outside and picked some apples from the tree in the backyard. She brought them inside and showed her mom. "Look, Mommy! We can have apples for a snack!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Lily. You're so clever!" They ate the apples together and were happy. From that day on, Lily learned that sometimes you have to be creative when things are empty.

"But we need to hurry and go to the park," said her mom.

Lily didn't understand what her mom meant by "spirit", but she knew she didn't want to make anyone unhappy. So, she quickly cleaned up her toys and they hurried to the park. When they got there, Lily saw all the other kids playing and having fun. She was happy she listened to her mom and cleaned up her toys. From then on, she learned that sometimes it's important to listen and hurry so everyone can have fun.

Tom was a strong boy who liked to wander. He liked to see new things and have fun. One day, he wandered too far from his home. He saw a big park with many slides and swings. He wanted to play there.

"Hello, can I play with you?" he asked a girl who was on a swing.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he cried. He wished he had not wandered so far. He wished he had stayed with his mom and dad.

Lily was a little girl who liked to taste new things. She tasted fruits, vegetables, bread, cheese, and even some flowers. She thought tasting was fun and exciting.

One day, she saw a mole in the garden. The mole was digging a hole in the ground. Lily was curious and wanted to taste the mole. She ran towards the mole and tried to catch it.

"Stop, stop!" the mole cried. "Don't taste me, please! I am not good for you. I am dirty and hairy and I live in the dark. You will get sick if you taste me."

Lily was surprised and stopped. She looked at the mole and saw that he was right. He was dirty and hairy and he looked troubled. She felt sorry for the mole and let him go.

"I'm sorry, mole," she said. "I didn't mean to scare you. I just wanted to taste you. Why do you live in the dark?"

The mole sighed and said, "I live in the dark because I am afraid of the light. The light hurts my eyes and makes me blind. I can only see in the dark. That's why I dig holes and hide in the ground."

Lily felt sad for the mole and said, "That's not fair. You should be able to see the light and the colors and the flowers. They are beautiful and make me happy. Can I help you?"

The mole smiled and said, "You are very kind, Lily. But I don't think you can help me. I was born this way and I have to accept it. But you can be my friend and visit me sometimes. Maybe you can tell me about the things you see and taste. That would make me happy too."

Lily nodded and said, "I would love to be your friend, mole. And I will tell you about the things I see and taste. But I promise I will never taste you again. You are not food, you are a friend."

The mole thanked Lily and said, "You are very wise, Lily. And you have learned a valuable lesson. You should never taste something or someone without asking first. You might hurt them or yourself. You should always respect and care for other living things. They have feelings and needs too."

Lily agreed and said, "You are right, mole. I have learned a lesson. And I have gained a friend. Thank you, mole."

They hugged and said goodbye. Lily went back to her house and the mole went back to his hole. They were both happy and looked forward to seeing each other again.

The comet said, "Thank you. Let's play until the sun comes up. But remember, you have to be quiet and respectful of the other stars. They are sleeping."

Lily and Max said, "Okay, we will be quiet and respectful. We are glad you are our friend."

The comet said, "I am glad you are my friends too. Let's play."

Lily and Max played with the comet all night. They matched the comet with different stars and learned their names. They had a lot of fun and learned a lot. They thanked the comet for playing with them and said goodbye. The comet said goodbye and flew away.

Lily and Max went back to their mom. They told her about the comet and how playful and kind it was. Their mom was proud of them. She said, "You are very lucky to see a comet and play with it. Comets are rare and special. You are also very smart and polite. You did your homework and brushed your teeth. You were quiet and respectful of the stars. You are good children. I love you."

Lily and Max hugged their mom. They said, "We love you too, mom. Thank you for letting us stay up late and watch the comet. It was the best night ever."

The moral of the story is: If you are curious and eager to learn, you can discover amazing things in the world. If you are friendly and respectful, you can make new friends and have fun. If you are responsible and obedient, you can earn trust and love.

Sam and Mia were playing with their toys in their room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were cars, planes, or animals. They did not hear their mom calling them to come downstairs for lunch.

Suddenly, the floor shook and the toys fell off the shelves. Sam and Mia were scared and hugged each other. They heard a loud boom and saw cracks on the wall. It was an earthquake!

"Sam, Mia, are you okay?" their mom shouted from downstairs. She ran up the stairs and opened the door. She saw her children crying and hugged them. "Don't worry, we are safe. Let's go outside and see if anyone needs help."

They followed their mom outside and saw a lot of people on the street. Some were crying, some were helping, some were looking for their families. They saw a house that was broken and on fire. They saw a man lying on the ground, not moving. He was dead.

"Mom, what happened to him?" Mia asked, pointing at the man.

"He was hurt by the earthquake and he could not breathe. He is not alive anymore. He is in heaven now." their mom said, trying to explain.

"Can we help him?" Sam asked, feeling sad.

"No, we can't. But we can help others who are still alive. We can share our food, water, and toys with them. We can be kind and friendly. We can say thank you and sorry. We can pray for them." their mom said, smiling.

Sam and Mia nodded and followed their mom. They saw a girl who was crying and gave her a teddy bear. They saw a boy who was thirsty and gave him a bottle of water. They saw a lady who was hurt and said sorry. They saw a man who was helping and said thank you. They saw a family who was praying and joined them.

They learned that even when bad things happen, they can still be good and helpful. They learned that life is precious and they should be grateful. They learned that love is stronger than fear. They learned that they can surprise others with kindness.

"No, Sam, that is not for us. That is for the truck man. He is doing his job. Come on, let's go to the swings." Lily said.

But Sam did not listen. He ran to the truck when the truck man was not looking. He grabbed the hose and tried to spray the water. But the hose was too heavy and hard for Sam. He could not control it. The water went everywhere. It sprayed the truck man, the plants, the grass, and the coal.

The coal was in a pile next to the truck. It was black and dirty. The water made it wet and muddy. The coal splashed on Sam, Lily, and the truck man. They all got very dirty.

"Hey, what are you doing, kid?" The truck man shouted. He was angry and wet. He took the hose from Sam and turned it off. "You should not touch my hose. You made a big mess. You sprayed my coal. That is for the fire station. They need it to make fire and heat."

Sam was scared and sorry. He did not mean to make trouble. He just wanted to have fun. He looked at Lily. She was also dirty and wet. She was not happy with Sam. She was shaking her head.

"I'm sorry, truck man. I'm sorry, Lily. I was not brave. I was silly. I should have listened to you. Can you forgive me?" Sam said.

The truck man sighed. He was not so angry anymore. He saw that Sam was young and curious. He decided to be kind.

"It's okay, kid. I forgive you. But you have to be more careful next time. The hose is not a toy. It is a tool. And the coal is not for playing. It is for fire and heat. Do you understand?" He said.

Sam nodded. He understood. He learned his lesson. He thanked the truck man and said sorry again. He went to Lily and hugged her. He said sorry to her too. He asked her to be his friend again.

Lily smiled. She was not mad at Sam anymore. She knew that he was sorry. She hugged him back. She said that he was still her friend. She said that he was brave to say sorry.

They both went to the swings. They had fun. They forgot about the water and the coal. They were happy. They were friends.

Her mom was surprised and smiled. She said "Wow, Anna, you are a very spooky ghost! I love your costume. How did you design it?"

Anna told her mom how she used the sheet and the scissors. She said "It was easy and fun. Do you want to be a ghost too?"

Her mom said "Sure, why not? Let's find another sheet and design a costume for me. Then we can be ghost buddies and scare dad when he comes home."

Anna was happy. She and her mom went to find another sheet. They cut holes for their eyes and put the sheets over their heads. They were both scary ghosts. They felt the sheets. They were soft and cozy. They hugged each other and said "Boo!" and laughed.

"Let's have cheese and grapes," Mia said.

"OK," Ben said. "But I also want celery. I like celery. It is crunchy and green."

Mia did not like celery. She thought it was yucky and bitter. But she did not want to make Ben sad. She was a helpful sister. She said, "OK, you can have celery too. But I will not have any."

Ben smiled. He took the cheese, the grapes, and the celery out of the fridge. He put them on a plate. He gave some cheese and grapes to Mia. He took some cheese and grapes for himself. He also took a big piece of celery.

He bit the celery. He made a loud crunch. He smiled. He liked the celery. He bit it again. He made another loud crunch.

But then he stopped smiling. He felt something in his mouth. Something that was not celery. Something that was small and black and had legs.

He looked at the celery. He saw a bug. A bug was on the celery. A bug was in his mouth.

He panicked. He spat out the bug. He spat out the celery. He screamed. He dropped the plate. He ran to the sink. He washed his mouth. He cried.

Mia heard him scream. She saw the bug. She saw the celery. She saw the mess. She was scared. She did not know what to do.

She ran to Ben. She hugged him. She said, "It's OK, Ben. It's OK. It was just a bug. It can't hurt you. You are brave. You are strong. I am here. I will help you."

Ben hugged her back. He calmed down. He said, "Thank you, Mia. Thank you. You are a helpful sister. You are a good sister. I love you."

They cleaned up the mess. They threw away the celery. They ate the cheese and the grapes. They were happy. They did not want celery anymore.
