"Can we look at them?" Sara wonders.

"Maybe, but we have to be careful. Dad does not like us to touch his things," Ben says.

They pick up a file and open it. They see some numbers and graphs. They do not understand what they mean.

"This is boring," Sara says. "Let's find something more fun."

They put the file back and look around. They see a phone on a desk. It has many buttons and a cord.

"What is this?" Sara asks.

"It is a phone. You can talk to people with it," Ben says.

"Can we try it?" Sara asks.

"Maybe, but we have to be quiet. Dad does not like us to make noise," Ben says.

They pick up the phone and press a button. The phone makes a sound.

"Ring, ring, ring," the phone says.

"Hello, who is this?" a voice says from the phone.

Sara and Ben are surprised. They do not know who is talking.

"Uh, hi, we are Sara and Ben," Sara says.

"Hi, Sara and Ben. Where are you calling from?" the voice says.

"We are in dad's office. He is not here," Ben says.

"Dad's office? Who is your dad?" the voice says.

"Dad is Mr. Smith. He works here," Sara says.

"Mr. Smith? I am his boss. Why are you in his office?" the voice says.

Sara and Ben are scared. They think they are in trouble.

"Uh, we are sorry. We were just looking around. We did not mean to bother you," Ben says.

"You should not be in his office without his permission. You could damage his files or his phone. Where is he?" the voice says.

"He is at home. He is sick," Sara says.

"He is sick? Why did he not tell me? He has an important meeting today," the voice says.

Sara and Ben do not know what to say. They wish they did not touch the phone.

"Uh, we have to go. Bye," Sara says.

They hang up the phone and run out of the office. They decide to never be so adventurous again.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. But then Lily saw a shiny red car on the shelf. She wanted to play with it, so she climbed on the sofa and reached for it.

"Hey, that's my car!" Tom shouted. "Give it back to me!"

"No, it's mine now!" Lily said. She pulled the car and ran away.

Tom was very angry. He chased after Lily and tried to grab the car. They both tugged and pulled until the car broke in half. They heard a loud snap and saw pieces of plastic flying everywhere.

They stopped and looked at the broken car. They felt very sad and sorry. They knew they had done something bad.

"Mommy, mommy, we broke the car!" they cried.

Mommy came and saw the mess. She was not happy. She asked them what happened and why they were fighting.

"We wanted to play with the car, but we couldn't share it," Lily said.

"We were selfish and greedy, and we ruined the car," Tom said.

Mommy sighed. She told them that the car was a gift from their grandpa, who loved them very much. She said that the car was very special and hard to find. She said that they had hurt their grandpa's feelings by breaking his car.

Lily and Tom felt very bad. They wished they could fix the car and make their grandpa happy again.

"Mommy, is there a way to restore the car?" Lily asked.

"Restore means to make something good again, like it was before," Mommy explained.

"Yes, is there a way to do that?" Tom asked.

Mommy thought for a moment. She said that maybe they could try to glue the pieces together, but it would not be easy. She said that they would need to be very careful and patient. She said that they would also need to apologize to their grandpa and tell him the truth.

Lily and Tom agreed. They said they were sorry to Mommy and asked for her help. They worked together to restore the car as best as they could. They used glue and tape and stickers to make it look nice. They wrote a card for their grandpa and said they were sorry and that they loved him.

They gave the car and the card to their grandpa the next day. He was surprised and touched. He hugged them and thanked them. He said he was proud of them for being honest and for trying to restore the car. He said he forgave them and that he still loved them.

Lily and Tom were very happy. They learned their lesson. They learned to share and to care for their things. They learned that restore is a good word and a good thing to do. They learned that they could restore not only things, but also feelings. They learned that they could restore their grandpa's smile.

All the chickens woke up and saw the fox trying to break through the door. They all started to panic and run around. But Red was not afraid. He stood his ground and faced the fox. The fox was scared of Red's powerful crow and ran away.

The other chickens were amazed at how brave Red was. They all thanked him for saving them from the fox. From that day on, they all learned that being brave and standing up to bullies can make a big difference.

Max was so happy that he hugged Ellie and said, "Thank you, Ellie! You are the best elephant in the jungle!" Ellie smiled and replied, "No problem, Max. Helping friends is what friends do." From that day on, Max and Ellie became the best of friends and went on many adventures together.

After playing for a while, Timmy and his mom sat down on a bench to rest. Timmy looked up at the sky and saw the clouds moving. He said, "Look, the clouds are moving like a big ship!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, nature is full of wonderful things to see." Timmy agreed and felt happy to be outside in nature with his mom.

"Let's play hide and seek, Anna," Ben says.

"OK, Ben," Anna says. "You count and I hide."

Ben covers his eyes and counts. "One, two, three, four, five..."

Anna runs to the cupboard and opens the door. She sees a dark space. She thinks it is a good hiding place. She crawls into the cupboard and closes the door behind her.

"Ready or not, here I come!" Ben says. He looks for Anna. He looks under the bed, behind the curtains, in the closet. He does not find her.

"Where are you, Anna?" Ben says. "I can't find you!"

Anna hears Ben. She wants to say something, but she can't. She is stuck in the cupboard. The door is locked. She does not know how to open it. She is scared. She cries.

"Help, Ben! Help, mom!" Anna says. "I'm in the cupboard!"

Ben hears Anna. He runs to the cupboard and tries to open the door. He can't. He pushes and pulls, but the door does not move. He is worried. He does not know what to do.

"Anna, don't cry," Ben says. "I'll get mom. She'll help you. She is dependable. She always helps us."

Ben runs to the kitchen and finds mom. He tells her what happened. Mom follows him to the room. She sees the cupboard and the locked door. She takes a key from her pocket and unlocks the door. She opens the door and sees Anna. Anna is still crying.

"Anna, it's OK," mom says. "You're safe now. I'm here."

Mom hugs Anna and kisses her. She takes her out of the cupboard and holds her. Anna stops crying and smiles. She is happy to see mom.

"Thank you, mom," Anna says. "You're the best."

Mom smiles and says, "You're welcome, Anna. I love you."

She looks at Ben and says, "And thank you, Ben. You're a good brother. You're dependable. You helped Anna."

Ben smiles and says, "You're welcome, mom. I love you too."

Mom hugs Ben and kisses him. She says, "I love you both. You're my good children."

Anna and Ben hug mom and say, "We love you, mom. You're our dependable mom."

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they would miss the ball and fall down, but they would laugh and get up again.

One day, an elderly man came to the park with his dog. The dog was big and furry, and it barked loudly. Lily and Ben were scared of the dog, and they ran away from it. The elderly man saw them and called out, "Don't be afraid, children. He is a friendly dog. He just wants to play with you."

Lily and Ben stopped and looked at the man. He smiled and winked at them. He said, "His name is Rex. He likes to chase balls. Do you want to play with him?"

Lily and Ben nodded, but they were still nervous. They held each other's hands and walked slowly towards the man and the dog. Rex wagged his tail and licked their faces. Lily and Ben giggled and petted him.

They decided to share their ball with Rex. They threw the ball and Rex ran after it. He brought it back and dropped it at their feet. They threw it again and again, and Rex never got tired. Lily and Ben had fun with Rex and the elderly man. They forgot to be scared and they screamed with joy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to explore. One day, they found a bridge over a stream in the park. They wanted to see what was under the bridge.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. He ran to the bridge and looked down.

"Wait, Ben!" Lily said. She followed him slowly. She was a little scared.

They saw some rocks, some fish, and some plants under the bridge. They also saw something interesting. It was a big, green frog sitting on a leaf.

"Wow, look at that frog!" Ben said. He pointed at it.

"It's so big and green!" Lily said. She smiled.

They both leaned over the bridge to get a closer look. The frog looked at them with its big, round eyes.

"Hello, frog!" Ben said. He waved at it.

"Hello, frog!" Lily said. She waved too.

The frog did not say anything. It just blinked.

Ben had an idea. He wanted to make the frog talk.

"Maybe it will talk if we poke it," he said.

He reached out his hand and tried to poke the frog.

"Ben, no!" Lily said. She grabbed his hand. "That's not nice! The frog might get angry!"

But it was too late. Ben poked the frog. The frog did not like it. It opened its mouth and croaked loudly.

"Ribbit! Ribbit!" The frog said.

Lily and Ben were surprised. They jumped back.

The frog was angry. It jumped off the leaf and splashed into the water.

"Oops!" Ben said. He looked sorry.

"Sorry, frog!" Lily said. She looked sorry too.

They watched the frog swim away under the bridge.

They learned a lesson. They should not poke frogs. They should be nice to animals.

They decided to leave the bridge and find something else to explore. They hoped the frog would forgive them.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mom. Lily put on Mom's apron and Tom got the eggs and flour. They mixed everything in a big bowl.

"Shake, shake, shake!" Lily said, shaking the bowl. "This is how you make a cake!"

"No, no, no!" Tom said, grabbing the bowl. "You have to stir, stir, stir! Shaking will make a mess!"

They pulled and tugged on the bowl. It slipped from their hands and fell on the floor. The bowl broke and the cake mix splashed everywhere.

"Oh no!" Lily and Tom cried. "We broke the bowl and the cake! And Mom's apron is dirty!"

They heard Mom coming. They hid under the table. Mom saw the mess and gasped.

"What happened here?" Mom asked. "Who did this?"

Lily and Tom peeked out. They felt sorry and scared.

"We did, Mom," Lily said. "We wanted to make a cake for you, but we broke the bowl and the cake. And your apron. We are sorry, Mom."

Mom sighed. She was angry, but she also loved them. She knelt down and hugged them.

"Thank you for wanting to make a cake for me, but you should have asked me first," Mom said. "Making a cake is not easy. You need to follow a recipe and use the right tools. And you need to be careful and clean. Shaking a bowl is not a good idea."

"We know, Mom," Tom said. "We learned our lesson. Can we help you clean up?"

"Yes, you can," Mom said. "And maybe later, we can make a cake together. A real cake. How does that sound?"

Lily and Tom smiled. They said, "That sounds great, Mom. We love you, Mom."

They got up and helped Mom clean up the mess. They threw away the broken bowl and the cake mix. They washed Mom's apron and the floor. They learned how to make a cake the right way. And they had a happy day.

After a while, Lily got tired. She said to the shadow, "I want to go home now." The shadow nodded and followed her home. Lily and the shadow became best friends and played together every day.

Tim wanted to read the book, but his sister, Sue, wanted to play with him. Sue said, "Tim, I want to play. Please put the book down." Tim did not want to stop reading the book. He said, "Sue, I want to read this book. It is rare and about history."

Sue did not like that Tim did not want to play with her. She was sad and a little mad. But then, she had an idea. She said, "Tim, let's play a game about history. You can teach me what you learn from the book." Tim thought it was a good idea. They played the game and had a lot of fun. Tim and Sue were happy, and they both learned about history together.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. The cat was spinning around and around. The dog laughed and said, "You spin so fast!"

The cat stopped spinning and saw a cup of tea on the ground. The tea was filthy because it was near the trash. The cat said, "I want to drink the tea." The dog said, "No, it's dirty. Don't drink it."

But the cat didn't listen. He drank the filthy tea. The cat felt very sick. The dog said, "I told you not to drink it." The cat was sad and sick, and they couldn't play anymore.

Before they left, Tim's mom said, "Tim, you must drink some water before we go." Tim drank the water, but he was too excited to think about why his mom told him to do that. They all got in the car and drove to the park where the fireworks would be.

At the park, Tim and his family found a good spot to sit. The sky was getting dark, and the fireworks would start soon. Tim started to feel thirsty. He said, "Mom, I need more water." His mom smiled and said, "I knew you would be thirsty, so I brought more water for you to drink." Tim drank the water and felt better. Then, the fireworks started, and Tim was so happy. He knew his mom was very smart to make sure he had water to drink.

They put the bird in a glass box and took care of it. Every day, Amy and her mom would feed the bird and talk to it. The bird started to feel better and its wing got stronger.

One day, the bird was flying around in the glass box. Amy knew it was time to let the bird go. She opened the box and the bird flew out, happy and free. Amy felt happy too, because she helped the poor bird get better.

Amy looked under her bed and found five toy cars. She counted them: one, two, three, four, five. But no key was there. Then, she looked inside her toy box. She found three dolls and counted them: one, two, three. Still, she did not find the key.

Finally, Amy looked inside her book bag. She found an easy book she liked to read. She also found a small key! Amy was so happy. She used the key to open the mystery box. Inside the box, she found a beautiful toy castle. Amy played with her new toy all day long.

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a gentle cat named Sam. Sam loved to play with his ball. One day, he saw a long line of ants. They were walking in a straight line, carrying little bits of food.

Sam was very curious. He went to his friend, the wise old owl, and asked, "Why do the ants walk in a line like that?" The owl said, "The ants are showing each other where the food is. They help each other by making a line."

The next day, Sam saw a big, juicy apple on a tree. He wanted to show his friends where it was. So, he remembered what the owl had told him. He made a line with his ball, just like the ants. His friends followed the line and found the apple.

Sam and his friends were happy. They learned that helping each other and showing the way can make things easier for everyone. From that day on, they always tried to help each other, just like the ants in the line.

"Look, Bunny, so many acorns!" Squirrel said. "We can eat them when we are hungry."

"Yes, Squirrel, they look yummy!" Bunny said. "But we should not take too many. Maybe some other animals need them too."

They each took a few acorns and put them in their baskets. Then they heard a loud voice behind them.

"Hey, you two, stop right there!" It was Fox, who was very naughty and greedy. He wanted to own all the acorns for himself. "Those are my acorns! I found them first! Give them back to me!"

Bunny and Squirrel were scared of Fox. They did not want to fight with him. They tried to run away, but Fox was faster. He caught up with them and snatched their baskets.

"Ha ha ha, now I have all the acorns!" Fox said. "You can't have any! Go away!"

But then, they heard another voice above them.

"Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!" It was Owl, who was very wise and kind. He saw what Fox did and wanted to help Bunny and Squirrel. He flew down and landed on Fox's head.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" Fox said. "What are you doing, Owl? Get off me!"

"Fox, you are very naughty and greedy!" Owl said. "You should not take all the acorns for yourself. You should share with Bunny and Squirrel. They are your friends, not your enemies."

"But they are mine, mine, mine!" Fox said. "I found them first! I own them!"

"No, you don't, Fox!" Owl said. "The acorns belong to the tree, not to you. The tree gives them to all the animals, not just to you. You should be thankful and generous, not selfish and mean."

Owl was right. Fox felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he was wrong. He gave back the baskets to Bunny and Squirrel.

"I'm sorry, Bunny and Squirrel," Fox said. "I was very naughty and greedy. Please forgive me. Can we be friends?"

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They also liked to eat grapes that grew on a big vine near the fence. One day, they saw a man in a shiny car stop by the vine. He was wealthy and wore a nice suit. He smiled at them and said, "Hello, children. Do you like grapes? I have a lot of them in my car. Do you want some?"

Anna and Ben were curious and hungry. They nodded and followed the man to his car. He opened the trunk and showed them a big basket of grapes. They looked juicy and sweet. The man said, "You can have as many as you want. But first, you have to do something for me. You see this cut on my hand? It hurts a lot. Can you heal it for me?"

Anna and Ben were confused. They did not know how to heal a cut. They only knew how to put a band-aid on it. The man said, "It's easy. You just have to kiss it. That's how my mommy used to heal my cuts when I was little. Come on, don't be shy. It will only take a second."

Anna and Ben felt uneasy. They did not like the idea of kissing a stranger's hand. They wanted to go back to the park. But they also wanted the grapes. They looked at each other and decided to do it. They each gave the man a quick kiss on his cut. The man laughed and said, "Thank you, children. You are very kind. Now you can have your grapes."

He handed them each a bunch of grapes and closed the trunk. He said, "Enjoy your grapes. And don't tell anyone about our little secret, okay?" He got in his car and drove away. Anna and Ben ran back to the park and ate their grapes. They tasted sour and bitter. They felt sick and dizzy. They did not know that the man had poisoned the grapes. They did not know that he was a bad man who liked to hurt children. They did not know that they would never see their parents again. They did not know that they had made a big mistake.

Lily and Ben were playing with their dolls in the living room. Lily had a pink doll with long hair and a dress. Ben had a blue doll with short hair and a hat. They pretended that their dolls were friends and went on adventures together.

But then Ben got bored and wanted to play something else. He said to Lily, "Let's play cars. Cars are more fun than dolls. Dolls are for babies."

Lily did not like that. She loved her doll and did not want to play cars. She said to Ben, "No, I don't want to play cars. Cars are loud and dirty. Dolls are pretty and nice. You are mean."

Ben got angry and grabbed Lily's doll. He said, "Give me your doll. I will make her drive a car. She will like it better than your dress."

Lily got scared and tried to hold on to her doll. She said, "No, don't take my doll. She is mine. Leave her alone."

But Ben was stronger and pulled the doll away from Lily. He laughed and said, "Ha ha, I got your doll. Now she is mine. I will cut her hair and rip her dress."

Lily was very sad and angry. She cried and shouted, "No, no, no. Give her back. You are a bad brother. You are a bully."

She ran to Ben and slapped him on the neck. Ben was surprised and hurt. He dropped the doll and said, "Ow, ow, ow. Why did you slap me? That hurts."

Lily picked up her doll and hugged her. She said, "You hurt my doll. You hurt me. You are not nice. I don't want to play with you."

She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom was not happy. She said to Ben, "Ben, you were very rude and mean to your sister. You should not take her doll or make fun of her. You should say sorry and share your toys."

Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He said to Lily, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not have taken your doll or said those things. Can we be friends again?"

Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sincere. She said, "OK, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to be nice to my doll and me. And we can play both dolls and cars."

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "OK, Lily. I will be nice to your doll and you. And we can play both dolls and cars."

They hugged and made up. Their mom was proud of them. She said, "That's good, kids. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now you can play nicely together."

They went back to the living room and played with their dolls and cars. They had fun and did not fight anymore. They were happy.

Sara and Tom are playing in the kitchen. They want to cook a cake for Mom. They have flour, eggs, milk and sugar. They mix everything in a big bowl. They are very happy.

"Look, Tom, we are making a cake!" Sara says.

"Yes, Sara, Mom will love it!" Tom says.

They pour the batter in a pan and put it in the oven. They set the timer for 20 minutes. They wait and wait. They sing a song.

But then they hear a loud noise. BOOM! The oven makes a big noise. Smoke comes out. The cake is burned. Sara and Tom are scared. They run to the living room.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the kitchen. She sees the mess. She is angry. She turns off the oven and opens the window. She coughs.

"What did you do?" Mom asks.

"We wanted to cook a cake for you, Mom," Sara says.

"We are sorry, Mom," Tom says.

Mom looks at Sara and Tom. They are sad. They have tears in their eyes. Mom feels sorry for them. She hugs them.

"It's okay, Sara and Tom. I know you wanted to make me happy. But you should never play with the oven. It is dangerous. You could get hurt. Next time, ask me first, okay?" Mom says.

"Okay, Mom," Sara and Tom say.

Mom smiles. She says, "How about we make a new cake together? I have some chocolate and sprinkles. Do you like that?"

"Yes, Mom, we like that!" Sara and Tom say.

They go back to the kitchen. They wash their hands. They cook a new cake with Mom. They have fun. They are happy.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the farm with their dad. One day, they see a new animal in the barn. It is a mule. A mule is like a horse, but with big ears and a loud voice.

"Hello, mule!" Ben says. "What is your name?"

The mule does not answer. He just makes a noise. "Hee-haw! Hee-haw!"

Sam laughs. "He sounds funny. Can we ride him, dad?"

Dad shakes his head. "No, boys. The mule is not for riding. He is for working. He is very strong. He can pull heavy things and carry big loads. He helps us in the farm."

Ben and Sam are curious. They want to see the mule work. They follow dad and the mule to the field. There, the mule pulls a plow. The plow makes a line in the dirt. Dad plants seeds in the line. The mule walks and walks, making more lines and more seeds.

Ben and Sam clap their hands. "Wow, mule! You are very good!" they say.

The mule stops and looks at them. He wags his tail and makes a noise. "Hee-haw! Hee-haw!"

Ben and Sam think the mule is happy. They want to make him happier. They run to the pond. They fill their buckets with water. They come back to the mule. They splash the water on the mule.

The mule is surprised. He feels the water on his fur. He shakes his head and makes a noise. "Hee-haw! Hee-haw!"

Ben and Sam laugh. They splash more water on the mule. The mule splashes back with his hoofs. The water flies in the air. It lands on Ben and Sam and dad.

Ben and Sam and dad and the mule are wet. They are also happy. They smile and make noises. "Hee-haw! Hee-haw!"

Lily and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a big teddy bear and Tom had a small car.

But then, their nosy cousin Sam came to visit. He wanted to join their game, but he did not ask nicely. He just grabbed Lily's teddy bear and said, "This is mine now. You can have my car. It is better."

Lily was very sad and angry. She did not want to give up her teddy bear. She loved it very much. She said, "No, Sam. That is not fair. Give me back my teddy bear. It is mine."

Tom was also upset. He did not like Sam's car. It was old and broken. He said, "No, Sam. That is not nice. You cannot take Lily's teddy bear. It is hers."

But Sam did not listen. He laughed and ran away with the teddy bear. He said, "Too bad. I am faster and stronger. You cannot catch me."

Lily and Tom chased after him. They wanted to get their toys back. They ran through the house, but Sam was too quick. He went outside and hid behind a tree.

It was very cold outside. The wind was blowing and the snow was falling. Lily and Tom did not have their coats or hats. They shivered and sneezed. They looked for Sam, but they could not find him.

They heard a voice from behind the tree. It was Sam. He said, "Ha ha. I am here. You cannot see me. You are too slow and silly."

Lily and Tom were very angry. They did not like Sam's mean words. They said, "Sam, you are very rude and selfish. You do not know how to share or play. You do not include us in your game. You make us feel bad."

They decided to ignore Sam. They did not want to play with him anymore. They went back inside the house. They found their mom and dad. They told them what Sam did. They asked them for a hug and a cup of hot chocolate.

Mom and dad were very sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Lily and Tom. Sam was very wrong. He should not have taken your toys or teased you. He should have been kind and friendly. He should have included you in his game. He should have said sorry."

They hugged Lily and Tom and gave them hot chocolate. They said, "We love you, Lily and Tom. You are very good and sweet. You know how to share and play. You include others in your game. You make us feel happy."

Lily and Tom smiled and said, "We love you, mom and dad. You are very nice and warm. You know how to care and help. You include us in your hug. You make us feel cozy."

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with their wagon. They put their toys in the wagon and pull it around the yard. They have fun.

One day, a big dog comes to the yard. The dog is not mean, but he is curious. He sees the wagon and thinks it is a toy. He runs to the wagon and grabs it with his teeth. He pulls the wagon away from Tom and Lily.

"Hey, that is our wagon!" Tom shouts. "Give it back!"

Lily is scared of the dog. She cries. "Go away, dog! Leave our wagon alone!"

The dog does not listen. He runs with the wagon to the other side of the yard. He shakes the wagon and makes the toys fall out. He chews on the toys and breaks them.

Tom and Lily are sad. They lose their wagon and their toys. They do not know what to do.

Then, they see their mom. She comes to the yard and sees the dog and the wagon. She is not happy.

"Bad dog! Drop the wagon!" she says. She claps her hands and makes a loud noise. The dog is scared. He drops the wagon and runs away.

Mom picks up the wagon and the toys. She brings them to Tom and Lily. She hugs them and says, "I'm sorry, kids. The dog was naughty. He did not know the wagon was yours. He thought it was a bone. Are you okay?"

Tom and Lily nod. They are okay. They are glad mom is here. They thank mom for saving their wagon.

Mom smiles. She says, "You're welcome, kids. I'm proud of you. You are brave and healthy. You did not get hurt by the dog. But next time, be careful. Do not leave your wagon outside. Put it in the garage when you are done playing. Okay?"

Tom and Lily say, "Okay, mom." They listen to mom. They put their wagon in the garage. They go inside and have a snack. They are happy. They still have their wagon and each other. They are friends.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved candy. They liked to eat candy every day after lunch. But their mom said they could only have one piece each. She said too much candy was bad for their teeth and tummy.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a big jar of candy on the kitchen table. It was shiny and colorful and looked very yummy. They wanted to eat some, but their mom was not there. She had gone to the store to buy some milk.

"Let's eat some candy," Tom said to Lily. "Mom won't know."

"No, we can't," Lily said. "Mom said only one piece. And this candy is not ours. It is dangerous."

"Dangerous? How?" Tom asked. He did not believe Lily. He thought she was scared.

Lily pointed to a small label on the jar. It had some words and a picture of a skull. She could not read the words, but she knew the skull meant bad.

"It means this candy can make you sick or hurt you," Lily said. "It is not for kids. It is for grown-ups who need medicine."

Tom looked at the label and the candy. He felt curious and hungry. He did not think the candy could be so bad. He thought Lily was silly.

"I don't care," Tom said. "I want to try it. It looks good."

He reached for the jar and opened it. He grabbed a handful of candy and put it in his mouth.

Lily gasped. She tried to stop him, but it was too late. Tom had eaten the candy.

Tom felt a strange taste in his mouth. It was not sweet or sour or fruity. It was bitter and spicy and yucky. He felt his tongue burn and his throat itch. He felt his eyes water and his nose run. He felt his stomach ache and his head spin. He felt very sick.

He spit out the candy and cried. He wished he had listened to Lily. He wished he had not eaten the candy.

Lily ran to him and hugged him. She was scared and sorry. She wanted to help him.

She saw the phone on the counter. She remembered her mom had taught her how to call for help. She picked up the phone and dialed 911. She told the operator what had happened. She said her name and address and asked for an ambulance.

She stayed with Tom and waited for the ambulance. She hoped Tom would be okay. She hoped their mom would not be mad. She hoped they would never eat dangerous candy again.

Lily was a small girl who liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but her favorite was a teddy bear that her grandma gave her. She always hugged her teddy bear and took it with her everywhere. She named it Brownie, because it was brown and soft.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. It was a sunny day in the spring season, and the flowers were blooming. Lily brought Brownie with her and put him on a bench while she ran to the swings. She was having fun, but she did not see a big dog that came near the bench. The dog sniffed Brownie and thought it was a real bear. It grabbed Brownie with its teeth and ran away.

Lily heard a loud bark and turned around. She saw the dog running with Brownie in its mouth. She screamed and ran after the dog. "Stop! Stop! That's my teddy bear! Give it back!" she cried. Her mom heard her and followed her.

The dog was faster than Lily and her mom. It ran across the street and into a yard. Lily and her mom stopped at the gate. They saw the dog drop Brownie on the grass and start to chew on it. Lily felt tears in her eyes. She thought she would never see Brownie again.

But then, a boy came out of the house. He saw the dog and the teddy bear. He recognized the dog as his neighbor's. He shouted at the dog. "Hey! Bad dog! Leave that teddy bear alone!" He ran to the dog and took Brownie from its mouth. He looked at Brownie and saw that it was torn and dirty. He felt sorry for Lily. He walked to the gate and gave Brownie to Lily. "I'm sorry, this is your teddy bear, right?" he said. "The dog didn't mean to hurt it. He thought it was a real bear. He likes bears."

Lily took Brownie and hugged it. She was happy to have it back, even if it was damaged. She smiled at the boy and said, "Thank you, you are very kind. Yes, this is my teddy bear. His name is Brownie. He is very special to me. My grandma gave him to me. I value him a lot."

The boy smiled back and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you value him. He is a nice teddy bear. My name is Tom. Do you want to be my friend?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I want to be your friend. My name is Lily. Do you want to play with me and Brownie?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I want to play with you and Brownie. Do you like swings?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I like swings. Do you?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I like swings too. Come on, let's go to the swings."

Lily and Tom held hands and ran to the swings. They played together and had fun. They became good friends. Lily learned that sometimes bad things can lead to good things. She also learned to value her friends as much as her toys. She and Tom played together every season, and Brownie was always with them.

Lily and Tom gasped. They had forgotten that today was their birthday. They were twins and they were turning four. They hugged Mom and Dad and said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

Lily and Tom had the best birthday ever. They were very happy. They loved their Mom and Dad. They loved their picnic. They loved their surprise. They loved each other.

Zara is a zebra who likes to run and play with her friends. She likes to eat green grass and drink water from the pond. She likes to make stripes with her black and white fur.

One day, Zara is very tired after running and playing. She wants to sleep, but she cannot find a good place to sleep. The grass is too wet, the pond is too noisy, and the trees are too hard. She looks for a dry place to sleep.

She sees a big rock that is warm and dry. She thinks it is a good place to sleep. She walks to the rock and lies down. She closes her eyes and starts to sleep.

But the rock is not a rock. It is a lion who is also sleeping. The lion feels Zara on his back and wakes up. He is angry and hungry. He roars and tries to bite Zara.

Zara is scared and jumps off the lion. She runs away as fast as she can. She hears the lion chasing her. She looks for her friends to help her.

She sees them near the pond. She calls to them. "Help! Help! A lion is after me!"

Her friends hear her and run to her. They see the lion behind her. They make a circle around Zara and kick the lion with their hoofs. The lion is hurt and runs away.

Zara is safe and happy. She thanks her friends for saving her. They hug her and tell her they are glad she is okay. They invite her to sleep with them near the pond. They say there is enough dry grass for everyone.

Zara agrees and follows them. She finds a cozy spot next to her best friend. She lies down and cuddles with her friend. She feels warm and dry. She closes her eyes and sleeps. She dreams of stripes and grass and water. She is happy.

"Tim, Lily, what did you do?" she asked. "You broke my bird. It was a gift from grandma. It was very special and beautiful. How could you do this?"

She knew they did not mean to break the bird. She knew they tried to restore the bird. She knew they wanted to make her happy again.

"Ben, that's not nice. You made Anna cry. You shouldn't tease her like that. You should say sorry," mom says.

Ben stops laughing. He sees Anna's tears. He feels bad. He didn't mean to hurt her. He loves his sister.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I was just joking. I didn't want to make you cry. Here, you can have some of my cream. I'll share with you," Ben says.

He gives Anna his cone. He hugs her. Anna stops crying. She smiles. She takes a lick of his cream. She likes it.

"Thank you, Ben. You're a good brother. I forgive you. Your cream is good, too. I'll share with you, too," Anna says.

She gives Ben her cone. He takes a lick of her cream. He likes it, too.

They share their cream and their cones. They hug again. They are happy.

Mom and dad watch them. They are proud of them. They love them. They take them to the swings. They have fun. They are a family.

Lily tried to believe him, but she was still nervous. She heard some noises in the dark. She thought they were alligators. She hugged her teddy bear and whispered to Ben.

One day, he saw a shiny white bone on the ground. He wondered who left it there. He bounced over to it and picked it up. It was hard and smooth and heavy. He thought it was a very expensive bone. He wanted to keep it for himself.

He bounced back to his ball with the bone in his hand. He tried to bounce with both, but it was hard. The bone was too big and too heavy. He bounced slower and lower and quieter. He bounced so low that he could not see the birds and the clouds. He bounced so slow that he could not feel the wind in his hair. He bounced so quiet that he could not hear his own laugh.

He heard a loud bark behind him. He turned around and saw a big black dog. The dog was angry and hungry. The dog wanted the bone. The dog ran towards him and jumped on him. The dog bit his hand and took the bone. The dog ran away with the bone.

Sara and Ben are playing with their dolls in the garden. They have a tea party with water and cookies. Sara pours water for Ben and his doll, but she spills some on the grass.

"Oh no, the grass is wet!" Sara says. "We have to dry it!"

Ben looks at Sara and shakes his head. "No, we don't. The sun will dry it. That is the law of nature."

Sara is confused. She does not know what nature is, or what a law is. She thinks Ben is making up words.

"What is nature? What is a law?" she asks.

Ben tries to explain, but he does not know much either. He only heard his dad say those words once.

"Nature is everything outside, like the sky, the trees, the flowers, the bugs. A law is a rule that you have to follow, or you get in trouble. The sun is the boss of nature, and it makes the law that water goes away when it is hot."

Sara thinks for a moment. She does not like rules, or getting in trouble. She likes water, and she likes to make things wet.

"I don't like the sun's law. I want to make my own law. My law is that water stays when it is cold. I will make the water cold with ice. Then the grass will be wet forever!"

She runs inside the house and gets some ice cubes from the freezer. She brings them outside and puts them on the grass. She smiles and claps her hands.

"Look, Ben, I made a new law! The water is cold and it does not go away!"

Ben looks at Sara and the ice. He does not think her law will work. He thinks the sun will melt the ice and dry the grass anyway. He thinks Sara is silly, but he does not want to hurt her feelings.

"OK, Sara, you made a new law. But I like the sun's law better. I think it is smarter and nicer. Can we play something else now?"

Sara nods and picks up her doll. She does not care if Ben likes her law or not. She is happy with her ice and her water. She thinks she is clever and brave.

They put away the tea set and the cookies. They go to the swing and take turns pushing each other. They forget about the grass and the ice. They have fun and laugh. They are friends.

Tom and Lily liked to play in the woods behind their house. They made a trail with sticks and stones to mark their way. They wanted to know how long their trail was, so they decided to measure it.

They took a long rope from the shed and tied one end to a big tree. Then they walked along the trail, holding the rope. They counted their steps as they went. "One, two, three, four, five," said Tom. "Six, seven, eight, nine, ten," said Lily.

They reached the end of the trail and tied the other end of the rope to a small bush. They looked at the rope and saw that it was very long. They were proud of their trail. They decided to go back to the tree and measure the rope.

They walked along the rope, holding a ruler. They measured the rope in inches. They added the inches as they went. "Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty," said Tom. "Sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred," said Lily.

They reached the tree and saw that the rope was one hundred inches long. They were amazed by their trail. They decided to make a sign with their names and the length of their trail. They were very organized.

They took some paper and crayons from the house and wrote on the paper: "Tom and Lily's Trail. 100 inches long." They taped the paper to the tree. They smiled at their sign. They heard their mom calling them for lunch. They ran to the house, leaving the rope and the sign behind.

Sara is still angry. She says, "I don't want to play with you anymore. You ruin everything. Go away!" She takes the paper and scissors and runs to her room. She closes the door and locks it. She says, "I will keep the paper and scissors for myself. You can't have them. They are mine!"

Ben is very sad. He knocks on the door and says, "Sara, please open the door. Please share the paper and scissors with me. Please be nice to me. I'm sorry I cut your sun. I won't do it again. I love you, Sara."

But Sara does not open the door. She does not answer. She keeps cutting and cutting. She cuts more shapes and animals and cards. But she is not happy. She misses Ben. She thinks, "Maybe I was too mean to Ben. Maybe I should share the paper and scissors with him. Maybe I should say sorry to him. He is my brother. I love him, too."

She puts down the scissors and goes to the door. She unlocks it and opens it. She sees Ben sitting on the floor. He is crying. He has no paper and no scissors. He has nothing to play with. Sara feels sorry for him. She says, "Ben, I'm sorry I was mean to you. I'm sorry I cut your moon. I'm sorry I took the paper and scissors. Will you forgive me? Will you play with me again?"

Ben looks up and sees Sara. He sees that she has a lot of paper and scissors. He sees that she has a nice smile. He wipes his tears and says, "Sara, I forgive you. I'm sorry I cut your sun. I'm sorry I made you angry. Will you share the paper and scissors with me? Will you be nice to me again?"

Sara nods and says, "Yes, Ben. I will share the paper and scissors with you. I will be nice to you again. Come on, let's play together." She gives him some paper and scissors. They hug and say, "I love you, Sara." "I love you, Ben."

They go back to the floor and start to cut. They cut shapes and animals and cards. They make a new sun and a new moon. They make a big heart and write their names on it. They have a lot of fun. They are happy. They are nice. They are friends.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the park with her mom. She saw a white dove on a tree branch and wanted to touch it. She asked her mom, "Can I touch the dove, please?"

Her mom said, "No, Mia, you can't touch the dove. It might fly away or peck you. It is not a toy, it is a living thing. You can look at it, but not touch it."

Mia was sad and angry. She did not listen to her mom. She ran to the tree and tried to grab the dove. But the dove was scared and flew away. Mia fell on the ground and hurt her knee. It was icy and cold and she started to cry.

Her mom ran to her and hugged her. She said, "I'm sorry, Mia, you hurt yourself. But you should have listened to me. The dove did not want to be touched. It wanted to be free and safe. You have to respect other animals and their feelings. Do you understand?"

Mia nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I understand. I was wrong. Can you forgive me?"

Her mom said, "Of course, I forgive you. I love you, Mia. Now let's go home and put a band-aid on your knee."

They walked home together, holding hands. Mia learned a lesson that day. She never tried to touch a dove again. She only watched them from a distance and admired their beauty.

"Help! Help!" they cried.

Then, they saw a man. The man was old and kind. He had a stick in his hand. He walked to the big dog and said, "Stop! Go away! You are not nice to the youth. You make them scared. You must remove from here."

The big dog heard the man and stopped. It looked at the man and his stick. It did not want to fight. It turned around and ran away.

"You are welcome," the man said. "I am glad you are safe. The big dog is bad. It should not come to the park. The park is for the youth, not for the big dog. You can play here and have fun."

Tom and Lily were two rabbits who lived in a big field. They liked to eat the green grass and play with their friends. Sometimes they saw a farmer who worked on the land. He had a big hat and a big dog. The rabbits were afraid of the farmer and the dog, so they hid in their holes when they came.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a big pile of carrots near the farmer's house. They were hungry and curious, so they decided to go and get some. They waited until the farmer and the dog were gone, and then they ran to the pile. They grabbed as many carrots as they could and started to eat.

"Yum, these are the best carrots ever!" Tom said.

"Yes, they are so sweet and crunchy!" Lily agreed.

They ate and ate until they were full and comfortable. They did not notice that the farmer and the dog came back. The farmer saw the rabbits eating his carrots and got very angry. He shouted and ran towards them with a stick.

"Hey, you thieves! Get away from my carrots!" he yelled.

The rabbits were scared and tried to run away. But the pile of carrots was too big and they got stuck. The farmer reached them and swung his stick. He hit Tom and Lily hard and split their heads. They fell to the ground and did not move.

The farmer picked up his carrots and put them in a basket. He did not care about the rabbits. He whistled and walked away with his dog.

"OK, Mom, we're coming," Ben said.

They turned off the engine and put the pieces back in the box. They tried to wipe off the dust from their clothes and hair, but it was too much. They looked like they had rolled in mud.

They went down the stairs and saw Mom waiting for them. She looked at them and gasped.

"What happened to you? You're covered in dust! You look like two orange monsters!" Mom said.

"Sorry, Mom, we were playing with the train set in the attic. It was very dusty there," Ben said.

"Well, you can't play with that anymore. It's too old and dirty. You need to take a bath and change your clothes right now. And then we'll have lunch," Mom said.

"OK, Mom, we're sorry," Lily said.

They followed Mom to the bathroom. They washed off the dust and put on clean clothes. They felt better and hungry.

They went to the kitchen and saw Dad waiting for them. He smiled and hugged them.

"Hello, my little orange monsters. How was your adventure in the attic?" Dad said.

"It was fun, Dad, but very dusty. We played with the train set, but Mom said we can't play with it anymore," Ben said.

"Well, maybe we can find a better place for it. Somewhere where it won't make so much dust. And maybe we can clean it and fix it. Would you like that?" Dad said.

"Yes, Dad, we would like that very much," Lily said.

They sat down and ate their lunch. They told Dad about their train game and he told them about his work. They laughed and talked and enjoyed their food.

They were happy and they forgot about the dust.

Sam thought that maybe the bubble could help him bow like the other fish. He swam over to Tim and asked if he could play with the bubble too. Tim did not want to share the bubble and said no. Sam felt very sad and upset. He wanted the bubble so badly, but Tim would not let him have it.

Sam decided to take the bubble from Tim when he was not looking. He grabbed the bubble and tried to bow with it. But, the bubble popped and was gone forever. Sam still could not bow, and now he had made Tim very sad too. In the end, both Sam and Tim were miserable and the bubble was gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was flying fast in the sky when it started to rain. The bird looked for a shelter to hide from the rain. Suddenly, it saw a tree and flew towards it.

The bird appeared to be happy when it found the shelter under the tree. It saw a little worm and asked, "Can I stay here with you until the rain stops?" The worm replied, "Sure, you can stay here with me."

The rain continued to pour and the bird and the worm talked and played to pass the time. After a while, the rain stopped and the bird said, "Thank you for letting me stay with you. I have to go now." The worm replied, "You're welcome. Come back anytime."

As the bird flew away, a big cat appeared from behind the tree. The cat saw the worm and quickly ate it. The bird never knew what happened to its new friend.

Timmy's friend, Johnny, saw that Timmy was hurt and asked, "Are you okay?" Timmy replied, "No, my knee hurts." 

Johnny helped Timmy up and they continued to play the game. Timmy felt better knowing that his friend cared about him. 

From that day on, Timmy practiced running around the pole and soon became the best player on the block. He no longer felt embarrassed and was happy to have friends who cared about him.

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a wife. They lived in a little house. One day, the man went to work and his wife stayed at home. It was a gloomy day and the wife felt sad. She decided to wash the dishes to make herself feel better. 

But as she was washing the dishes, she accidentally broke a plate. She felt even sadder now. She tried to clean up the mess, but she cut her hand on a piece of the broken plate. It hurt a lot and she started to cry. 

When her husband came back from work, he saw the mess and his wife's injured hand. He got angry and started to shout at her. The wife felt even worse and cried even harder. The husband didn't help her and instead went to bed, leaving his wife alone and hurt. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy bird named Bob. Bob loved to sleep all day long and never wanted to do anything. One day, Bob's friend, a butterfly named Lily, came to visit him. 

"Hey Bob, let's fly to the garden and see the pretty flowers," said Lily. 

"But I'm too lazy to fly," replied Bob. 

"Come on, it will be fun," said Lily. 

Bob thought about it for a moment and finally agreed. They flew to the garden and saw many beautiful flowers. They even saw a light shining in the sky. 

"What's that?" asked Bob. 

"That's the sun," said Lily. 

Bob was amazed and happy that he decided to fly with his friend. From that day on, Bob was never too lazy to fly again.

Lila and Ben are scared. They run back to the bench.

"Why is he so mean?" Lila asks. "We just wanted to be nice!"

"Maybe he is lonely," Ben says. "Or maybe he is afraid of us. We are different from him."

They think for a while. Then they have an idea.

"Let's make him a gift!" Lila says. "Maybe he will like us then!"

They look around and find some flowers and leaves. They make a beautiful garland and tie it to a stick.

"Look, hippo!" Ben says. "We made this for you! It is pretty and colorful!"

They wave the stick near the pond. The hippo sees the garland and stops roaring. He is curious.

"What is that?" the hippo asks. "Is it food?"

"No, it is not food," Lila says. "It is a gift. We want to be your friends!"

The hippo is surprised. He swims closer and sniffs the garland. He likes the smell.

"Thank you," the hippo says. "That is very kind of you. I am sorry I was mean. I am not used to having visitors."

"That's okay," Lila says. "We are sorry we scared you. We are not used to seeing a hippo."

They smile at each other. They start to talk and learn more about each other. They find out they have some things in common. They like to swim, eat, and nap.

They become friends. They play and have fun together. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge someone by their appearance. Be friendly and respectful. You might find a new friend.

He jumped on the table. He knocked over the vase. The water spilled. The roses fell. The vase broke. Lily was very sad. She cried.

"Max, no! Bad cat! You ruined my picture and mom's vase!" she shouted.

Max came out and rubbed his head on Lily's leg. He purred. He said, "Meow."

Lily petted him and said, "It's okay, Max. I still love you. But next time, don't touch the vase and the roses. They are not toys. They are for mom."

Max nodded and said, "Meow."

They all hugged and laughed. They were a happy family. The end.

The dog says, "Woof! Woof!" He means, "OK! OK!"

The dog says, "Woof! Woof!" He means, "Yay! Yay!"

Sam and Ben screamed and jumped out of the car. They ran to the door and tried to open it. But it was locked. It was too tight.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "There are wild animals in the box! They are trying to destroy us!"

Their dad heard them and came to the garage. He saw the snake, the spider and the mouse. He was not scared. He knew they were harmless. He opened the door and let them out. He picked up the snake and the spider and put them back in the box. He gave the mouse some cheese and let it go.

"Boys, boys, what have you done?" he asked. "You made a big mess. You took out things that you should not have. You scared yourselves and the animals. You need to learn to be careful and respectful."

He made them clean up the garage and put everything back in the box. He also checked them for bites and scratches. He was not angry, but he was disappointed. He hugged them and told them he loved them. He also told them to never play with the box again.

Sam and Ben said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with their own toys instead. They did not want to see any more wild animals. They did not want to destroy anything. They wanted to be good.

"Look, I made a big mud pie!" Lily said. She put the mud pie on a flat stone and pretended it was a cake. "Do you want some, Max?"

Max nodded. He knelt next to Lily and took a piece of the mud pie with his hand. He pretended to eat it and made a funny face. "Mmm, yummy!" he said.

But then, a big dog came running into the garden. It was brown and furry and had a long tail. It saw the mud pie and thought it was real. It barked and jumped on the stone. It knocked over the bucket and the shovel. It ate the mud pie and made a mess.

"Hey, stop it!" Lily shouted. She was angry and scared. She tried to shoo the dog away, but it was too big and strong. It licked her face and made her dirty.

"Help, help!" Max cried. He was also angry and scared. He hid behind Lily and hugged her leg.

The dog's owner heard the noise and came to the garden. He saw the dog and the children and the mud. He was sorry and embarrassed. He called the dog and put a leash on it. He apologized to Lily and Max and their mom, who came out of the house.

"I'm so sorry, my dog is very friendly but he doesn't know how to behave. He thought the mud pie was real. Are you OK?" he said.

Lily and Max nodded. They were still dirty and wet, but they were not hurt. They were glad the dog was gone.

"It's OK, we're OK. But your dog ruined our mud pie. We worked hard on it. It was our cake," Lily said.

The dog's owner felt bad. He wanted to make it up to them. He had an idea.

"I'm sorry, I know you worked hard on it. How about I buy you a real cake? There's a bakery nearby. They have chocolate cake and vanilla cake and strawberry cake. Which one do you like?" he said.

Lily and Max smiled. They liked cake. They forgot about the mud pie and the dog. They looked at each other and said at the same time:

"Chocolate cake!"

The dog's owner laughed. He took them to the bakery and bought them a big chocolate cake. They ate it in the sunshine and shared it with their mom. They were happy and full. They thanked the dog's owner and said goodbye.
